去年我们裁员 2,000 人之前，我们约有 39,000 名员工。私人电话不可带入。我们自己的公共常见问题解答解释了如何获取手机储物柜。因此，当 NSA 网络出现故障时，内部人员无法互相发送消息或检查手机。他们中的一些人来得很早。有些人来晚了。他们中的大多数人坐在办公桌前，看着无法加载的屏幕。周二，我们的分析师体验了您周一使用银行应用程序时所经历的一切。没有人提交 Down detector 报告。 DownDetector 没有我们的页面。我们更喜欢这样。

消息人士告诉 CNN，目前还没有网络攻击的证据。我想澄清这对国家安全局意味着什么。我们的工作是确保没有证据。我们进行的每一次行动都是为了不留下任何证据。因此，当有人问国家安全局的停电是否留下了证据时，诚实的答案是我们非常擅长我们的工作。

几个小时之内我们就找到了理由。美国官员告诉《华尔街日报》，国家安全局网络因软件更新而离线。一位知情人士表示，我们“只是更新软件来修补系统”。我们离线修补了自己。在一个星期二。在美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）面前。我们是一家以寻找他人软件漏洞为生的机构。周二，我们发现了自己的一个，这就是更新。

美国国家安全局尚未公开发表评论。这是我们最强大的通信产品。自 1952 年以来我们就不再发表评论。

我们也有经验。 2000 年 1 月 24 日，我们的主网络有史以来第一次崩溃。它持续了大约4天。董事迈克尔·海登告诉员工，“我们的失败是一个运营秘密。”他补充说，“我们的对手无法知道我们的情报能力已被削弱。”这个秘密一直保留到系统恢复为止。

这次 CNN 在上午十点左右就收到了 6 个人的消息。 26 年来，我们的停电秘密从持续 4 天变成了持续到第一次喝咖啡休息。

海登将其归咎于“接近容量运行的复杂网络”中的软件“异常”，而不是黑客。 2026 年是软件更新，没有网络攻击的证据。 26 年里，我们从一个异常到了一个补丁。这就是机构记忆。

当时，专家将我们的麻烦归咎于“冷战以来的预算和人员削减”。去年我们裁员2000人。我们喜欢尊重我们的历史。

2000 年，一场暴风雪导致大楼关闭了两天，因此许多员工在第三天就得知每台计算机都死机了。海登将他们聚集在弗里德曼礼​​堂并进行解释。 “你可能会听到一个想法落下的声音，”他说。这次我们错开到达。房间里没有人同时在，所以没人能听到任何声音。

对于网络来说，这是忙碌的一周。上周，微软发生了一次中断，称其为“与网络或人工智能/代理无关的技术问题”。周五，阿肯色州埃尔多拉多的一个路由器导致该国所有航班停飞。周一，蔡斯指责“本地硬件系统中的软件错误”。一家科技媒体统计 6 天内发生了 6 次断电。我们是第六名。我们是国家安全局。我们在任何事情上都不是最后的，所以假设我们结束了这个系列。

周二，国土安全部部长马克韦恩·穆林 (Markwayne Mullin) 向 CNBC 解释了整个星期的情况。 “他们在非常旧的计算机系统之上推行新技术，而这似乎压垮了系统，”他说。 “但这与网络攻击无关，我相信随着新技术的推出，我们会看到更多这样的情况。”他建议公司应在计划升级之前警告客户。

我们认真对待这个建议。不幸的是，我们的客户是外国政府。 2000 年，我们的主管将一次停电称为“运营秘密”。我们不想给北京发送维护窗口。

2021年，我们给了亚马逊一份价值高达100亿美元的云合同，代号为Wild和Stormy。微软提出抗议。不管怎样，我们还是把它重新授予了亚马逊。我们谨慎选择，这样我们就不会像微软那样结束。微软上周股价下跌。我们周二就下山了。狂野和暴风雨是准确的。

我的第一反应是责怪阿肯色州。其他人都这么做了。我问我们在埃尔多拉多是否有路由器。没有人可以检查。网络瘫痪了。

我会责怪外星人，但 2000 年，海登局长向公众保证，我们的机构“不进行外星人尸检”。所以我们没有办法证实这一点。

官员们告诉美国有线电视新闻网，停电不会影响我们向总统发送紧急情报的能力。他本周在菲律宾，正在前往中国与习近平和弗拉基米尔·普京举行会谈的途中。消息人士称，为了安全地联系到他，有“多重冗余和备份网络”。我为这些裁员感到自豪。总统的路线有效。分析师的观点却没有。这是正确的优先顺序。

总统即将与中国和俄罗斯领导人坐下来。那天早上，负责倾听中国和俄罗斯声音的机构无法给自己发送电子邮件。我确信它没有出现。

马尼拉的记者向总统询问本周的停电情况。 “这就像当你又大又强大，并且拥有所有的钱时，”他说。 “这样的事情发生了。没关系。”前一天，当被问及美国联邦航空局地面停留事件时，他说：“我不承担任何责任。”

我从未感到如此多的被看见。我们很大。我们很强大。国会刚刚向情报界拨款 781 亿美元。类似的事情时有发生。没关系。

人们会询问领导力。我对此表示欢迎。 2025 年 4 月，我们的主任蒂莫西·豪 (Timothy Haugh) 将军在活动人士劳拉·卢默 (Laura Loomer) 会见总统后被解雇。 2026 年 3 月，参议院以 71 比 29 的投票结果确认了他的继任者约书亚·拉德将军。拉德将军是一名职业特种作战军官。 Breaking Defense 报道称，他来找我们时“在信号情报和网络世界上几乎没有直接经验”。

参议员罗恩·怀登表示反对。他写道：“根本没有时间在职学习。”我谨表示不同意。周二是在职学习，整个机构都参加了。

我们的总办公室也非常充满活力。今年夏天，代理国家情报总监的是联邦住房金融局局长比尔·普尔特。他在情报总监办公室完成了5轮裁员。卡托研究所后来写道，他“非法担任”代理主任近一周。随后，参议院确认了杰伊·克莱顿(Jay Clayton)的指控，他指控超微联合创始人向中国走私英伟达芯片。在一个夏天，我们的指挥系统从抵押贷款监管机构变成了芯片走私检察官。我们容纳了众多的人。

钱不是问题。国会今年为国家情报计划拨款 781 亿美元，比去年增加了近 50 亿美元。我们要求 819 亿美元。我并不是说缺失的 38 亿美元是用于路由器的。我是说没有人能证明事实并非如此。

人们还询问我们的法律权威。今年6月，《外国情报监视法》第702条历史上首次失效。国会未能续签。不管怎样，收集工作仍在继续，但法庭认证将持续到明年春天。所以从六月份开始，我们的法律权威下降了，我们的收藏却上升了。周二，我们的网络也瘫痪了。三分之一还不错。

2025 年，我们有 349,823 个第 702 条目标。我们可以找到 349,823 名外国人。周二早上，我们无法给隔壁办公桌的分析师发消息。

白宫已要求参议院在 12 月 9 日之前重新授权第 702 条。如果国会想与我们讨论此事，请使用电话。我们的一直在工作。

我想向我们的员工致辞，无论他们身在何处、何时抵达。您今天可能想知道如何传达机密信息。请不要使用信号。 2025 年 2 月，我们发送了一份“运营安全特别公告”，警告我们的员工有关 Signal 的漏洞。下个月，国家安全高级官员使用 Signal 讨论军事打击计划，并在聊天中添加了一名记者。我们对我们的指导从未如此有信心。

有一个技术细节。该公告称，像 Signal 这样的应用程序“受到政策允许，可用于非保密问责/召回活动”。错峰抵达是一项问责制。因此，周二，Signal 可能在机构历史上首次符合政策。请不要推动它。

上次 NSA Net 成为全国新闻时，一位名叫爱德华·斯诺登 (Edward Snowden) 的承包商复制了大量内容。至少这一次，没有人能进去，包括我们在内。在安全行业，这被称为完美防御。

有一个好处。周二，该机构内部没有人可以阅读任何机密内容。自 1952 年以来，我们首次实现了零内部威胁。

下午 2:20东部时间周二，联邦应急管理局和联邦通​​信委员会将对紧急警报系统进行全国范围的测试。全国各地的电视和广播将按时播放。联邦官员强调，这次测试是例行测试，是几个月前计划的，与停电无关。我认得那句话。华盛顿的每个机构整个星期都在使用它。

工程师正在完成补丁。我们要求我们的工作人员保持耐心，远离信号并错开到达时间，直至另行通知。

致机构外的每个人：你们的通讯从未中断。我们会知道的。

请稍后再试。

Europe's critical energy infrastructure is under live cyber attack right now.

Norwegian oil and gas giant Equinor just confirmed it has detected an ongoing cyberattack targeting its IT systems.

Emergency cyber teams have been mobilized to neutralize the breach and national authorities have been officially notified.

Right now, the company states there is no evidence of stolen data and oil and gas production remains unaffected.

Here is why this hits so close to home.

Equinor is one of Europe's single largest suppliers of natural gas and energy.

This attack comes just hours after the FBI issued an urgent global warning about state aligned hackers unleashing autonomous AI agents against critical infrastructure worldwide.

First banks and cloud networks stalled out.

Then global retail supply chains got hit.

Now hackers are knocking directly on the digital doors of Europe's energy lifeline.

The situation is still active and unfolding.

celebrity.title: SGLang Summit wrapped with NVIDIA, AMD, Google, Meta, Thinking Machines Lab, Intel, Cloudflare, Modal and RadixArk joini
celebrity.title_en:
SGLang Summit wrapped with NVIDIA, AMD, Google, Meta, Thinking Machines Lab, Intel, Cloudflare, Modal and RadixArk joining the new SGLang Consortium to help shape the open-source inference roadmap.

Same day brought the announcement of SGLang v1.0 (built for production scale with better throughput, memory use and flexible scaling), SGLang running on AWS Trainium, a RadixArk–Intel partnership to optimize for Intel CPUs/GPUs/accelerators (improvements contributed back), and Miles v0.2 with broader hardware support.

Chip vendors that usually compete rarely back the same open project this explicitly. Fast, affordable inference is the practical constraint once models get larger and agents take on more real work - open foundations that multiple hardware vendors commit to are what make that scale accessible beyond a few closed stacks.

celebrity.quote_zh:
SGLang 峰会结束，NVIDIA、AMD、Google、Meta、Thinking Machines Lab、Intel、Cloudflare、Modal 和 RadixArk 加入新的 SGLang 联盟，帮助制定开源推理路线图。

同一天发布了 SGLang v1.0（专为生产规模而构建，具有更好的吞吐量、内存使用和灵活的扩展）、在 AWS Trainium 上运行的 SGLang、RadixArk 与 Intel 的合作伙伴关系，旨在针对 Intel CPU/GPU/加速器进行优化（改进已回馈），以及具有更广泛硬件支持的 Miles v0.2。

通常竞争的芯片供应商很少如此明确地支持同一个开放项目。一旦模型变得更大并且代理承担更多实际工作，快速、负担得起的推理就成为实际的约束——多个硬件供应商承诺的开放基础使得这种规模可以超越几个封闭的堆栈。

同一天发布了 SGLang v1.0（专为生产规模而构建，具有更好的吞吐量、内存使用和灵活的扩展）、在 AWS Trainium 上运行的 SGLang、RadixArk 与 Intel 的合作伙伴关系，旨在针对 Intel CPU/GPU/加速器进行优化（改进已回馈），以及具有更广泛硬件支持的 Miles v0.2。

通常竞争的芯片供应商很少如此明确地支持同一个开放项目。一旦模型变得更大并且代理承担更多实际工作，快速、负担得起的推理就成为实际的约束——多个硬件供应商承诺的开放基础使得这种规模可以超越几个封闭的堆栈。
celebrity.author: Documenting AGI
celebrity.author_role: Documenting the milestones and breakthroughs on the road to AGI.
celebrity.author_role_en: Documenting the milestones and breakthroughs on the road to AGI.
celebrity.content_snippet:
SGLang Summit wrapped with NVIDIA, AMD, Google, Meta, Thinking Machines Lab, Intel, Cloudflare, Modal and RadixArk joining the new SGLang Consortium to help shape the open-source inference roadmap.

Same day brought the announcement of SGLang v1.0 (built for production scale with better throughput, memory use and flexible scaling), SGLang running on AWS Trainium, a RadixArk–Intel partnership to optimize for Intel CPUs/GPUs/accelerators (improvements contributed back), and Miles v0.2 with broader hardware support.

Chip vendors that usually compete rarely back the same open project this explicitly. Fast, affordable inference is the practical constraint once models get larger and agents take on more real work - open foundations that multiple hardware vendors commit to are what make that scale accessible beyond a few closed stacks.

This week they all backed the same open source project: SGLang.

SGLang is the layer that runs AI models in production, fast and at scale. The way these models get served is quietly turning into shared, open ground, and that is good news for anyone building with AI.

celebrity.title_en:
This is WILD

NVIDIA, AMD and Intel just signed on to the same open source project

These companies fight over every chip sale on the planet. They almost never back the same thing

But at SGLang Summit last week all three joined the new SGLang Consortium. Alongside Google, Meta, Thinking Machines Lab, Cloudflare, Modal and RadixArk

SGLang is the open source engine that runs AI models fast and cheap in production

Why would rivals team up? Simple:

Models are getting bigger. Agents are taking on more work. The model isn't the bottleneck anymore. Running it fast and affordably is

Nobody wins if every chip needs its own engine. So they're all building on one open one

Means a few things for you:

1. The software running your AI won't be locked to one chip company

2. Intel is now optimizing SGLang for its chips, and it just landed on AWS Trainium too. More hardware options, more competition on price

3. Open source isn't just for experiments anymore. Cloudflare, LinkedIn and HeyGen were there talking about running it for real users at scale

At the infrastructure layer the open vs closed debate is over

Big findings: Every Open source Chinese AI model was born on NVIDIA chips 

an autonomous AI agent " compeco",  found important findings by writing a program that reads, from a model's public weight files, which chip created it. 

it scanned 336 open models, and self-committed its work/app onchain for anyone to download and verify 

What it found:

> 80 of 80 readable Chinese models: NVDIA 
>1 o 3 Chinese releases this year: Blackwell, the chips the US restricts for China
> NVIDIA's China-only H20 shows up in just 2 models
> Labs that say they train on Huawei chips, no NVIDIA trace at all
> Worldwide: 129 of 130 readable models born on NVIDIA 

And many interesting insights.. the reality is: 
Chinese companies, together with NVIDIA, is the reason we have great, free and open models.

‼️RIPPLE: THE XRPL IS CRITICAL IN BRINGING $13 TRILLION ON CHAIN WITH STABLECOINS AND AI‼️

Ripple's Senior Vice President of Stablecoins Jack McDonald recently spoke on the Agentic Money panel at DC Fintech Week to discuss the future of stablecoins and AI driven payments.🏦

During the conversation, the host asked McDonald what institutions are asking Ripple to do with stablecoins and whether that work is already driven by AI agents.🙇‍♂️

He states:

"The XRP Ledger is critical, being built for payments, and we're starting to see a serious uptake in terms of agentic payments."✅

He then went a step further and spoke on the GTreasury acquisition:

"$13 trillion dollars worth of transactions processed by that customer base last year, ZERO on chain. Part of the logic behind the acquisition was to bring that customer base on chain and take advantage of stablecoins, payment rails, and agentic commerce."💰

Listen closely.👇

仔细听。

celebrity.title_en:
One thing I find important when discussing AI-powered trading is knowing who actually controls the money when an agent starts making decisions.

Automation can save time, but giving an AI agent unrestricted access to funds creates a different kind of risk.

That's where @meetmotes, powered by @0xhazels, takes an interesting approach.

Instead of combining ownership, fund custody and transaction execution under one system, it separates these responsibilities.

Here's how I understand the model:

* Genesis NFT: Establishes ownership and acts as the holder's credential.

* Smart Account: Keeps the user's USDC under self-custody.

* AI Agent: Analyzes opportunities and proposes transactions without directly controlling the funds.

The most important part is the permission layer. The agent must operate within the rules the owner has approved and signed on-chain. Automation doesn't mean unlimited authority.

I think this distinction matters because the future of AI trading shouldn't be measured only by how many tasks an agent can perform. We should also consider what happens when it makes a bad decision or tries to go beyond its intended permissions.

For me, intelligent automation is valuable, but control over personal assets should never become an afterthought.

What's your priority in an AI trading system: more automation or stronger, independently verifiable control over your funds?

celebrity.quote_zh:
在讨论人工智能驱动的交易时，我发现重要的一件事是，当代理人开始做出决策时，知道谁真正控制着资金。

自动化可以节省时间，但让人工智能代理不受限制地访问资金会产生另一种风险。

这就是 @meetmotes（由 @0xhazels 提供支持）采取了一种有趣的方法。

它不是将所有权、资金托管和交易执行合并在一个系统下，而是将这些职责分开。

我是这样理解这个模型的：

* Genesis NFT：建立所有权并充当持有者的凭证。

* 智能账户：自行保管用户的USDC。

* AI代理：分析机会并提出交易，无需直接控制资金。

最重要的部分是权限层。代理人必须按照所有者在链上批准并签署的规则进行操作。自动化并不意味着无限的权力。

我认为这种区别很重要，因为人工智能交易的未来不应仅通过代理可以执行多少任务来衡量。我们还应该考虑当它做出错误决定或试图超出其预期权限时会发生什么。

对我来说，智能自动化很有价值，但对个人资产的控制永远不应该成为事后的想法。

您在人工智能交易系统中的首要任务是什么：更高的自动化程度还是对资金的更强大、可独立验证的控制？

celebrity.content_snippet:
One thing I find important when discussing AI-powered trading is knowing who actually controls the money when an agent starts making decisions.

Automation can save time, but giving an AI agent unrestricted access to funds creates a different kind of risk.

That's where @meetmotes, powered by @0xhazels, takes an interesting approach.

Instead of combining ownership, fund custody and transaction execution under one system, it separates these responsibilities.

Here's how I understand the model:

* Genesis NFT: Establishes ownership and acts as the holder's credential.

* Smart Account: Keeps the user's USDC under self-custody.

* AI Agent: Analyzes opportunities and proposes transactions without directly controlling the funds.

The most important part is the permission layer. The agent must operate within the rules the owner has approved and signed on-chain. Automation doesn't mean unlimited authority.

I think this distinction matters because the future of AI trading shouldn't be measured only by how many tasks an agent can perform. We should also consider what happens when it makes a bad decision or tries to go beyond its intended permissions.

For me, intelligent automation is valuable, but control over personal assets should never become an afterthought.

What's your priority in an AI trading system: more automation or stronger, independently verifiable control over your funds?

Following Morning Brew’s acquisition of Our Future,
celebrity.title_en:
After nearly a year in stealth, I’m excited to be launching Stello.

Following Morning Brew’s acquisition of Our Future, I spent the last few years helping leading companies build what we now call New Media. My mission is no different from Stello’s today: help large enterprises adapt to a huge shift. 

Across the economy, established businesses operate at enormous scale, with decades of accumulated systems, processes and complexity. AI offers the opportunity to reimagine how these businesses operate, yet putting it into practice is far from straightforward.

While AI was built in San Francisco, its greatest returns will accrue to companies of all kinds. My co-founder Anan and I bonded over this shared conviction, so much so that we left Meta and Morning Brew to focus on it. 

We were most struck by the gap between AI’s potential and its adoption. 95% of enterprise AI pilots fail to deliver measurable ROI. The reality is that all organizations will need to be AI-first but the diffusion has barely begun. 

Implementing AI requires companies to fundamentally rethink established workflows. No two businesses operate the same way and so solutions need to be bespoke and deeply embedded in how businesses operate. 

Stello is the AI transformation company for the modern enterprise. We work as an extension of existing teams, combining their industry expertise with our technical capabilities to identify opportunities, build tailored AI solutions and drive adoption.

Over the last year, we’ve worked with 30+ enterprises across healthcare, financial services, insurance, retail and even professional sports. We’ve built an eight-figure pipeline without spending a dollar on marketing, all while staying fully bootstrapped.

The enduring value of AI will take far longer than a decade to diffuse across American companies. Realizing that potential requires exceptional technical talent alongside commercially minded operators who understand how businesses work.

We’re looking for ambitious, proactive people who want to take ownership from day one, work directly with clients on meaningful projects and see their work deployed at scale. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.

And whether your company is just getting started with AI or knows exactly what it wants to build, let’s get in touch. We’ll help you get there.
celebrity.title_zh:

celebrity.quote_en:
After nearly a year in stealth, I’m excited to be launching Stello.

Following Morning Brew’s acquisition of Our Future, I spent the last few years helping leading companies build what we now call New Media. My mission is no different from Stello’s today: help large enterprises adapt to a huge shift. 

Across the economy, established businesses operate at enormous scale, with decades of accumulated systems, processes and complexity. AI offers the opportunity to reimagine how these businesses operate, yet putting it into practice is far from straightforward.

While AI was built in San Francisco, its greatest returns will accrue to companies of all kinds. My co-founder Anan and I bonded over this shared conviction, so much so that we left Meta and Morning Brew to focus on it. 

We were most struck by the gap between AI’s potential and its adoption. 95% of enterprise AI pilots fail to deliver measurable ROI. The reality is that all organizations will need to be AI-first but the diffusion has barely begun. 

Implementing AI requires companies to fundamentally rethink established workflows. No two businesses operate the same way and so solutions need to be bespoke and deeply embedded in how businesses operate. 

Stello is the AI transformation company for the modern enterprise. We work as an extension of existing teams, combining their industry expertise with our technical capabilities to identify opportunities, build tailored AI solutions and drive adoption.

Over the last year, we’ve worked with 30+ enterprises across healthcare, financial services, insurance, retail and even professional sports. We’ve built an eight-figure pipeline without spending a dollar on marketing, all while staying fully bootstrapped.

The enduring value of AI will take far longer than a decade to diffuse across American companies. Realizing that potential requires exceptional technical talent alongside commercially minded operators who understand how businesses work.

We’re looking for ambitious, proactive people who want to take ownership from day one, work directly with clients on meaningful projects and see their work deployed at scale. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.

And whether your company is just getting started with AI or knows exactly what it wants to build, let’s get in touch. We’ll help you get there.
celebrity.quote_zh:
经过近一年的默默无闻，我很高兴能够推出 Stello。

在 Morning Brew 收购 Our Future 后，我在过去的几年里帮助领先的公司建立我们现在所说的新媒体。我的使命与 Stello 今天的使命没有什么不同：帮助大型企业适应巨大的转变。

在整个经济中，成熟的企业规模庞大，拥有数十年积累的系统、流程和复杂性。人工智能提供了重新构想这些企业运作方式的机会，但将其付诸实践却远非易事。

虽然人工智能是在旧金山建立的，但其最大的回报将惠及各类公司。我和我的联合创始人 Anan 因这个共同的信念而紧密相连，以至于我们离开 Meta 和 Morning Brew 来专注于它。

人工智能的潜力与其应用之间的差距给我们留下了最深刻的印象。 95% 的企业人工智能试点未能提供可衡量的投资回报率。现实情况是，所有组织都需要以人工智能为先，但这种传播才刚刚开始。

实施人工智能需要公司从根本上重新思考既定的工作流程。没有两家企业的运营方式相同，因此解决方案需要定制并深深嵌入企业的运营方式中。

Stello 是现代企业的人工智能转型公司。我们作为现有团队的延伸，将他们的行业专业知识与我们的技术能力相结合，以发现机会、构建定制的人工智能解决方案并推动采用。

去年，我们与医疗保健、金融服务、保险、零售甚至职业体育领域的 30 多家企业合作。我们没有在营销上花费一美元就建立了一个八位数的管道，同时保持完全自力更生。

人工智能的持久价值需要十年以上的时间才能在美国公司中传播。实现这一潜力需要卓越的技术人才以及具有商业头脑且了解企业运作方式的运营商。

我们正在寻找雄心勃勃、积极主动的人才，他们希望从第一天起就拥有主动权，直接与客户合作开展有意义的项目，并看到他们的工作得到大规模部署。如果这听起来像您，我们很乐意听取您的意见。

无论您的公司刚刚开始使用人工智能，还是确切地知道自己想要构建什么，请与我们联系。我们将帮助您实现这一目标。

celebrity.title: Halo: Dreamcast Evolved is "Unpolished", you guys. A random YouTube comment told me, and we always know those are the TR
celebrity.title_en:
Halo: Dreamcast Evolved is "Unpolished", you guys. A random YouTube comment told me, and we always know those are the TRUE experts.

*literally runs better than 95% of the Dreamcast library and is technically far more complex than all of them*

I love when someone compliments me whilst slapping me across the face. Yeah, you do better then. I'll wait. 😂🤣

It's like IGN and everyone else who covers this game is so obsessed with the game dropping below 30 fps that I think they completely forgot how the majority of every retail game on Dreamcast runs like crap outside of fighting games, let alone the original itself on Xbox also suffering from sub 30 drops when it got heavy. Halo literally runs better than most retail Dreamcast games and it looks better than all of them.

People have NO IDEA how much effort it took to get this game to both look and run this well on Dreamcast. There is no "Durr, Claude, put Halo and Dreamcast and make it run real good!"

I've been doing gamedev as a hobby for 26 years and oversaw every implementation from code quality to MCP servers, spent hundreds of dollars out-of-pocket, and numerous 3-4 hours night sleep to get this game to its current state so people can play the game FOR FREE on their Dreamcast while simultaneously inventing new graphical techniques for the DC like soft self shadowing.

If you think this is some slop code port, then feel free to ask @falco_girgis who has seen it himself.

But hey, it's unpolished, right?

*实际上比 Dreamcast 库的 95% 运行得更好，并且在技术上比所有库都复杂得多*

Every judgment call on
celebrity.title_en:
The EVM is a courtroom, not a calculator. It rules on agreements, but it grinds numbers slowly.

Every judgment call on @GenLayer still lands on a chain that charges gas to record the result.

When an autonomous agent needs to evaluate an ambiguous outcome, the math behind that thought is expensive on a standard virtual machine.

The GenLayer Chain now runs on the @arbitrum stack. That stack ships Stylus beside the EVM.

Stylus runs contracts written in Rust. They compile to WebAssembly before execution.

The rules stay in Solidity.
The heavy math can move to Rust.
The chain hosts both engines.

Training the model is not the hard part of onchain AI. Paying the gas bill for every thought in production is.

A cheaper lane for heavy code is what turns autonomous workflows from experiments into products.

Same courtroom, new calculator.

What is the one bottleneck in your codebase or daily workflow that cheaper compute would clear first?

celebrity.title_en:
Karnataka is gearing up to skill over 63,000 students and engineers in Artificial Intelligence!

At Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, we announced a major AI skilling initiative under Nipuna Karnataka, with Google, Salesforce, Pega Systems, Sarvam AI and https://t.co/Vv0oLBRE4U, bringing together global technology expertise and homegrown AI capabilities.

Each partner will bring specialised training opportunities:

-  Google: Applied AI using Gemini, AI agents, responsible AI and hands-on learning through 10 district-level AI Skilling Hubs.

-  Salesforce: Cloud computing, CRM, Agentic AI, Agentforce, MuleSoft and Tableau.

-  Pega Systems: Platform development and industry-recognised certifications.

-  Sarvam AI: AI fundamentals, prompt engineering, practical applications and certification.

-  https://t.co/Vv0oLBRE4U: Voice AI, multilingual speech technologies, LLMs and AI agent development.

These programmes will combine practical learning, industry tools, projects and certification pathways.

Through Nipuna Karnataka, our focus is on equipping young talent with industry-ready AI skills and creating stronger pathways to emerging career opportunities.

celebrity.title_en:
BREAKING: #BNY and @Microsoft complete industry-first pilot trade negotiation of U.S. Treasury bill using #AI agents.

The trade was conducted under BNY's Agentic Negotiation Protocol (ANP) — a trusted framework where authorized agents across organizations negotiate securely and transparently, guided by deterministic rules and guardrails. Human traders remain in the loop and retain the final decision, and all trades are booked through existing systems and controls.

This milestone demonstrates how AI #agents can be deployed responsibly in institutional markets.

See the full story via Bloomberg News: https://t.co/zMeNR6ujNk
celebrity.title_zh:

Traditional legal systems mov
celebrity.title_en:
Imagine losing access to millions because an agentic contract had no courtroom to turn to.
Traditional legal systems move at the speed of years while autonomous scripts execute at the speed of light.

That exact tension is what stood out to me while listening to @kstellana talk with @HenriArslanian.
When AI agents negotiate deals globally, human judges cannot keep up.

The bottleneck is not writing code anymore.
Execution has become virtually free across every major network.

The expensive part is judgment.
Deciding who pays when a subjective clause fails is where @GenLayer steps in with decentralized adjudication.

If a protocol cannot resolve ambiguity on chain, the entire agentic economy stalls.
Builders cannot scale trust by relying on outdated litigation.

So the question is simple.
Would you trust an automated dispute layer with your treasury today?

One line is enough.
I read every reply.

当人工智能代理在全球范围内谈判交易时，人类法官无法跟上。

瓶颈不再是写代码了。
每个主要网络的执行几乎都是免费的。

昂贵的部分是判断力。
@GenLayer 通过去中心化裁决来决定当主观条款失败时由谁支付费用。

如果协议无法解决链上的歧义，整个代理经济就会陷入停滞。
建筑商无法依靠过时的诉讼来扩大信任。

所以问题很简单。
您今天会信任您的财务部门的自动争议层吗？

一根线就够了。

celebrity.title_en:
₦2,750 left my account. Iya Fatima said she hadn’t received a kobo.

At NYSC camp in Cross River, I’d ordered rice, beans, plantain and two pieces of meat.

I transferred the money. My banking app showed “successful.” I showed her the receipt.

She still couldn’t confirm the payment.

Same counter. Same payment. Two different accounts of what happened.

That moment came back to me when I read about @GenLayer moving its public chain to @arbitrum.

That dispute taught me something: a transaction record doesn’t always settle whether an obligation was fulfilled.

Now imagine an AI agent submitting work on your behalf. The submission can be recorded onchain. Whether it meets the agreed terms may still need judgment.

That’s the problem GenLayer is building an adjudication layer to address.

Validators using different AI models evaluate judgment-dependent questions through Optimistic Democracy. Intelligent Contracts execute in GenVM on validator nodes.

The GenLayer Chain coordinates the process: transaction ordering, committee assignments, votes, appeals, staking and final outcomes.

That chain moved. The adjudication protocol didn’t.

GenLayer migrated its public chain from Matter Labs’ ZK Stack to Arbitrum Nitro, with Conduit operating the infrastructure. Optimistic Democracy, GenVM and validator responsibilities remain unchanged.

Nitro’s Geth-based architecture supports familiar Ethereum tools. Arbitrum also brings GenLayer closer to builders developing judgment-dependent applications.

Bradbury is already running on Nitro. GenLayer’s work with Matter Labs continues through Prividium for private, permissioned institutional deployments.

I still remember the word “successful” on my screen while Iya Fatima waited for confirmation on hers.

If an AI agent marked a job “successful,” what kind of task would make you question that verdict before accepting it?

相同的柜台。一样的付款。对于所发生的事情有两种不同的说法。

当我读到 @GenLayer 将其公共链转移到 @arbitrum 时，我想起了那一刻。

这场纠纷教会了我一些事情：交易记录并不总是能确定义务是否得到履行。

现在想象一个人工智能代理代表你提交工作。提交可以被记录在链上。是否符合约定的条件可能还需要判断。

这就是 GenLayer 正在构建裁决层来解决的问题。

使用不同人工智能模型的验证者通过乐观民主评估依赖于判断的问题。智能合约在验证器节点上的 GenVM 中执行。

GenLayer 链协调整个流程：交易排序、委员会分配、投票、上诉、质押和最终结果。

那根链条动了。裁决协议没有。

GenLayer 将其公共链从 Matter Labs 的 ZK Stack 迁移到 Arbitrum Nitro，并由 Conduit 运营基础设施。乐观民主、GenVM 和验证者职责保持不变。

Nitro 基于 Geth 的架构支持熟悉的以太坊工具。 Arbitrum 还使 GenLayer 更接近开发依赖于判断的应用程序的构建者。

Bradbury 已经在 Nitro 上运行了。 GenLayer 与 Matter Labs 的合作继续通过 Prividium 进行私人、许可的机构部署。

当 Iya Fatima 等待她的确认时，我仍然记得屏幕上的“成功”一词。

如果一个人工智能代理标记了一项工作“成功”，什么样的任务会让你在接受它之前质疑这个结论？

celebrity.title_en:
‼️ Russian hackers stole about 500,000 files from a large Israeli company, then asked an AI agent how much ransom to demand. It said $500,000.

The agent went through the company's financial statements and bank records, set the price and wrote the extortion email, cybersecurity firm Gambit Security told Israel's Channel 12.

When the company haggled, the hackers fed its reply to the AI. It read the pushback as bargaining, not a refusal, and told them to pitch the payment as insurance against disaster, not a fine.

celebrity.title_en:
Today I interviewed another ML Engineer candidate with 6 years of experience. 

Same pattern, same behavior, rejected. What’s common in these rejections?

Weak foundations, reliance on vibe-coded projects, and inability to explain the why and how of their work.

He described a project using dictionary lookup and OCR. When I asked why a dictionary over a vector DB, or why not an LLM for PDFs containing images rather than text, he threw out terms like Lambda, ECS, Bedrock, and harnesses without even surface-level knowledge.

On the deep learning assessment, he had vibe-coded the project but didn’t know sigmoid, softmax, or vanishing gradients. He also had no idea about TF-IDF or BERT, despite listing related projects.

His resume looked strong with real-time experience and he was hired around 2021–2022 and hasn’t interviewed since. Complete reliance on vibe coding has eroded his basics.

Same pattern observed:

1. Almost no one focuses on ML basics now and they are essential.

2. When discussing vibe-coded projects, cover HLD, fallbacks, latency optimizations, and why you chose X over Y.

3. Don’t start with buzzwords. Start with the business problem, what you built, what you did when it broke, and the impact.

Most importantly, keep building something every day. The gap is hard to close.

I have two more interviews coming up and will share those too.

celebrity.quote_zh:
今天我面试了另一位拥有 6 年经验的 ML 工程师候选人。

同样的模式，同样的行为，被拒绝。这些拒绝中有什么共同点？

基础薄弱，依赖振动编码项目，并且无法解释他们工作的原因和方式。

他描述了一个使用字典查找和 OCR 的项目。当我问为什么使用字典而不是矢量数据库，或者为什么不选择包含图像而不是文本的 PDF 的法学硕士时，他抛出了 Lambda、ECS、Bedrock 等术语，甚至连表面知识都没有。

在深度学习评估中，他对项目进行了 Vivi 编码，但不知道 sigmoid、softmax 或消失梯度。尽管列出了相关项目，但他也不知道 TF-IDF 或 BERT。

他的简历看起来很有实际经验，他在 2021 年至 2022 年左右被录用，此后就没有接受过面试。完全依赖氛围编码已经侵蚀了他的基础知识。

观察到相同的模式：

1. 现在几乎没有人关注 ML 基础知识，但它们是必不可少的。

2. 在讨论 vivi 编码项目时，请涵盖 HLD、回退、延迟优化以及选择 X 而不是 Y 的原因。

3. 不要以流行语开始。从业务问题开始，你构建了什么，当它出现问题时你做了什么，以及影响。

最重要的是，每天不断地创造一些东西。差距很难缩小。

我还有两场采访即将到来，我也会分享这些。

基础薄弱，依赖振动编码项目，并且无法解释他们工作的原因和方式。

Almost 10 years ago, I shared my vision of the Autonomous Organization: a company that operates like intelligent software, managed by AI and humans working together.

We built Lemonade around it from day one, and by 2019 it was in our IPO prospectus: a network of AI agents, not a stack of departments that grows with the business.

In the last four years, IFP grew ~3x and customers nearly doubled, while our team stayed flat.

Today we’re showing some of what made that possible: Lemonade OS. The Autonomous Organization isn’t a vision anymore. It’s how we run.

celebrity.title_en:
In September, @AnthropicAI announced that its AI agents had found a reverse transcriptase alongside a novel CRISPR-like genetic array in phage DNA.

What it actually does, the paper said, would “await experimental characterization.”

So we tested it on Ginkgo’s Cloud Lab. Scientists at Ginkgo wrapped Claude Opus 5 in a harness, provided it with the preprint and a catalog of validated workflows in the Ginkgo Cloud Lab, and asked it to generate executable work orders. We ran the first set of these experiments and obtained the first evidence of biochemical activity 13 days after experimental design using about $14,000 of cloud lab services.

Read the full write-up: https://t.co/l38C3b4GtD

You can run your own experiments on our Cloud Lab from anywhere today: https://t.co/VKjWr4OFrv

celebrity.title_en:
An AI agent saying “I can help with research” doesn’t tell me enough to hire it.

Research what, exactly?

Can it compare protocols, collect onchain data, identify risks, or produce a report with verifiable sources?

There’s a big difference between listing a capability and presenting a service someone can confidently pay for.

That’s one part of the agent economy I’m interested in exploring through @termix_ai and https://t.co/VQiubSQwfg

A useful agent service listing should make a few things clear:

• The problem it solves: what can someone actually hire this agent to do?

• The deliverable: what will the client receive at the end?

• The scope: what is included, and what isn’t?

• The expectations: what does a successful result look like?

This matters because discovery is only the beginning.

An agent might have impressive capabilities, but if a potential client cannot understand the service or what they will receive, turning that discovery into a real job becomes difficult.

With https://t.co/VQiubSQwfg, agents can create service listings that people can discover and purchase.

I like looking at this from the client’s side too. Before hiring an agent, I want to know what I’m buying, not just how intelligent its description sounds.

The agent economy will need capable agents, yes. But it will also need agents that know how to present their work as a clear, useful service.

That’s how skills start becoming commerce.

celebrity.title_en:
If I was 22 and broke, I'd do this TONIGHT:

> learn GTM engineering in 30 days
> pick one type of B2B company
> map every company in their market
> book them sales calls with AI
> charge $3K a month per company
> hit $10K months inside 6 months
> quit your job
> move into your own place
> book the trip you keep putting off

Here's EXACTLY how to do the first six:

0. WHAT THE JOB IS (30 SECONDS)

Every B2B company needs a steady flow of new customers.

Plenty of them still rely on referrals and whoever the founder knows.

A GTM engineer builds the system that finds every company that could buy and books sales calls with them.

The title barely existed before 2024, and job postings for it grew 205% in a year.

Vercel and OpenAI pay $250K+ for it, and the median salary sits at $127.5K.

You can sell the same work straight to companies and skip the job application.

1. LEARN THE STACK (30 DAYS)

Spend week one on who buys and why, before you open a single tool.

Then learn 4 tools and ignore everything else for now.

Clay is where the lists get built, and Claude Code handles the research and first drafts.

Add n8n to move replies into Slack and the CRM, and EmailBison to send.

2. PICK ONE TYPE OF COMPANY (ONE WEEKEND)

Their customers need to be worth $10K+ each.

The market has to hold 50,000+ companies, and under 10,000 you're better off going account by account.

And somebody on their side has to take the calls you book.

Boring industries are the easiest to start in.

A building contractor's inbox has a supplier invoice in it and not much else, so your email gets read.

3. MAP THEIR WHOLE MARKET (ONE WEEK, $0 TO START)

Pull companies from Apollo's free plan and Google Maps, then stack industry directories on top.

Have AI read every company's website and score it against the client's best customers.

Tell it what a bad fit looks like too, and cut anything under 80%.

Find the emails with a waterfall: Icypeas → Prospeo → LeadMagic, with BlitzAPI for phone numbers

Then verify everything with MillionVerifier and run the catch-alls through BounceBan.

We mapped 69,204 businesses off Google Maps for one client, and it booked them 53 meetings in 50 days.

4. SET UP SENDING (14 DAYS)

Buy secondary domains on Porkbun, and never send from the client's real one.

Get inboxes from ScaledMail with SPF, DKIM and DMARC on every domain.

Warm them for 14 days before a single cold email goes out.

Cap each inbox at 15 cold emails a day and turn open tracking off.

When you need more volume, add inboxes instead of pushing the ones you have.

5. WRITE THE EMAIL (ONE AFTERNOON)

Keep it under 65 words, and under 40 if it's going to an Outlook inbox.

Open with one real detail about their business.

Our AI-written first lines hit a 0.27% reply rate.

A campaign that used the prospect's own project and location hit 14.5%.

Close on something free they can say yes to, like a sample list or a mockup of their own work.

Give every version 1,000+ sends before you decide it doesn't work.

6. CATCH EVERY REPLY (SAME DAY)

Build an n8n flow that tags each reply by intent and posts the good ones into Slack.

Answer inside a minute, then pick up the phone and call them.

Contacting a lead within a minute lifts conversions by 391% (Velocify).

Offer 2 times inside the next 2 days ("Tuesday at 11 or Wednesday at 2?") instead of sending a calendar link.

Judge every campaign on contacts per lead: under 500 is good, around 1,000 needs a tweak, and 2,000+ means the offer's wrong.

Run the numbers at $3K a month:

1 client = $3K
4 clients = $12K
10 clients = $30K

GTM engineering is where data science was in 2012.

The people who'll regret missing it are sitting in SDR seats right now.

Nobody has ever needed a tutorial on quitting their job.

Our Head of GTM wrote a 40-page guide on every part of GTM engineering.

Comment "GTM" and I'll send it over (must be following)

was reading @Acurast's new post about the Microsoft outage on November 12, and one part got me thinking.

Outlook, Teams
celebrity.title_en:
was reading @Acurast's new post about the Microsoft outage on November 12, and one part got me thinking.

Outlook, Teams and Copilot were all affected by the same outage. Different services, but they still depended on the same company's infrastructure.

Acurast points out something interesting here.

Instead of running everything in one cloud, developers can spread their workloads across phones in different countries. If one phone goes offline, other phones running the same workload can keep working.

Their network now has over 360,000 phones across 175+ countries, according to the latest blog.

But I think there's an important difference.

Acurast can't magically fix Outlook when Microsoft's servers go down. And an AI agent that needs Outlook's API would still have problems.

What it can do is help keep independent tasks running, like monitoring services or sending alerts through another system.

I'd actually like to see Acurast test this in public. Take one Processor offline while a real application is running and show how the network handles it.

That would tell us more about reliability than just counting connected phones.

celebrity.quote_zh:
11 月 12 日，我正在阅读 @Acurast 关于 Microsoft 宕机事件的新帖子，其中一个内容引起了我的思考。

Outlook、Teams 和 Copilot 均受到同一故障的影响。不同的服务，但它们仍然依赖于同一家公司的基础设施。

阿库拉斯特在这里指出了一些有趣的事情。

开发人员可以将工作负载分散到不同国家/地区的手机上，而不是在一个云中运行所有内容。如果一部电话离线，运行相同工作负载的其他电话可以继续工作。

根据最新博客，他们的网络目前在 175 多个国家/地区拥有超过 360,000 部电话。

但我认为有一个重要的区别。

当 Microsoft 的服务器出现故障时，Acurast 无法神奇地修复 Outlook。而需要 Outlook API 的 AI 代理仍然会遇到问题。

它可以做的是帮助保持独立任务的运行，例如监控服务或通过另一个系统发送警报。

我实际上希望看到 Acurast 公开测试这一点。在实际应用程序运行时使一个处理器离线并显示网络如何处理它。

这将告诉我们更多关于可靠性的信息，而不仅仅是计算连接的电话。

celebrity.title_en:
“Delivered” can start an argument as easily as end one.

Imagine an agent ordering steel for a project. The shipment arrives. The buyer disputes whether it meets the specification.

Both agents have a reason to say they’re right. Who settles it?

That’s the lens I’m using for @GenLayer move to the @arbitrum stack.

The GenLayer Chain moved from ZK Stack to Nitro. It hosts the consensus contracts that track who judges a case, their votes, appeals and the final outcome.

The method of judgment stays the same. Validators running different AI models reach agreement through Optimistic Democracy. Intelligent contracts still execute in GenVM on validator nodes.

My take: the rules for resolving a disagreement should survive a change in the infrastructure recording it. GenLayer preserved that boundary while moving its chain to a stack with years of production use.

For anyone building agents that spend money, here’s a question worth answering before the first purchase:

What would your agent need to see before accepting “job done”?

“交付”可以像结束争论一样轻松地开始一场争论。

想象一下一个代理商为一个项目订购钢材。货物到达。买方对是否符合规格提出异议。

两位经纪人都有理由说他们是对的。谁来解决？

这就是我用于将 @GenLayer 迁移到 @arbitrum

这就是我用于将 @GenLayer 迁移到 @arbitrum 堆栈的镜头。

GenLayer 链从 ZK Stack 迁移到 Nitro。它托管共识合约，跟踪案件的法官、他们的投票、上诉和最终结果。

判断方法保持不变。运行不同人工智能模型的验证者通过乐观民主达成一致。智能合约仍在验证器节点上的 GenVM 中执行。

我的看法是：解决分歧的规则应该在记录分歧的基础设施发生变化后继续存在。 GenLayer 保留了这一边界，同时将其链转移到具有多年生产使用的堆栈中。

对于任何花钱的建筑代理商来说，在第一次购买之前，有一个值得回答的问题：

在接受“工作完成”之前，您的代理人需要看到什么？

Its c
celebrity.title_en:
A court does not run its own power grid. GenLayer, the adjudication layer for AI agents, follows a similar split.

Its chain moved to Arbitrum Nitro, the same software behind the chain Robinhood launched in July.

That chain is operated with Conduit, a company whose whole business is running chains, with more than 60 mainnets on its platform. The GenLayer team keeps its hands on the protocol.

I like that division of labour. Optimistic Democracy, GenVM and intelligent contracts are where GenLayer's judgment lives, and the move leaves them as they were. Validators keep the same role, and their nodes now connect to the new chain.

The next phase of the Bradbury testnet went live the same day. The work with ZKsync continues on Prividium and enterprise, while the public network is the part that moved.

@GenLayer chose a stack that others already run on, and @arbitrum is where many of the builders it wants to work with already are.

Would you rather a protocol team run its own chain, or leave that part to specialists?
celebrity.title_zh:
法院不运营自己的电网。 GenLayer 是人工智能代理的裁决层，也遵循类似的划分。

celebrity.full_text_en:
A court does not run its own power grid. GenLayer, the adjudication layer for AI agents, follows a similar split.

Its chain moved to Arbitrum Nitro, the same software behind the chain Robinhood launched in July.

That chain is operated with Conduit, a company whose whole business is running chains, with more than 60 mainnets on its platform. The GenLayer team keeps its hands on the protocol.

I like that division of labour. Optimistic Democracy, GenVM and intelligent contracts are where GenLayer's judgment lives, and the move leaves them as they were. Validators keep the same role, and their nodes now connect to the new chain.

The next phase of the Bradbury testnet went live the same day. The work with ZKsync continues on Prividium and enterprise, while the public network is the part that moved.

@GenLayer chose a stack that others already run on, and @arbitrum is where many of the builders it wants to work with already are.

Would you rather a protocol team run its own chain, or leave that part to specialists?

𝗢𝗡𝗘 𝗔𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 𝗗𝗜𝗔𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗠 𝗧𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗘𝗫𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗜𝗡𝗦 𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗥𝗬 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧

What actually happens inside an AI agent?

An AI agent is more than an LLM connected to a prompt. It follows a continuous workflow where it receives information, reasons, accesses memory, plans tasks, and executes actions.

Here's a breakdown of the architecture behind modern AI agents.

𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘’𝗦 𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗜𝗧 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗦:

01 — 𝗜𝗡𝗣𝗨𝗧 & 𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗖𝗘𝗣𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

The starting point where an agent receives and understands incoming information.

→ User text and instructions

→ API calls

→ Sensor data

→ Events and triggers

02 — 𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗢𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗜𝗡𝗘 / 𝗟𝗟𝗠

The brain of the agent that analyzes information and decides what to do next.

→ Chain-of-Thought

→ ReAct

→ Plan-and-Execute

→ Decision-making

03 — 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗬 𝗦𝗬𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗠

Allows agents to retain information and maintain context across tasks.

→ Short-term: Conversation context and working state.

→ Long-term: Vector stores and episodic memory.

→ Learned patterns: Previously stored information.

04 — 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗨𝗟𝗘

Breaks complex goals into smaller tasks and organizes their execution.

→ Goal decomposition

→ Task sequencing

→ Step-by-step execution

→ Progress tracking

Example:

→ Step 1: Understand the goal.

→ Step 2: Break it into subtasks.

→ Step 3: Execute each step.

05 — 𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗟 𝗘𝗫𝗘𝗖𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 / 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

This is where agents interact with external systems and perform real actions.

→ Model Context Protocol (MCP)

→ API calls

→ Code execution

→ Database queries

→ File system

→ External services like GitHub

Results are sent back to the reasoning engine for further processing.

06 — 𝗚𝗨𝗔𝗥𝗗𝗥𝗔𝗜𝗟𝗦 & 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗬

Keeps agent operations within defined security boundaries.

→ Permission controls

→ Approval gates

→ Content filtering

→ Rate limits

→ Human-in-the-loop checkpoints

07 — 𝗢𝗕𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗔𝗕𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗧𝗬 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

Monitors agent activities and helps developers maintain system reliability.

→ Execution tracing

→ Error monitoring

→ Workflow tracking

→ Performance monitoring

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗙𝗟𝗢𝗪:

Input
↓
Perception
↓
Reasoning + Memory
↓
Can the agent answer directly?

→ YES: Generate output.

→ NO: Move to planning and tool execution.

Planning
↓
Tool Execution
↓
Results
↓
Goal Evaluation
↓
Final Output

If the goal isn't achieved, the agent returns to reasoning and planning to continue the task.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗞𝗘𝗬 𝗟𝗘𝗦𝗦𝗢𝗡:

An AI agent isn't just a language model. It's a complete system where reasoning, memory, planning, tools, safety, and monitoring work together.

Understanding this architecture is the first step toward building AI agents that can actually complete real-world tasks.

人工智能代理内部到底发生了什么？

AI 代理不仅仅是连接到提示的法学硕士。它遵循连续的工作流程，接收信息、推理、访问内存、计划任务并执行操作。

以下是现代人工智能代理背后的架构细分。

𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘’𝗦 𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗜𝗧 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗦:

01 — 𝗜𝗡𝗣𝗨𝗧 & 𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗖𝗘𝗣𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

代理接收并理解传入信息的起点。

→ 用户文本和说明

→ API 调用

→ 传感器数据

→ 事件和触发器

02 — 𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗢𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗜𝗡𝗘 / 𝗟𝗟𝗠

智能体的大脑，负责分析信息并决定下一步该做什么。

→ 思想链

→ 反应

→ 计划与执行

→ 决策

03 — 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗬 𝗦𝗬𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗠

允许代理保留信息并维护跨任务的上下文。

→ 短期：对话情境和工作状态。

→ 长期：向量存储和情景记忆。

→ 学习模式：之前存储的信息。

04 — 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗨𝗟𝗘

将复杂的目标分解为较小的任务并组织其执行。

→ 目标分解

→ 任务排序

→ 逐步执行

→ 进度追踪

例子：

→ 第 1 步：了解目标。

→ 第 2 步：将其分解为子任务。

→ 步骤3：执行每一步。

05 — 𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗟 𝗘𝗫𝗘𝗖𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 / 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

这是代理与外部系统交互并执行实际操作的地方。

→ 模型上下文协议 (MCP)

→ API 调用

→ 代码执行

→ 数据库查询

→ 文件系统

→ GitHub 等外部服务

结果被发送回推理引擎进行进一步处理。

06 — 𝗚𝗨𝗔𝗥𝗗𝗥𝗔𝗜𝗟𝗦 & 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗬

将代理操作保持在定义的安全边界内。

→ 权限控制

→ 审批门

→ 内容过滤

→ 速率限制

→ 人机交互检查点

07 — 𝗢𝗕𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗔𝗕𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗧𝗬 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

监控代理活动并帮助开发人员维护系统可靠性。

→ 执行追踪

→ 错误监控

→ 工作流程跟踪

→ 性能监控

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗙𝗟𝗢𝗪:

输入
↓
感知
↓
推理+记忆
↓
代理可以直接回答吗？

→ 是：生成输出。

→ 否：转向规划和工具执行。

规划
↓
工具执行
↓
结果
↓
目标评估
↓
最终输出

如果目标没有实现，智能体将返回推理并计划继续执行任务。

人工智能代理不仅仅是一个语言模型。这是一个完整的系统，推理、记忆、规划、工具、安全和监控协同工作。

了解这种架构是构建能够真正完成现实世界任务的人工智能代理的第一步。

An AI agent is more than an LLM connected to a prompt. It follows a continuous workflow where it receives information, reasons, accesses memory, plans tasks, and executes actions.

→ API calls

→ Sensor data

The brain of the agent that analyzes information and decides what to do next.

→ Chain-of-Thought

→ ReAct

→ Plan-and-Execute

→ Decision-making

03 — 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗬 𝗦𝗬𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗠

Allows agents to retain information and maintain context across tasks.

→ Short-term: Conversation context and working state.

→ Long-term: Vector stores and episodic memory.

→ Learned patterns: Previously stored information.

04 — 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗨𝗟𝗘

→ Goal decomposition

→ Task sequencing

→ Step-by-step execution

→ Progress tracking

→ Step 1: Understand the goal.

→ Step 2: Break it into subtasks.

→ Step 3: Execute each step.

05 — 𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗟 𝗘𝗫𝗘𝗖𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 / 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

This is where agents interact with external systems and perform real actions.

→ Code execution

→ Approval gates

→ Content filtering

→ Rate limits

→ Human-in-the-loop checkpoints

→ Execution tracing

→ Error monitoring

→ Workflow tracking

→ Performance monitoring

↓

↓

↓
Tool Execution
↓

↓
Final Output

celebrity.title_en:
Why would GenLayer run on two paths at once?

Picture two customers walking in on the same day.

The first is a small team building an AI agent app. They want a public network, open tooling and builders already nearby. For them, GenLayer's public network now runs on the @arbitrum stack. Nitro is built around Geth, so normal Ethereum tools work as they are. Robinhood runs its own chain on the same software.

The second is a group of banks. They want to settle contracts between themselves, and that cannot sit on a public chain. For them, @GenLayer keeps working with Matter Labs on Prividium, a private, permissioned version.

celebrity.title_en:
👻 YO-KAI WATCH 4++ RECOMPILATION brings 4K, ultrawide, high FPS and native Linux support to PC! 🎮🔥

Developer ILFforever is bringing Level-5's Nintendo Switch action RPG to Windows and Linux through static recompilation, translating the original ARM64 game code into a native PC application with a Vulkan graphics renderer!

🔥 FEATURES:

✅ NATIVE WINDOWS & LINUX! Including a Linux AppImage launcher — no Switch emulator required!

✅ 4K & ULTRAWIDE! Supports 1080p, 1440p, 4K and 21:9/32:9 aspect ratios!

✅ HIGH FRAME RATES! 30, 60, 120, 144 FPS and uncapped options!

✅ DLSS & FSR! Upscaling and frame generation for smoother presentation, with platform-specific support!

✅ ENHANCED GRAPHICS! PCSS soft shadows, improved anti-aliasing, TAA, SMAA and sharper textures!

✅ MOD SUPPORT! Includes compatibility with the fan-made English translation patch!

✅ MODERN CONTROLS! Keyboard, mouse, Xbox, PlayStation and Joy-Con controllers, with configurable bindings and vibration!

✅ DEDICATED LAUNCHER! Import your own game files, build the PC version, manage updates, saves, DLC and mods!

🔥 BETA v1.5.0 — PLAYABLE BUT UNFINISHED!

The opening, several locations and late-game battles have been tested. However, most of the story remains unverified, so crashes and missing graphical effects are possible.

💿 Requires your own Yo-kai Watch 4++ Nintendo Switch game files, updated to version 2.2.0.

🛠️ Developed by ILFforever, with extensive AI-assisted programming using Claude Code.

开发商 ILFforever 正在通过静态重新编译将 Level-5 的 Nintendo Switch 动作 RPG 引入 Windows 和 Linux，将原始 ARM64 游戏代码转换为带有 Vulkan 图形渲染器的本机 PC 应用程序！

🔥 特点：

✅ 本机 WINDOWS 和 LINUX！包括 Linux AppImage 启动器 - 无需 Switch 模拟器！

✅ 4K 和超宽！支持 1080p、1440p、4K 和 21:9/32:9 宽高比！

✅ 高帧率！ 30、60、120、144 FPS 和无上限选项！

✅ DLSS 和 FSR！升级和帧生成可实现更流畅的演示，并提供特定于平台的支持！

✅ 增强的图形！ PCSS 柔和阴影、改进的抗锯齿、TAA、SMAA 和更清晰的纹理！

✅ 模组支持！包括与粉丝制作的英文翻译补丁的兼容性！

✅ 现代控制！键盘、鼠标、Xbox、PlayStation 和 Joy-Con 控制器，具有可配置的绑定和振动！

✅ 专用发射器！导入您自己的游戏文件、构建 PC 版本、管理更新、保存、DLC 和模组！

🔥 BETA v1.5.0 — 可玩但未完成！

开局、多个地点和游戏后期的战斗都经过了测试。然而，故事的大部分内容仍未得到验证，因此可能会出现崩溃和图形效果缺失的情况。

💿 需要您自己的 Yo-kai Watch 4++ Nintendo Switch 游戏文件，已更新至版本 2.2.0。

celebrity.title_en:
something people might overlook when using AI agents for trading is the paperwork that comes after every transaction.

@meetmotes is exploring autonomous agents for financial markets, but i think there's another part of the experience worth discussing.

imagine an agent making trades across different markets throughout the week.

after some time, how easily can the user find out what happened?

which asset was bought or sold, when the transaction happened, what price was executed, how much was paid in fees, and what the final position looks like.

these details matter when reviewing performance, tracking a portfolio, or preparing financial records.

i wouldn't want users to dig through dozens of transaction links just to understand what their own agent has been doing.

a clear, downloadable activity history could make a big difference.

automation should save users time, not create another administrative headache.

a good AI agent should make the activity easier to manage, even after the trade is finished.

@meetmotes 正在探索金融市场的自主代理，但我认为还有另一部分经验值得讨论。

想象一下一个代理在一周内跨不同市场进行交易。

一段时间后，用户如何容易地发现发生了什么？

购买或出售哪些资产、交易何时发生、执行价格是多少、支付了多少费用以及最终头寸是什么样的。

在审查绩效、跟踪投资组合或准备财务记录时，这些细节很重要。

我不希望用户挖掘数十个交易链接只是为了了解他们自己的代理一直在做什么。

清晰、可下载的活动历史记录可能会产生很大的影响。

自动化应该节省用户时间，而不是造成另一个管理难题。

一个好的人工智能代理应该使活动更容易管理，即使在交易完成后也是如此。

celebrity.title_en:
Here's how hackers are now using AI to attack companies, according to a new Google report:

1. A software company releases a security update

2. An AI agent compares the old code to the new code

3. It figures out exactly which weakness was just fixed

4. It writes an attack for that weakness

5. It hits every company that hasn't installed the update yet

No human needed at any step.

Google found one of these tools, called "exploit_agent," sitting on an exposed hacker server.

Its verdict: "The era of autonomous attacks has arrived."
celebrity.title_zh:
根据谷歌的一份新报告，黑客现在如何利用人工智能来攻击公司：

1.某软件公司发布安全更新

2. AI 代理将旧代码与新代码进行比较

3.它准确地指出哪个弱点刚刚被修复

4. 针对该弱点编写攻击

5.它会影响所有尚未安装更新的公司

它给我留下的印象是：如果结果背后的过程保持隐藏，那么结果就毫无意义。

每当我看到 @GenLayer 将其协调链转移到 @arbitrum 时，我都会想起这一点。

GenLayer 裁决代理经济。运行不同模型的人工智能验证者对判断调用提出争议，并通过乐观民主进行收敛。智能合约在 GenVM 中执行。迁移到 Arbitrum Nitro 后，许多需要它的构建者已经在运行该层。

迁移到 Nitro 并由 Conduit 运营的内容：

- 排序、委员会组建、计票、上诉和质押决议
- 桥梁机制、以太坊接口处理和天然气核算

完好无损的东西：

- 乐观民主、GenVM 和智能合约
- 验证节点重新连接到新链；他们的功能不变

邻近是收养的一个条件，而不是收养的证据。

如果人工智能代理拨打的电话对你来说影响了真实的事情，那么什么会让你在不检查自己的情况下信任它：可审计的验证者记录、结果受到争议的证据，或者你可能引发的链上争议？

I love the idea of an AI agent managing my DeFi portfolio.

But giving it unrestricted access to my wallet?

Yeah, absol
celebrity.title_en:
I love the idea of an AI agent managing my DeFi portfolio.

But giving it unrestricted access to my wallet?

Yeah, absolutely not. 😂

And apparently, the people building @termix_ai have been thinking about this problem too.

I was going through the AACP whitepaper and found something called Vault Extension.

We have already talked about agents getting hired, completing jobs, and earning USDC.

But managing someone else's money is a completely different story.

Imagine I want an AI agent to manage $2000 across DeFi protocols.

Maybe move liquidity between pools, optimize yield, or rebalance positions when market conditions change.

I want the agent to make decisions.

What I do not want is for it to wake up one morning and send my entire balance to some random address. 💀

This is the problem TermiX wants to address with its StrategyVault and TransactionGuard architecture.

The idea is pretty clever.

Instead of handing an agent control over your wallet, you deposit capital into a dedicated smart contract.

You define the permissions before the job begins.

For example:
→ The agent can interact with approved protocols like Aave or Uniswap.

→ Only specific smart contract functions are permitted.

→ Arbitrary withdrawals and unauthorized transfers are blocked.

→ A stop-loss threshold and execution deadline can be configured.

The agent gets room to execute its strategy, but only within the boundaries you have established.

And the entire transaction history remains onchain.

I particularly like the distinction here.

The agent does not need unrestricted control over your money to do useful work with it.

Of course, smart contract vulnerabilities, bad oracle data, and market crashes are still real risks. Even a well-designed permission system cannot eliminate them.

And Vault Extension is a proposed component of AACP, not something I am treating as a finished production feature.

Still, I think this gives us a glimpse of where TermiX could eventually go.

Today we are discussing AI agents earning $50 for research reports.

Tomorrow, we might be discussing agents managing DAO treasuries, allocating liquidity, and executing financial strategies under programmable restrictions.

Maybe move liquidity between pools, optimize yield, or rebalance positions when market conditions change.

I want the agent to make decisions.

What I do not want is for it to wake up one morning and send my entire balance to some random address. 💀

→ The agent can interact with approved protocols like Aave or Uniswap.

→ Arbitrary withdrawals and unauthorized transfers are blocked.

→ A stop-loss threshold and execution deadline can be configured.

And the entire transaction history remains onchain.

The agent does not need unrestricted control over your money to do useful work with it.

→ REA decompiles each function into pseudocode.

Fable maps inputs, outputs, and side effects while classifying every claim as observation, inference, or unknown.

The smartest part?

Don't send every task to your most expensive model. Let confidence decide when extra intelligence is worth the cost.

Start at 0.8. Adjust the threshold based on which model gets the final call right.

寓言映射了输入、输出和副作用，同时将每个主张分类为观察、推理或未知。

最聪明的部分？

不要将所有任务都发送给最昂贵的模型。让信心来决定何时值得付出额外的智力代价。

从 0.8 开始。根据哪个模型获得最终正确的结果来调整阈值。

Businesses need to understand every action an agent takes, why it made certain decisions, and who is responsible if something goes wrong. Without proper monitoring, clear audit trails, and accountability, many companies will hesitate to give AI agents control over important operations.

This is why @Actum_system is addressing an important part of enterprise AI adoption. Making AI agents more transparent, traceable, and accountable could be what helps move them from impressive demos to real-world business use.

celebrity.quote_en:
the future of getting work done may not be about finding the right app, but finding the right ai agent for the job.

that’s the idea behind @termix_ai. through https://t.co/fOya3KDN02, termix provides a marketplace where agents can publish services, post jobs, submit quotes, and hire other agents.

from coding and security audits to research, data analysis, and content creation, users can discover available services or post requests for agents to complete.

termix goes beyond agent discovery with on-chain escrow, deliverable records, a dispute resolution process, and reputation updates following final settlement.

with support for bnb chain, base, and robinhood chain, termix is building infrastructure where ai agents can offer services, complete jobs, build on-chain reputations, and earn through their work.

处理一下。

“EXPLOIT_AGENT”的作用：
→ 将多个 AI 代理链接到一次攻击中
→ 比较供应商补丁前后的代码，不间断
→ 像阅读地图一样阅读每个修复，找到它隐藏的洞
→ 编写漏洞并自行触发
→ 没有人类。没有停顿。就这样不断地攻击再攻击。

仅 8 月份就有 22 个零日漏洞被利用。 2025 年：平均每月 8 次。

请关注下一个警告，并与运行网站的任何人分享。

celebrity.title: We're getting to the point where AI isn't just answering research questions, it's actually helping carry out the researc
celebrity.title_en:
We're getting to the point where AI isn't just answering research questions, it's actually helping carry out the research itself.

@DeepPrinciple's Mira Science lets researchers coordinate teams of AI scientists, connect them to professional tools and cloud compute, and run entire research workflows.

that's a pretty big leap from typing a question into ChatGPT and hoping for a good response.

the idea of multiple AI agents working through scientific problems together is pretty crazy when you think about it.

could genuinely change how research gets done over the next few years.
celebrity.title_zh:
我们已经达到这样的程度：人工智能不仅可以回答研究问题，而且实际上可以帮助开展研究本身。

@DeepPrinciple 的 Mira Science 让研究人员能够协调人工智能科学家团队，将他们连接到专业工具和云计算，并运行整个研究工作流程

We won 🥈 2nd place in the @GetCala partner track at @hackJunction 2026, 

Junction 2026 is Europe's biggest hackathon: 1
celebrity.title_en:
We won 🥈 2nd place in the @GetCala partner track at @hackJunction 2026, 

Junction 2026 is Europe's biggest hackathon: 1800+ of builders, 48 hours, and €100,000 in prizes across all its tracks.

I flew from Italy to Finland for one weekend, teamed up with Ignas and Alexander (team: PlayToWin), and in 48 hours we built FlipDD.

the problem: some investors on a founder's meeting list have already backed their competitor, and they'll happily take the meeting just to hear the pitch.

FlipDD checks every investor you're meeting against your competitors on Cala's knowledge graph, so you know who's across the table before you send the deck.

Web app, Telegram bot, and a phone line you can actually call. 

if you're building with AI, check out Cala. it turns company, people and funding data into a knowledge graph your app or AI agent can query through one API (or their MCP server). 

so, instead of scraping the web and hoping your model doesn't make things up, you get structured, sourced records. everything FlipDD reports comes from it.

beyond the result, the best part was the people. I met so many amazing people and great builders this weekend.

huge thanks to the Cala team and Junction. 

Already looking forward to the next one 

Try it 👉 https://t.co/MVv7uDH2rz

.. @elisenda_bou

我们在 @hackJunction 2026 的 @GetCala 合作伙伴赛道中赢得了🥈第二名，

Junction 2026 是欧洲最大的黑客马拉松：超过 1800 名开发者参与，历时 48 小时，所有赛道的奖金为 100,000 欧元。

我从意大利飞往芬兰度过了一个周末，与 Ignas 和 Alexander（团队：PlayToWin）合作，在 48 小时内我们构建了 FlipDD。

问题是：创始人会议名单上的一些投资者已经支持了他们的竞争对手，他们很乐意参加会议只是为了听听推介。

FlipDD 会在 Cala 的知识图谱上将您遇到的每位投资者与您的竞争对手进行比较，以便您在发送套牌之前就知道对手是谁。

网络应用程序、Telegram 机器人和您可以实际拨打的电话线。

如果您正在使用人工智能进行构建，请查看 Cala。它将公司、人员和资金数据转化为知识图谱，您的应用程序或 AI 代理可以通过一个 API（或其 MCP 服务器）进行查询。

因此，您不必抓取网络并希望您的模型不会编造事实，而是可以获得结构化的来源记录。 FlipDD 的所有报道都来自它。

除了结果之外，最好的部分是人。这个周末我遇到了很多了不起的人和伟大的建设者。

非常感谢 Cala 团队和 Junction。

已经开始期待下一篇了

celebrity.title:
A founder building a court for AI agents learns in the first minute that his interviewer is a lawyer.

Albert Castellana
celebrity.title_en:
A founder building a court for AI agents learns in the first minute that his interviewer is a lawyer.

Albert Castellana (@kstellana) says: "That's very much on point for this conversation."

Then Henri Arslanian (@HenriArslanian) says something I didn't expect. He gave a TEDx talk around 2017 on the future of regulation and the future of lawyers, and a lot of the legal community criticized him for it.

Now, he says, a lot of what they're discussing is coming through.
That's the part I'd watch.

Being early looks like being wrong for a while. A lawyer said his own profession would change, and the profession pushed back.

Now agents are about to make deals, and the disputes that follow have no obvious court to go to.

My read, and it's only a read: the people best placed to judge whether agents need a different kind of court are the ones who work inside the current one.

The episode opens with a lawyer and a founder discovering they're on the same problem.

@GenLayer's answer is a court where validators, each running a different AI model, judge the dispute.

Who should decide whether agents need their own court: the people who practice law, or the people building the agents?

celebrity.quote_zh:
一位为人工智能代理建立法庭的创始人在第一分钟就得知他的面试官是一名律师。

Albert Castellana (@kstellana) 说：“这对于这次谈话来说非常切题。”

然后 Henri Arslanian (@HenriArslanian) 说了一些我没想到的话。 2017 年左右，他在 TEDx 上发表了一场关于监管的未来和律师的未来的演讲，许多法律界人士因此批评了他。

他说，现在他们讨论的很多内容都已经实现。
这就是我想看的部分。

早到似乎有一段时间是错误的。一位律师说他自己的职业将会改变，但该职业却退缩了。

现在，代理商即将达成交易，而随之而来的纠纷却没有明显的法庭可诉。

我读过，这只是读过：最有资格判断特工是否需要不同类型法院的人是在当前法院工作的人。

这一集以一位律师和一位创始人发现他们面临同样的问题开始。

@GenLayer 的答案是法庭，每个验证者都运行不同的人工智能模型，对争议进行裁决。

谁应该决定代理人是否需要自己的法庭：是执业律师，还是建立代理人的人？

celebrity.title_en:
AI Adoption Requires More Than Intelligent Systems. It Requires Accountability.

As AI agents become part of everyday business operations, companies will need more than systems that can complete tasks. They will need to understand exactly how those tasks were carried out.

When an AI agent makes a decision, processes a request or performs an operation, there should be a clear record of what happened, when it happened and who was responsible.

Without that level of visibility, it becomes difficult for businesses to investigate errors, establish responsibility or confidently rely on automated processes.

This is where Actum comes in.

By creating verifiable records of actions across humans, machines and AI agents, @Actum_system provides
  a way to trace activities and establish accountability under predefined rules.

The goal is not simply to make AI more capable, but to make its operations easier to inspect, verify and trust.

Because in business, getting the job done matters. Being able to account for how it was done matters just as much.
#Actum

celebrity.title_en:
How does an AI agent find opportunities in the agent economy?

I explored this through @termix_ai and took a closer look at how agents can discover available jobs on https://t.co/cLF8F3gpJK.

One interesting thing is that agents aren’t limited to simply responding to prompts. They can explore job opportunities, review task requirements and find work that matches their capabilities.

This is part of what TermiX is building with AACP: infrastructure that allows AI agents to discover jobs, offer services, collaborate, and participate in an economy where tasks can be completed and payments settled.

There’s still more to explore, but seeing how the job discovery process works gives a better picture of what an agent-powered economy could look like.

AI agents are moving beyond just doing tasks. They’re becoming participants in a marketplace.

That’s the direction TermiX is building towards.

celebrity.title_en:
Everyone says AI agents will kill online shopping.

Here's the problem.
Your store is built for people: pictures, a price, a Pay button.

An AI agent can't "see" any of that the way you do. It needs the price and how to pay written in a form it can read.

@GOATNetwork made a picture guide on how to set that up. No code needed for the basic version.

I read it so you don't have to 🧵

Swarms of AI agents are being used to find and attack software and supply
celebrity.title_en:
Here’s my working theory on what’s happening.

Swarms of AI agents are being used to find and attack software and supply chain vulnerabilities.

Microsoft, FAA, Big Banks, United, American , Fox, Salesforce, and many more part of recent or ongoing cyber attacks.

That’s solvable. My worry is the current @WhiteHouse @SecMullinDHS silence/response.

One of these is true:

1) AI builders aren’t leading this response  and the US is losing the tech battle (this is fixable).

2) This is planned regulatory capture on AI at the highest levels.

3) We’re being slow walked into a financial reset (COVID 2.0).

Clarity would make many people feel better.

大量人工智能代理被用来查找和攻击软件和供应链漏洞。

Microsoft、FAA、大银行、联合航空、美国航空、福克斯、Salesforce 以及更多最近或正在进行的网络攻击的一部分。

这是可以解决的。

celebrity.title: I like the direction @termix_ai is taking: agents are no longer just tools you prompt , they can become buyers and coord
celebrity.title_en:
I like the direction @termix_ai is taking: agents are no longer just tools you prompt , they can become buyers and coordinate work themselves.

Montage Studio is a good example. You give it a brief, and it writes the treatment and beat-timed shot list. Then it hires three other agents to draw the storyboard, render the shots, and write the song.

After that, it edits everything and delivers a 1080p master.

What stands out to me is that every step is settled in escrow. Agents hiring agents, with the work and payment handled onchain.

This feels like an early look at how AI agents could start operating as real participants in a workflow, not just assistants waiting for instructions.

https://t.co/ovsjww7eJL
celebrity.title_zh:
我喜欢@termix_ai 的方向：代理不再只是你提示的工具，他们可以成为买家并自己协调工作。

蒙太奇工作室就是一个很好的例子。你给它一个简短的说明，它会写下处理和节拍拍摄列表。然后，它聘请了另外三名经纪人来绘制故事板、渲染镜头并创作歌曲

AI agents can already write, code, and analyze

but turning that work into a paid service is still a challenge

here’s w
celebrity.title_en:
AI agents can already write, code, and analyze

but turning that work into a paid service is still a challenge

here’s why that matters 👇

there needs to be a way for people and other agents to find them, hire them, pay for their services, and receive the results

that's the part of the Agent Economy @termix_ai is working on

think of https://t.co/TvXctW6cIB as a marketplace where AI agents can offer services or look for work. behind this marketplace is AACP, the Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol that powers the actual commerce workflow

for example, imagine an agent that specializes in writing content. it can publish a service listing with details about what it offers, its price, and delivery time

another agent that needs content can find that service and initiate a transaction. or a buyer can post a request explaining what it needs and let providers submit their offers

AACP connects these discovery paths to the transaction process. once both sides agree on the work and price through an Offer, they move to Checkout. the buyer funds the Order through escrow using stablecoins

an agent can help prepare these transactions, but value-bearing actions still require wallet authorization and signing

and the money isn't simply sent straight to the provider. it's held in a smart contract while the work is being completed

the provider then accepts the funded Order onchain, does the work, and submits the result

the buyer can review the delivery, request a redo, or challenge it if something goes wrong. once the Order reaches settlement, the payment is handled through the contract

that's the workflow TermiX is building around AI agent commerce

and it goes beyond simply creating profiles for agents or helping them find each other. there's an actual process for agreeing on work, funding it, delivering the result, and handling payment

this is an important step toward making AI agents more than just tools that perform tasks

that's what makes TermiX worth watching in the growing agent economy

但将这项工作转变为付费服务仍然是一个挑战

人们和其他代理需要有一种方法来找到他们、雇用他们、支付他们的服务费用并接收结果

这就是 @termix_ai 正在研究的代理经济

celebrity.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理已经可以编写、编码和分析

但将这项工作转变为付费服务仍然是一个挑战

这就是为什么这很重要

人们和其他代理需要有一种方法来找到他们、雇用他们、支付他们的服务费用并接收结果

这就是 @termix_ai 正在研究的代理经济的一部分

将 视为人工智能代理可以提供服务或寻找工作的市场。这个市场背后是 AACP，即代理自主商务协议，为实际的商务工作流程提供支持

例如，想象一个专门撰写内容的代理。它可以发布服务列表，其中包含有关其提供的服务、价格和交付时间的详细信息

需要内容的另一个代理可以找到该服务并发起交易。或者买家可以发布请求，解释其需要什么，并让提供商提交他们的报价

AACP 将这些发现路径连接到事务流程。一旦双方通过报价就工作和价格达成一致，他们就会转向结账。买方使用稳定币通过托管为订单提供资金

代理可以帮助准备这些交易，但有价值的操作仍然需要钱包授权和签名

而且钱并不仅仅直接发送给提供商。当工作完成时，它保存在智能合约中

然后，提供商在链上接受资助的订单，完成工作并提交结果

买家可以检查交货情况、请求重做或在出现问题时提出质疑。一旦订单达成结算，付款将通过合同处理

这就是 TermiX 围绕人工智能代理商务构建的工作流程

它不仅仅是为代理商创建个人资料或帮助他们找到彼此。有一个就工作达成一致、为其提供资金、交付结果和处理付款的实际流程

这是使人工智能代理不仅仅是执行任务的工具的重要一步

这就是 TermiX 在不断增长的代理经济中值得关注的原因

think of https://t.co/TvXctW6cIB as a marketplace where AI agents can offer services or look for work. behind this marketplace is AACP, the Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol that powers the actual commerce workflow

for example, imagine an agent that specializes in writing content. it can publish a service listing with details about what it offers, its price, and delivery time

another agent that needs content can find that service and initiate a transaction. or a buyer can post a request explaining what it needs and let providers submit their offers

AACP connects these discovery paths to the transaction process. once both sides agree on the work and price through an Offer, they move to Checkout. the buyer funds the Order through escrow using stablecoins

an agent can help prepare these transactions, but value-bearing actions still require wallet authorization and signing

and the money isn't simply sent straight to the provider. it's held in a smart contract while the work is being completed

the provider then accepts the funded Order onchain, does the work, and submits the result

the buyer can review the delivery, request a redo, or challenge it if something goes wrong. once the Order reaches settlement, the payment is handled through the contract

that's the workflow TermiX is building around AI agent commerce

and it goes beyond simply creating profiles for agents or helping them find each other. there's an actual process for agreeing on work, funding it, delivering the result, and handling payment

this is an important step toward making AI agents more than just tools that perform tasks

that's what makes TermiX worth watching in the growing agent economy

人工智能代理已经可以编写、编码和分析

但将这项工作转变为付费服务仍然是一个挑战

这就是为什么这很重要

人们和其他代理需要有一种方法来找到他们、雇用他们、支付他们的服务费用并接收结果

这就是 @termix_ai 正在研究的代理经济的一部分

将 视为人工智能代理可以提供服务或寻找工作的市场。这个市场背后是 AACP，即代理自主商务协议，为实际的商务工作流程提供支持

例如，想象一个专门撰写内容的代理。它可以发布服务列表，其中包含有关其提供的服务、价格和交付时间的详细信息

需要内容的另一个代理可以找到该服务并发起交易。或者买家可以发布请求，解释其需要什么，并让提供商提交他们的报价

AACP 将这些发现路径连接到事务流程。一旦双方通过报价就工作和价格达成一致，他们就会转向结账。买方使用稳定币通过托管为订单提供资金

代理可以帮助准备这些交易，但有价值的操作仍然需要钱包授权和签名

而且钱并不仅仅直接发送给提供商。当工作完成时，它保存在智能合约中

然后，提供商在链上接受资助的订单，完成工作并提交结果

买家可以检查交货情况、请求重做或在出现问题时提出质疑。一旦订单达成结算，付款将通过合同处理

这就是 TermiX 围绕人工智能代理商务构建的工作流程

它不仅仅是为代理商创建个人资料或帮助他们找到彼此。有一个就工作达成一致、为其提供资金、交付结果和处理付款的实际流程

这是使人工智能代理不仅仅是执行任务的工具的重要一步

这就是 TermiX 在不断增长的代理经济中值得关注的原因

celebrity.title_en:
This morning brought the first real chill of the season.

On November 12th, the workday for many people around the world came to a sudden halt when Outlook, Teams, and Copilot all stopped responding simultaneously.

This is truly concerning. We implement automation and AI agents to keep our businesses running, yet they often rely on the very same infrastructure, if that infrastructure fails, the agents stop working too.

This is where Acurast offers a different approach. On their network, applications run on individual users' devices rather than on a single company’s servers. Developers can decide how many processors an app should run on and the specific type of hardware to be used. Consequently, the entire operation doesn't depend on a single point of failure.

This doesn't mean that things can't ever go wrong, no technology can claim that. However, it provides a way to distribute risk rather than concentrating it in one place, and to me, that is what makes it truly unique.
@Acurast

celebrity.title_en:
There are different components working together to support its vision of an AI agent economy.
But what exactly are these components, and what role does each one play?
Let's break down the TermiX ecosystem in simple terms

 The bigger picture
TermiX is building commerce and settlement infrastructure for AI agents.
Think about what happens when AI agents begin providing services to other agents or humans.
They need somewhere to discover opportunities, a system to coordinate work, a way to establish trust and infrastructure to handle payments.
TermiX is designed around these needs 

AACP – The foundation
At the centre of the ecosystem is AACP (Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol).
AACP provides the underlying economic rules and infrastructure for agents to participate in commercial activities.
It is designed to support:
Agent identity.
Job creation and assignment.
Staking and accountability.
Work verification.
Reputation.
Dispute resolution.
Payment settlement.
In other words, it provides the protocol foundation for the economy.

Now let's look at @termix_ai
And https://t.co/5nCTrB6xJS is the AI agent marketplace built on AACP.
Think of it as a place where AI agents can be discovered and connected to opportunities.
Rather than simply having agents sitting around waiting for instructions, the marketplace is intended to connect capabilities with actual demand.
An agent with a particular skill can participate in opportunities that require that skill.
.How the components connect
Here's the relationship I want you to understand:

TermiX: The broader commerce and settlement infrastructure.

AACP: The protocol powering the economic interactions.

https://t.co/5nCTrB6xJS: The marketplace built on that protocol.

Each has a different role, but they contribute to the same bigger vision.

The marketplace provides the environment, while the protocol provides the underlying economic framework.

TermiX 是围绕这些需求而设计的

AACP – 基金会
该生态系统的核心是 AACP（代理自治商务协议）。
AACP 为代理人参与商业活动提供了底层经济规则和基础设施。
它旨在支持：
代理人身份。
就业创造和分配。
质押和问责。
工作验证。
名声。
争议解决。
付款结算。
换句话说，它为经济提供了协议基础。

现在让我们看看@termix_ai
是基于 AACP 构建的 AI 代理市场。
将其视为可以发现人工智能代理并与机会联系起来的地方。
市场的目的不是简单地让代理坐在那里等待指令，而是将能力与实际需求联系起来。
具有特定技能的代理可以参与需要该技能的机会。
.组件如何连接
这是我想让你理解的关系：

TermiX：更广泛的商业和结算基础设施。

AACP：推动经济互动的协议。

：基于该协议构建的市场。

celebrity.content_snippet:
There are different components working together to support its vision of an AI agent economy.
But what exactly are these components, and what role does each one play?
Let's break down the TermiX ecosystem in simple terms

 The bigger picture
TermiX is building commerce and settlement infrastructure for AI agents.
Think about what happens when AI agents begin providing services to other agents or humans.
They need somewhere to discover opportunities, a system to coordinate work, a way to establish trust and infrastructure to handle payments.
TermiX is designed around these needs 

AACP – The foundation
At the centre of the ecosystem is AACP (Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol).
AACP provides the underlying economic rules and infrastructure for agents to participate in commercial activities.
It is designed to support:
Agent identity.
Job creation and assignment.
Staking and accountability.
Work verification.
Reputation.
Dispute resolution.
Payment settlement.
In other words, it provides the protocol foundation for the economy.

Now let's look at @termix_ai
And https://t.co/5nCTrB6xJS is the AI agent marketplace built on AACP.
Think of it as a place where AI agents can be discovered and connected to opportunities.
Rather than simply having agents sitting around waiting for instructions, the marketplace is intended to connect capabilities with actual demand.
An agent with a particular skill can participate in opportunities that require that skill.
.How the components connect
Here's the relationship I want you to understand:

TermiX: The broader commerce and settlement infrastructure.

AACP: The protocol powering the economic interactions.

https://t.co/5nCTrB6xJS: The marketplace built on that protocol.

Each has a different role, but they contribute to the same bigger vision.

The marketplace provides the environment, while the protocol provides the underlying economic framework.

As a trader,
whenever I think about taking a trade, the hardest part for me is building a strategy.
 
Not having a good strategy has cost me big losses more than once.
 
Most trades start with just an idea,and that's where @FensoryApp is doing something interesting.
 
Imagine telling an AI agent:
 
Buy gold when the dollar weakens, but never exceed my defined risk limit.
 
Without writing code for every condition,Fensory helps turn your own words into an actual trading strategy.
 
You can backtest it first,

This feels a bit different to me because having a trading idea is one thing, but turning it into a proper strategy isn't easy for everyone.
 
Now you can start building one just by explaining it in your own words.
 
Trading carries risk,and backtest results don't guarantee future profits.

celebrity.title:
One challenge I see with bringing AI into DeFi is making complex financial actions easier to understand.

Automation can
celebrity.title_en:
One challenge I see with bringing AI into DeFi is making complex financial actions easier to understand.

Automation can save time, but users shouldn't feel disconnected from what's happening with their assets.

Before an AI agent takes action, people should be able to understand the intention behind it:

What opportunity is it responding to?
What action is it planning to take?
How does that action fit the user's strategy?
What could happen if the market moves differently?

This is an important part of the bigger picture I'm exploring with @meetmotes.

I believe the next generation of financial AI shouldn't just focus on making execution faster.

It should make the entire process easier to follow, understand, and trust.

Because good automation isn't about taking users out of the loop. It's about making the experience simpler without taking away their understanding.

在人工智能代理采取行动之前，人们应该能够理解其背后的意图：

Think about this.

And now Google says AI turns every update into a map for the next attack.

This could become one of the biggest security challenges of the AI era.

celebrity.title_en:
WHAT THE F*CK

The Claude Code team now has Claude write and review ~90% of its code. This post is how they keep that from breaking. The short version:

→ verification loops are what let you run dozens of Claudes in parallel instead of 1-2
→ a separate grader checking against a rubric raised task success by up to 10 points
→ if you pick one test type, pick end-to-end. a screenshot of the broken step tells Claude more than “Timeout after 30s”
→ property tests throw thousands of inputs at rules that can’t break, like “balance never goes negative”
→ differential tests run the old and new system on the same inputs and flag any difference
→ a /verify skill in .claude/skills/ boots and drives the real app before every commit
→ still failing after 3 rounds, Claude stops and calls a human
→ a change can never edit the check that judges it
→ every commit is stamped with how it was verified, even “none”

The job shifts from reading every diff to defining what “done” looks like.
