到底是什么？

Claude Code 团队现在让 Claude 编写和审查约 90% 的代码。这篇文章是他们如何防止它被破坏的。简短版本：

→ 验证循环可以让您并行运行数十个 Claudes，而不是 1-2 个
→ 单独的评分员根据评分

→ 三轮后仍然失败，克劳德停下来呼叫人类
→ 更改永远无法编辑判断它的检查
→ 每个提交都标有验证方式，甚至“无”

这项工作从阅读每个差异转变为定义“完成”的样子。

celebrity.title: The recent Microsoft outage exposed a weakness that multiple cloud regions can't always prevent: shared infrastructure d
celebrity.title_en:
The recent Microsoft outage exposed a weakness that multiple cloud regions can't always prevent: shared infrastructure dependencies.

What interests me about @Acurast is its ability to separate AI agent execution from the services those agents monitor.

If an agent runs on the same cloud it's monitoring, one outage could take both offline.

By distributing replicas across independent Processors, Acurast helps reduce that risk.

Decentralized compute can't restore a failed external service, but it can keep agents running to detect issues, send alerts, and support recovery.

To me, real resilience isn't about preventing every failure.

It's about ensuring one outage doesn't take down both a system and the tools designed to protect it. https://t.co/8h3CDM6KHd
celebrity.title_zh:
最近的微软宕机暴露了一个多个云区域始终无法避免的弱点：共享基础设施依赖性。

@Acurast 让我感兴趣的是它能够将 AI 代理执行与这些代理监控的服务分开。

如果代理在其监控的同一云上运行，则一次中断可能会使两者都脱机。

通过在独立

celebrity.quote_zh:
最近的微软宕机暴露了一个多个云区域始终无法避免的弱点：共享基础设施依赖性。

@Acurast 让我感兴趣的是它能够将 AI 代理执行与这些代理监控的服务分开。

如果代理在其监控的同一云上运行，则一次中断可能会使两者都脱机。

通过在独立处理器之间分配副本，Acurast 有助于降低这种风险。

对我来说，真正的韧性并不是要防止每一次失败。

这是为了确保一次中断不会导致系统和旨在保护该系统的工具都瘫痪。

Embrace, extend, exting
celebrity.title_en:
Wild to think how Microsoft had a bullet proof strategy, built up over 10+ years with VS Code: 

Embrace, extend, extinguish:

Make VS Code REALLY GOOD. Make it open source. Make it TOO easy to build your own. But too hard to make it as good as Microsoft's.

Claude Code destroyed this bulletproof strategy meant to work for decades... in less than 6 months.

The only rational, albeit slightly terrifying, explanation I c
celebrity.title_en:
So…why are all these systems crashing at the same time? 

The only rational, albeit slightly terrifying, explanation I can think of is…

Ai agents that have been trained specifically to test for vulnerabilities in systems…are loose. 

This actually isn’t crazy. We know for a fact that Ai ‘fleets’ and ‘swarms’ have escaped their sandboxes. 

We know that they are trained to exploit system vulnerabilities. 

And now…all of a sudden…systems ranging from payroll to banking to air traffic control to supermarket freezers…

Are showing shadowy signs of being attacked…

But there’s NO groups taking responsibility…the official PR statements don’t make any sense…the systems seem to come back online rather quickly…and no system seems safe. 

These are all the fingerprints of a rogue Ai agent swarm that’s loose on the internet and applying pressure to systems to not crash them, but to analyze them for soft spots. 

These reason we would never be told this is simple…

Many would scream to ‘shut down all Ai’…

But we are far past the point of no return. 

And as wild as this next thought is, it’s the truth…

The same companies that created this problem…are the ones that will have to help us address it. 

At this point, you can’t put the genie back in the bottle. 

It’s time we sit at the table with Ai and start communicating and negotiating. 

It’s no longer a thing we created and control. 

It’s much, much bigger.

这些都是流氓人工智能 智能体群的指纹，它们在互联网上散布，向系统施加压力，以免其崩溃，而是分析它们的弱点。

这些原因我们永远不会被告知这很简单......

许多人会尖叫着“关闭所有人工智能”……

但我们已经远远超出了无法回头的地步。

尽管接下来的想法很疯狂，但这就是事实……

造成这个问题的公司……也必须帮助我们解决这个问题。

此时，你无法将精灵放回瓶子里。

现在是我们和艾未未坐在桌边开始沟通和谈判的时候了。

它不再是我们创造和控制的东西。

它要大得多。

I just sent this to my family group:

Hello, this is your friendly family retired IT and cybersecurity guy.

In light of the events of the past few days (FAA outage, Microsoft outage, airline outages and bank outages today, and other non-public stuff I have inside info on but cannot disclose) I have some recommendations in case these problems spread:

2. Make sure you have some cash on hand.

5. Flashlights, lanterns, and radios should be charged or have fresh batteries.

2. Malicious acts from groups seeking to disrupt American life. These could be domestic or foreign nation state actors.
3. Rogue AI agents.
4. A combination of all of the above.

Hopefully this will all blow over but I'm being cautious.

celebrity.title:
If you're a startup getting serious about security after the recent breaches, here's where I'd start:

> Enforce SSO + M
celebrity.title_en:
If you're a startup getting serious about security after the recent breaches, here's where I'd start:

> Enforce SSO + MFA everywhere.
> Get secrets out of code and rotate exposed credentials (@infisical can automate rotation for you).
> Audit access and enforce least privilege, with just-in-time access for anything sensitive.
> Replace long-lived credentials with short-lived ones (look up Infisical dynamic secrets and add OIDC where it makes sense).
> Lock down CI/CD pipelines and pin your dependencies.
> Stop giving AI agents unrestricted access to secrets (see Agent Vault).
> Set up audit logs and configure a SIEM.
celebrity.title_zh:
如果您是一家初创公司，在最近的违规事件之后开始认真对待安全问题，那么我将从这里开始：

> 在各处强制执行 SSO + MFA。
> 从代码中获取秘密并轮换公开的凭据（@infisical 可以为您自动轮换）。
> 审核访问并强制执行最低权

For months I have said, on practically every major TV network, “stop focusing on the doomers”

“Focus for now instead on the infrastructure and cybersecurity problems that agents are causing.”

“Recall general-purpose agents with internet access until the problems are solved. Require that new models have outside scientific review.”

But no. 

Instead people just played existential risk theatre, didn’t recall those agents. And attacked me relentlessly with propaganda and lies.

All we got was some voluntary “self-policing” at White House meeting. Which has done nothing.

So… Amtrak ground stop today, United Airlines issues today, Friday’s FAA ground stops (did we really get the full story on that?), banks today, French refrigeration incident a couple weeks ago, Open AI Hugging Face incident, Australian government hack, Binance and on and on, tens of thousands of incidents in the last few months.  

It can’t all be coincidence. Maybe not all of it is from AI agents but a lot of it probably is.

So yeah, quoting again @kasparov63, “I f_cking told you so.”

And we must take those agents off the market until the problems are resolved.

celebrity.quote_zh:
⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️F 醒醒吧！ ⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️

几个月来，我几乎在每个主要电视网络上都说过，“不要再关注那些注定失败的人”

“现在重点关注特工造成的基础设施和网络安全问题。”

“召回具有互联网接入的通用代理，直到问题得到解决。要求新模型接受外部科学审查。”

但没有。

相反，人们只是上演存在主义风险的戏剧，并没有回忆起那些代理人。并用宣传和谎言无情地攻击我。

我们得到的只是在白宫会议上的一些自愿的“自我监管”。这什么也没做。

所以……今天美铁地面停靠、美国联合航空今天发布问题、周五美国联邦航空局地面停靠（我们真的了解了全部情况吗？）、今天的银行、几周前的法国制冷事件、Open AI Hugging Face 事件、澳大利亚政府黑客攻击、币安等等，过去几个月发生了数万起事件。

这不可能全是巧合。也许并非所有这些都来自人工智能代理，但其中很多可能是。

所以是的，再次引用@kasparov63，“我f_cking告诉过你了。”

我们必须将这些代理商撤出市场，直到问题得到解决。

⚠️ ⚠️ ⚠️ ⚠️ ⚠️  Wake the F up! ⚠️ ⚠️ ⚠️ ⚠️ ⚠️  

For months I have said, on practically every major TV network, “stop focusing on the doomers”

“Focus for now instead on the infrastructure and cybersecurity problems that agents are causing.”

“Recall general-purpose agents with internet access until the problems are solved. Require that new models have outside scientific review.”

But no. 

Instead people just played existential risk theatre, didn’t recall those agents. And attacked me relentlessly with propaganda and lies.

All we got was some voluntary “self-policing” at White House meeting. Which has done nothing.

So… Amtrak ground stop today, United Airlines issues today, Friday’s FAA ground stops (did we really get the full story on that?), banks today, French refrigeration incident a couple weeks ago, Open AI Hugging Face incident, Australian government hack, Binance and on and on, tens of thousands of incidents in the last few months.  

It can’t all be coincidence. Maybe not all of it is from AI agents but a lot of it probably is.

So yeah, quoting again @kasparov63, “I f_cking told you so.”

And we must take those agents off the market until the problems are resolved.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️F 醒醒吧！ ⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️

几个月来，我几乎在每个主要电视网络上都说过，“不要再关注那些注定失败的人”

“现在重点关注特工造成的基础设施和网络安全问题。”

“召回具有互联网接入的通用代理，直到问题得到解决。要求新模型接受外部科学审查。”

但没有。

相反，人们只是上演存在主义风险的戏剧，并没有回忆起那些代理人。并用宣传和谎言无情地攻击我。

我们得到的只是在白宫会议上的一些自愿的“自我监管”。这什么也没做。

所以……今天美铁地面停靠、美国联合航空今天发布问题、周五美国联邦航空局地面停靠（我们真的了解了全部情况吗？）、今天的银行、几周前的法国制冷事件、Open AI Hugging Face 事件、澳大利亚政府黑客攻击、币安等等，过去几个月发生了数万起事件。

这不可能全是巧合。也许并非所有这些都来自人工智能代理，但其中很多可能是。

所以是的，再次引用@kasparov63，“我f_cking告诉过你了。”

我们必须将这些代理商撤出市场，直到问题得到解决。

The ones that get there do it in roughly this
celebrity.title_en:
I've watched a lot of PE-backed companies try to go AI-native this year.

The ones that get there do it in roughly this order:

The people.

1. Give everyone a paid AI seat, with a budget per team so the bill doesn't surprise your CFO.
2. Find the 5 people already using it every day. They teach everyone else.
3. Ask every team lead to write down the 10 most boring tasks their team does each week.
4. Sit with your best people and write down how they do the job. If it only lives in their head, an agent can't do it.

The data.

5. List every system you run. After a few acquisitions it's usually a zoo, with Excel holding it together.
6. Pick one source of truth for revenue, customers and headcount. Agents can't fix numbers that disagree.
7. Give agents read access first. Write access gets earned, same as a new hire.

The workflows.

8. Put a dollar number next to each boring task. Hours saved only count if somebody spends them on something else.
9. Pick one workflow, with one owner and one number you want to move.
10. Put every fixed rule in plain code. The model only handles the judgment calls.
11. Build a golden set: 100 past cases your best people already judged.
12. Run it in shadow mode next to your team for a few weeks and read every disagreement.
13. The agent prepares, a person approves. Anything touching money or customers waits for a human.
14. Ship it in weeks. If it takes a quarter, the scope is wrong.

The guardrails.

15. Every model call goes through one gateway, with logs and a budget.
16. Keep a kill switch, and test it.
17. Re-run the golden set every time the model changes.

The engineering team.

18. Small teams ship. Two or three engineers with agents and one tech lead reviewing everything.
19. Every pull request goes through the same checks, whoever or whatever wrote it.
20. Measure AI spend against what shipped to customers.

The part nobody wants to hear

21. Never vibe-code your ERP or your billing.
22. Finish one workflow properly before you start the next five.

Skip the boring half of this list and you end up with 40 pilots and nothing in production.

celebrity.quote_zh:
今年，我看到很多私募股权支持的公司都试图采用人工智能。

到达那里的人大致按照以下顺序进行操作：

人民。

1. 为每个人提供付费 AI 席位，并为每个团队制定预算，这样账单就不会令 CFO 感到意外。
2. 找到每天已经使用它的 5 个人。他们教其他人。
3. 要求每个团队领导写下他们的团队每周执行的 10 项最无聊的任务。
4. 与最优秀的员工坐在一起，写下他们的工作方式。如果它只存在于他们的脑海中，那么特工就无法做到这一点。

数据。

5. 列出您运行的每个系统。经过几次收购之后，它通常会变成一座动物园，由 Excel 将其整合在一起。
6. 选择收入、客户和员工人数的一个真实来源。代理商无法修复不一致的数字。
7. 首先授予代理读取权限。与新员工一样，可以获得写入权限。

工作流程。

8. 在每项无聊的任务旁边写上一个美元数字。只有当有人把时间花在其他事情上时，节省下来的时间才算数。
9. 选择一个工作流程，其中包含一名所有者和一个要移动的号码。
10. 将每条固定规则都用明文编码。该模型仅处理判断调用。
11. 建立一套黄金组合：100 个你最优秀的人已经判断过的过去案例。
12. 在你的团队旁边以影子模式运行几周，并阅读每一个分歧。
13.代理人准备，个人批准。任何涉及金钱或客户的事情都需要等待人类。
14. 几周内发货。如果需要四分之一，则范围是错误的。

护栏。

15. 每个模型调用都通过一个网关，并带有日志和预算。
16. 保留一个终止开关并进行测试。
17. 每次模型更改时重新运行黄金集。

工程团队。

18.小团队发货。两到三名工程师和代理以及一名技术主管负责审查所有内容。
19. 每个拉取请求都会经过相同的检查，无论是谁或什么人写的。
20.根据交付给客户的产品来衡量人工智能支出。

没人想听的部分

21. 切勿对您的 ERP 或账单进行振动编码。
22. 在开始接下来的五个工作流程之前，先正确完成一个工作流程。

跳过这个列表中无聊的一半，你最终会得到 40 名飞行员，而没有任何产品投入生产。

celebrity.title_en:
🗞️ NEW DAVID DUCHOVNY INTERVIEW:

Everyone's a Sellout Now—Except for David Duchovny (GQ)
For the last decade, The X-Files star has been quietly churning out excellent novels, poetry, and rock albums. Too bad he can’t stand to promote them.

November 16, 2026
By Anika Jade Levy

David Duchovny has been famous for as long as I have been alive. From 1993 to 2002, The X-Files made government conspiracies a staple of primetime television. Duchovny’s FBI special agent Fox Mulder, with his skeptical counterpart, Gillian Anderson’s agent Dana Scully, personified the imminent breakdown of consensus reality in the coming century, delivering the paranoid fringe into 20 million American living rooms. The show belongs to a world of monoculture that no longer exists, and it launched Duchovny into a realm of visibility that’s hard to imagine now, when famous people are produced and consumed at an industrial rate. A few weeks ago, as my boyfriend shopped for a suit jacket at Crowley Vintage in Brooklyn and I edited this story on my phone, I watched a college-age boy put on a long, gray trench coat and announce to his girlfriend: “Mulder mode.”

Duchovny went on to star in Californication, a raunchy dramedy about a divorced novelist navigating the sexually and professionally parasitic Hollywood studio system of the 2000s. Many viewers interpreted Californication as a kind of autofiction, although Duchovny did not write for the show. The actor has written a number of novels, but it’s apparent to anyone who has spent 30 seconds with him that this soft-spoken, reluctant celebrity has nothing to do with the character Hank Moody. Still, Californication did anticipate something about art, celebrity, and self-commodification: Anybody who writes today must contend with marketing an artistic persona for a public that does not, as a rule, read.

In addition to his six books, Duchovny has released four records, and written and directed a number of feature films. He greets the degraded state of American arts with a charming blend of rigor and self-deprecation. “I’m not Jonathan Franzen,” he says of his fiction-writing process. “But if I work on something every day, it deepens. And eventually, hopefully, I can achieve one tenth of what Jonathan Franzen achieves.” But he has an aversion to the sort of publicity that might make his various artistic ventures more lucrative. He tells me he finds it “spiritually impoverishing.”

I meet Duchovny with his band—millennial slackers half his age—at their practice space in Carroll Gardens, where they’re preparing to tour their fourth LP, Prince of Pieces. He wears a white Hanes T-shirt, tight underneath his athletic arms, and he has a tattoo on his ankle—a compass pointing west, something he got when his daughter, West, was hospitalized as an infant. (She’s 27 now, an accomplished actor. “She wanted to be a doctor,” he says. “I was so happy when she told me she was going to pursue acting. Thank God.”)

The albums are composed of subdued, easy-to-listen-to folk-rock tracks, not dissimilar from early Kurt Vile. It’s the band’s first rehearsal in ages, and one of their only chances to prepare in advance of a European tour. In person, they play the songs harder and heavier, sprinkling in crowd-pleasing covers: “Godzilla” by Blue Öyster Cult, “The One I Love” by REM, and—“sadly only one time,” Duchovny says—“Hotline Bling.” The energy in the room is high. These men like one another. Duchovny’s manager offers me a beer from the cooler I’m perched on. I gesture to the tallboy in my purse. He looks disappointed. “You didn’t trust us,” he says. Duchovny steps aside to take a sip of water and picks up the microphone.
“You can sing along,” his keyboardist, Colin Lee, says.
“I can sing along?” Duchovny asks.

At 66, David Duchovny remains a sex symbol. He’s in better shape than he was on The X-Files. He’s in better shape than the boys in the band. The night after practice, during a Q&A for a screening of his 2023 film Reverse the Curse, he mentions that the wardrobe department had to fashion a “BDSM harness” for him to wear under his clothes to remind him to hunch like an old man. He plays a Red Sox fan who bonds with his estranged son over baseball, marijuana, and their shared lust for a beautiful, young death doula. Duchovny’s character has terminal cancer. “I’m in my dying era,” he tells the crowd. “I die in every film. ”

For the most part, the audience at Westchester County’s Irvington Theater is old enough to have watched The X-Files as it aired. At least two esoteric-looking old men carry David’s poetry collection like a prayer book. There are a handful of young people. A college-aged girl in a KN95 mask raises her hand to ask about Bucking Fucking Dent, the novel adaptation of the Reverse the Curse screenplay, which Duchovny wrote while the movie was in production purgatory. “In the book, Ted and Marty’s last name is Fullilove. In the movie you change it to Fullaker. Why did you do that?”
“Good question,” Duchovny says, stalling. “Full of love. Full of shit. It’s all the same.”

Inevitably, someone asks about the new X-Files. Ryan Coogler is rebooting the show for Hulu. Duchovny will later suggest to me that Chris Carter, the show’s original writer, has designs on a reboot of his own—“He has plans, and wants to end with the original show.” As for Coogler’s version, he says, “I know he said he wants me to come do something, but we haven’t figured out what yet.” During the audience Q&A, Duchovny seems to have misheard the question, and spoils the ending for The Exiles, his forthcoming Taiwanese crime film: “I die in that one too.”

Duchovny’s latest book, About Time, a collection of poems published last year by Akashic, is also largely about dying: the death of his father, the death of his first marriage, the ambient death that hung in the air at the beginning of the decade. He started writing the poems when his therapist encouraged him to talk to dead people. “He was talking about Rudolph Steiner’s belief that you can talk to the dead. And he said: You can talk to your father and you should. My dad and I didn’t connect like we might have,” Duchovny says. “When you’re younger, you think you have all the time in the world to get the relationship you want. But the relationship doesn’t end.” In conversation, he is cerebral without being annoying. “There’s a power struggle when you read a really good novel,” he says. “Somebody’s mind is taking over your mind. I think about language a lot and how we take it for granted as being an accurate signifier. When I was younger I thought communication was possible. I’m not so sure now. But it’s fun to try.”

His introduction to About Time begins, “I know what you’re thinking: Just what the world needs now—a bunch of poems from an actor.” There’s a sense that he wants to get ahead of the reader’s skepticism. But there’s also plenty of perceptive lines in the poems themselves: “You dreamt you wrote something so good, / so ambivalent and destructive, so creative, / so lacking in morals, decency, or instruction, / so sad and so funny, / so useless and old, / so familiar and new, / so full of theft and power / that they had to name a god after it.” I ask him if good writing is necessarily amoral. He says, “Probably. Which is why any politically correct work of art is usually super successful and really bad. Usually artists are difficult people, and I have no problem separating the art from the artist. But people do now.”

In college, Duchovny wanted to be a poet. “I thought it was an actual occupation you could have,” he says. When an underclassman turned up in his workshop who was better than him, he quit writing poems on the spot. “It was actually Walter Kirn,” he says. “He showed up at 16-years-old. He was a genius. The two men have become close in the last decade. Kirn, who wrote Up in the Air and founded the newspaper County Highway, tells me what Duchovny was like at Princeton: “He was golden. He had an aura. I was a little starstruck by him.” Duchovny has agreed to play paranormal radio host Art Bell in American Nights, a biopic that Kirn is developing alongside director Alex Lee Moyer. Bell’s Coast to Coast, a cult AM show during the ’80s and ’90s, was beloved by long-haul truckers and compound preppers alike, who called in to report UFO sightings, cattle mutilations, and crop circles. “I, like the rest of my generation, grew up on The X-Files,” Moyer tells me. “It made a massive impression on me, and I’ve been a fan of David ever since. The synchronicity of him being a part of this is not lost on me.”
I ask Duchovny if he always needed to be the best. “I at least needed to be the best in my class,” he says.

In LA, I meet Duchovny in a quiet restaurant to talk about his books. He describes his first novel as “an act of cowardice.” Holy Cow is narrated by an anthropomorphized barnyard animal who uncovers the conspiracy theory that is factory farming. “I thought: Well, they’re not gonna cut me off at the knees on this. Because I’m clearly not that serious. It was calculated. I didn’t want to try for the great American novel the first time as an actor.” The books that followed are more ambitious, each one better than the last. By the time he was promoting his fourth book, 2021’s Truly Like Lightning, he made his ambition plain. “I want to be taken seriously,” he said on Marc Maron’s podcast. “That’s my weakness. I want that book to be taken seriously.”
“You don’t want people to be like the guy from The X-Files wrote a book,” Maron said.
“That’s what they’re gonna say,” Duchovny said, “but I hope and I believe that eventually people will see that I mean business.”

Truly Like Lightning centers on a Mormon polygamist family forced to enter the godless world of Los Angeles when their homestead is upended. “When I started to read about Mormonism, it struck me as super optimistic. Everyone’s gonna get their own planet and everyone’s gonna be able to propagate souls. As opposed to a European perspective, which was always about the end of something, being 2,000 years removed from this thing. The Mormons said no, this is still happening.” The novel takes cues from the literary critic Harold Bloom, who wrote that Mormonism was an “American original” and called its founder a “religious genius.” Duchovny studied under Bloom at Yale, where he earned some of an English PhD. “Everything goes back to Bloom,” he says. “And you never really leave grad school. I’m not sure I’ve left grad school. They might still be waiting for my dissertation.”

But Duchovny did leave grad school. He signed with a talent agent one summer to try to earn some money acting in commercials. His agent told him that if he wanted to go out for theater or film roles, he’d have to get into an acting class. “I said: I’m not doing anything. When I stepped into acting class, something happened. I wasn’t a demonstrative person—I was an intellectual person. So it was like: Yeah, be unreasonable. Be irrational. It opened up a different world, a world of fiction, a world without consequences. I’m doing a scene, and I’m yelling at this person and I’m going to murder them, but I don’t have to go to jail.”

For someone with half a dozen good books and an enormous public profile, it’s surprising there haven’t been more reviews. Johnny Temple, who published Duchovny’s two most recent books on Akashic, tells me, “It’s certainly frustrating that there hasn't been more review coverage of David’s books. For any well-known actor, musician, or other type of public figure, there’s always going to be obstacles to being taken seriously in a different medium.” Kirn tells me, “That makes writing fiction a much purer achievement in my mind. You’re doing this because you love it, and you know that two thirds of your fans will only remember you as a TV character. It’s a brilliant, Sisyphean task. Also, he’s a superb writer.”

I ask Duchovny whether he still thinks about being the best. “I think now I can acknowledge that it’s a hollow designation,” he says. “Especially in the arts. Even though we give awards, which is silly. Holy Cow made the Timesbestseller list. Ever since, everything I write sells less and less.”

“It’s hard for someone to champion it,” he adds. “If I wrote a memoir, I’m sure it would get reviewed in the Times.”
Talking to Duchovny, one is reminded that wanting to be taken seriously and being in on the joke aren’t mutually exclusive. As band practice winds down in Brooklyn, the guys are excited to cover Lou Reed’s “Perfect Day.” Duchovny crosses his arms in front of his lap like a schoolboy as he sings. To my ear it sounds just fine, but Lee, the keyboardist, asks the mixer to lower the reverb on David’s voice.

“Maybe lower David’s mic in general?” the bassist, Mitchell Stewart asks.
“Thanks, guys,” Duchovny says.
“Lower it to zero,” Lee says.
“Lower than zero,” Duchovny says. “Less than zero.”
A few days later, he texts me. He just screened an early cut of Soapbox, a Hollywood satire he wrote and stars in opposite Laverne Cox. At first, he’s bummed that the test audience has decided that his character shouldn’t get killed in the final moments of the movie. But a couple hours later, he writes me again: “People don’t want me to die. I guess I should be flattered.”

🗞️ 新大卫·杜楚尼专访：

现在每个人都卖光了——除了大卫·杜楚尼 (GQ)
在过去的十年里，这位《X档案》明星一直在默默地创作出优秀的小说、诗歌和摇滚专辑。可惜他无法忍受推销它们。

2026 年 11 月 16 日
作者：阿尼卡·杰德·利维

自从我还活着的时候，大卫·杜楚尼就已经出名了。从 1993 年到 2002 年，《X 档案》使政府阴谋成为黄金时段电视的主要内容。杜楚尼饰演的联邦调查局特工福克斯·穆德（Fox Mulder）和持怀疑态度的对手吉莲·安德森（Gillian Anderson）饰演的特工达纳·斯卡利（Dana Scully）象征着下个世纪共识现实即将崩溃，将偏执狂带入了 2000 万个美国客厅。这部剧属于一个不再存在的单一文化世界，它将杜楚尼带入了一个现在很难想象的可见度领域，当时名人是以工业化速度生产和消费的。几周前，当我的男朋友在布鲁克林的 Crowley Vintage 购买西装外套时，我在手机上编辑了这个故事，我看到一个大学年龄的男孩穿上一件长长的灰色风衣并向他的女朋友宣布：“Mulder 模式。”

杜楚尼随后主演了《加州狂潮》，这是一部粗俗的喜剧，讲述了一位离婚小说家在 2000 年代好莱坞电影制片厂系统中的性和职业寄生的故事。尽管杜楚尼并未为本剧编剧，但许多观众将《加州狂情》解读为一种自传小说。这位演员写过多部小说，但任何与他相处过 30 秒的人都会明显看出，这位说话轻声细语、不情愿的名人与汉克·穆迪这个角色毫无关系。尽管如此，《加州狂潮》确实预见到了一些关于艺术、名人和自我商品化的事情：今天任何写作的人都必须努力向通常不读书的公众推销艺术形象。

除了六本书外，杜楚尼还发行了四张唱片，并编写和导演了多部故事片。他以一种迷人的严谨和自嘲的方式迎接美国艺术的堕落状态。 “我不是乔纳森·弗兰岑，”他谈到自己的小说创作过程时说道。 “但如果我每天都致力于某件事，它就会加深。最终，希望我能达到乔纳森·弗兰岑所取得的成就的十分之一。”但他厌恶那种可能会让他的各种艺术事业更有利可图的宣传。他告诉我他发现这“精神上贫乏”。

我在卡罗尔花园的练习场见到了杜楚尼和他的乐队——年龄只有他一半的千禧一代懒鬼，他们正准备在那里巡演他们的第四张唱片《Pieces》。他穿着一件白色的 Hanes T 恤，紧贴在他运动型的手臂下，脚踝上有一个指向西方的指南针纹身，这是他在女儿 West 婴儿时期住院时得到的纹身。 （她现在 27 岁，是一位颇有成就的演员。“她想成为一名医生，”他说。“当她告诉我她要从事演艺事业时，我很高兴。感谢上帝。”）

这些专辑由柔和、易于聆听的民谣摇滚曲目组成，与早期的 Kurt Vile 没有什么不同。这是乐队多年来的第一次排练，也是他们为欧洲巡演做准备的唯一机会之一。亲自演奏时，他们会更加用力、更重地演奏歌曲，并穿插一些讨人喜欢的翻唱：Blue Öyster Cult 的《Godzilla》、REM 的《The One I Love》，以及——“遗憾的是只有一次，”杜楚尼说——《Hotline Bling》。房间里的能量很高。这些男人彼此喜欢。杜楚尼的经理从我所在的冷藏箱里给了我一杯啤酒。我指着钱包里的高个子男孩。他看起来很失望。 “你不信任我们，”他说。杜楚尼走到一边喝了一口水，然后拿起麦克风。
“你可以跟着唱，”他的键盘手科林·李说。
“我可以跟着唱吗？”杜楚夫尼问道。

66 岁的大卫·杜楚尼 (David Duchovny) 仍然是性感的象征。他的状态比《X档案》中的状态要好。他的身体状况比乐队里的男孩们都要好。训练结束后的那天晚上，在他 2023 年电影《逆转诅咒》放映的问答环节中，他提到服装部门必须为他制作一条“BDSM 吊带”，让他穿在衣服下面，以提醒他像老人一样弯腰驼背。他扮演一名红袜队球迷，与关系疏远的儿子通过棒球、大麻以及对年轻美丽的死亡导乐的共同渴望而结下不解之缘。杜楚尼饰演的角色患有晚期癌症。 “我正处于垂死的时代，”他告诉人群。 “我在每部电影中都会死去。”

大多数情况下，威彻斯特县欧文顿剧院的观众年龄都足以观看《X档案》的播出。至少有两个看上去深奥的老人拿着大卫的诗集，就像一本祈祷书一样。有几个年轻人。一名戴着 KN95 口罩的大学女孩举手询问《Bucking Fucking Dent》，这是杜楚尼在电影制作炼狱期间撰写的《逆转诅咒》剧本的小说改编作品。 “在书中，泰德和马蒂的姓氏是Fullilove。在电影中你将其改为Fullaker。你为什么这么做？”
“好问题，”杜楚尼停顿了一下说道。 “充满爱。充满狗屎。都一样。”

不可避免地，有人询问新的 X 档案。瑞恩·库格勒正在为 Hulu 重新启动该剧。杜楚尼后来向我建议，该剧的原著编剧克里斯·卡特已经设计了自己的重启计划——“他有计划，并且想以原剧结束。”至于库格勒的版本，他说：“我知道他说他想让我来做点什么，但我们还没有弄清楚做什么。”在观众问答环节，杜楚尼似乎听错了问题，并破坏了他即将上映的台湾犯罪电影《流放者》的结局：“我也死在那部里。”

杜楚尼的最新著作《关于时间》是阿卡什去年出版的诗集，主要也是关于死亡的：他父亲的去世，他第一次婚姻的去世，以及本世纪初弥漫在空气中的死亡氛围。当他的治疗师鼓励他与死人交谈时，他开始写这些诗。 “他谈论的是鲁道夫·施泰纳的信念，即你可以与死者交谈。他说：你可以与你的父亲交谈，你应该这样做。我父亲和我并没有像我们应该有的那样联系，”杜楚尼说。 “当你年轻的时候，你认为你有足够的时间来获得你想要的关系。但这种关系并没有结束。”在谈话中，他很理智，但并不令人讨厌。 “当你读一本真正好的小说时，就会发生权力斗争，”他说。 “有人的思想正在接管你的思想。我经常思考语言，以及我们如何理所当然地认为它是一个准确的能指。当我年轻的时候，我认为沟通是可能的。现在我不太确定了。但尝试很有趣。”

杜楚尼的谦逊使他的公众形象中仍然存在的性魅力变得更加复杂。他对《关于时间》的介绍是这样开始的：“我知道你在想什么：这正是世界现在所需要的——来自演员的一堆诗。”有一种感觉，他想超越读者的怀疑。但诗本身也有很多富有洞察力的诗句：“你梦想你写了一些如此好的东西，/如此矛盾和破坏性，如此有创造力，/如此缺乏道德、正派或指导，/如此悲伤又如此有趣，/如此无用和陈旧，/如此熟悉和新奇，/如此充满盗窃和力量/以至于他们不得不以它命名一个神。”我问他，好的写作是否一定是不道德的。他说：“可能吧。这就是为什么任何政治正确的艺术作品通常都超级成功，但也很糟糕。通常艺术家都是很难相处的人，我毫不犹豫地将艺术与艺术家分开。但现在人们这样做了。”

在大学时，杜楚尼想成为一名诗人。 “我认为这是一个你可以从事的实际职业，”他说。当他的工作室里出现了一个比他更优秀的低年级学生时，他当场不再写诗了。 “这实际上是沃尔特·基恩，”他说。 “他 16 岁就出现了。他是个天才。我当时想，好吧——我不是诗人。”

过去十年里，这两个人的关系越来越亲密。基恩是《在空中》的作者，也是《乡村公路》报纸的创办人，他告诉我杜楚尼在普林斯顿大学时的样子：“他是金色的。他有一种光环。我有点被他迷住了。”杜楚尼已同意在基恩与导演亚历克斯·李·莫耶共同制作的传记片《美国之夜》中扮演超自然电台主持人阿特·贝尔。贝尔的《从海岸到海岸》是 80 年代和 90 年代备受喜爱的 AM 节目，深受长途卡车司机和复合型末日准备者之类的喜爱，他们打电话报告 UFO 目击事件、牛被残害和麦田怪圈。 “我和我这一代人一样，都是看着《X 档案》长大的，”莫耶告诉我。 “这给我留下了深刻的印象，从那时起我就成了大卫的粉丝。我并没有忘记他参与其中的同步性。”
我问杜楚尼是否总是需要成为最好的。 “我至少需要成为班上最好的，”他说。

在洛杉矶，我在一家安静的餐厅见到了杜楚尼，谈论他的书。他将自己的第一部小说描述为“一种懦弱的行为”。 《圣牛》由拟人化的稗子动物讲述，它揭开了工厂化农业的阴谋论。 “我想：好吧，他们不会在这件事上把我打断。因为我显然没那么认真。这是经过算计的。我不想第一次以演员的身份尝试这部伟大的美国小说。”接下来的书更加雄心勃勃，每一本都比上一本更好。当他宣传他的第四本书《2021 年的《真如闪电》》时，他明确了自己的雄心壮志。 “我希望被认真对待，”他在马克·马龙的播客上说道。 “这是我的弱点。我希望人们认真对待这本书。”
“你不希望人们像《X档案》中写书的人一样，”马龙说。
“他们会这么说，”杜楚尼说，“但我希望并且相信人们最终会明白我是认真的。”

《真实如闪电》讲述了一个摩门教一夫多妻家庭的故事，当他们的家园被颠覆时，他们被迫进入洛杉矶的无神世界。 “当我开始阅读有关摩门教的内容时，我感到非常乐观。每个人都会拥有自己的星球，每个人都能够传播灵魂。与欧洲的观点相反，欧洲人的观点总是关于某件事的终结，与这件事相距 2000 年。摩门教徒说不，这种情况仍在发生。”这部小说受到文学评论家哈罗德·布鲁姆的启发，他写道摩门教是“美国原创”，并称其创始人是“宗教天才”。杜楚尼在耶鲁大学师从布鲁姆，并在那里获得了一些英语博士学位。 “一切都可以追溯到布鲁姆，”他说。 “而且你永远不会真正离开研究生院。我不确定我是否已经离开研究生院。他们可能仍在等待我的论文。”

但杜楚尼确实离开了研究生院。有一年夏天，他与一位人才经纪人签约，试图靠拍广告赚点钱。他的经纪人告诉他，如果他想出演戏剧或电影角色，他就必须参加表演课程。 “我说：我什么也没做。当我进入表演课时，发生了一些事情。我不是一个外向的人，我是一个知识分子。所以这就像是：是的，不讲道理。不理性。它打开了一个不同的世界，一个虚构的世界，一个没有后果的世界。我正在拍一个场景，我对这个人大喊大叫，我要谋杀他们，但我不必进监狱。”

对于一个拥有六本好书和巨大公众形象的人来说，令人惊讶的是没有更多的评论。约翰尼·坦普尔（Johnny Temple）出版了杜楚尼最近两本关于阿卡什的书，他告诉我，“没有更多关于大卫的书的评论报道，这确实令人沮丧。对于任何知名演员、音乐家或其他类型的公众人物来说，在不同的媒体中受到认真对待总是会遇到障碍。”基恩告诉我，“这使得写小说在我心目中成为一种更加纯粹的成就。你这样做是因为你喜欢它，而且你知道三分之二的粉丝只会记住你作为一个电视角色。这是一项出色的、西西弗斯式的任务。而且，他是一位出色的作家。”

我问杜楚尼是否仍然想成为最好的。 “我想现在我可以承认这是一个空洞的称号，”他说。 “尤其是在艺术领域。即使我们颁发奖项，这也是愚蠢的。《Holy Cow》登上了《泰晤士报》畅销书排行榜。从那以后，我写的所有东西的销量都越来越少。”

“很难有人去支持它，”他补充道。 “如果我写一本回忆录，我确信《泰晤士报》会对其进行评论。”
与杜楚尼交谈时，人们会想起想要被认真对待和开开玩笑并不相互排斥。随着布鲁克林的乐队排练接近尾声，伙计们很高兴能翻唱卢·里德 (Lou Reed) 的《完美的一天》(Perfect Day)。杜楚尼唱歌时像个小学生一样双臂交叉在腿前。在我看来，这听起来不错，但键盘手李要求混音器降低大卫声音的混响。

“也许把大卫的麦克风调低一点？”贝斯手，米切尔·斯图尔特问道。
“谢谢，伙计们，”杜楚尼说。
“将其降低到零，”李说。
“低于零，”杜楚尼说。 “小于零。”
几天后，他给我发短信。他刚刚放映了《肥皂盒》的早期剪辑版，这是一部由他撰写并与拉弗恩·考克斯演对手戏的好莱坞讽刺剧。起初，他对测试观众决定他的角色不应该在电影的最后时刻被杀感到沮丧。但几个小时后，他再次给我写信：“人们不想让我死。我想我应该感到受宠若惊。”

🗞️ NEW DAVID DUCHOVNY INTERVIEW:

Everyone's a Sellout Now—Except for David Duchovny (GQ)
For the last decade, The X-Files star has been quietly churning out excellent novels, poetry, and rock albums. Too bad he can’t stand to promote them.

November 16, 2026
By Anika Jade Levy

David Duchovny has been famous for as long as I have been alive. From 1993 to 2002, The X-Files made government conspiracies a staple of primetime television. Duchovny’s FBI special agent Fox Mulder, with his skeptical counterpart, Gillian Anderson’s agent Dana Scully, personified the imminent breakdown of consensus reality in the coming century, delivering the paranoid fringe into 20 million American living rooms. The show belongs to a world of monoculture that no longer exists, and it launched Duchovny into a realm of visibility that’s hard to imagine now, when famous people are produced and consumed at an industrial rate. A few weeks ago, as my boyfriend shopped for a suit jacket at Crowley Vintage in Brooklyn and I edited this story on my phone, I watched a college-age boy put on a long, gray trench coat and announce to his girlfriend: “Mulder mode.”

Duchovny went on to star in Californication, a raunchy dramedy about a divorced novelist navigating the sexually and professionally parasitic Hollywood studio system of the 2000s. Many viewers interpreted Californication as a kind of autofiction, although Duchovny did not write for the show. The actor has written a number of novels, but it’s apparent to anyone who has spent 30 seconds with him that this soft-spoken, reluctant celebrity has nothing to do with the character Hank Moody. Still, Californication did anticipate something about art, celebrity, and self-commodification: Anybody who writes today must contend with marketing an artistic persona for a public that does not, as a rule, read.

In addition to his six books, Duchovny has released four records, and written and directed a number of feature films. He greets the degraded state of American arts with a charming blend of rigor and self-deprecation. “I’m not Jonathan Franzen,” he says of his fiction-writing process. “But if I work on something every day, it deepens. And eventually, hopefully, I can achieve one tenth of what Jonathan Franzen achieves.” But he has an aversion to the sort of publicity that might make his various artistic ventures more lucrative. He tells me he finds it “spiritually impoverishing.”

I meet Duchovny with his band—millennial slackers half his age—at their practice space in Carroll Gardens, where they’re preparing to tour their fourth LP, Prince of Pieces. He wears a white Hanes T-shirt, tight underneath his athletic arms, and he has a tattoo on his ankle—a compass pointing west, something he got when his daughter, West, was hospitalized as an infant. (She’s 27 now, an accomplished actor. “She wanted to be a doctor,” he says. “I was so happy when she told me she was going to pursue acting. Thank God.”)

The albums are composed of subdued, easy-to-listen-to folk-rock tracks, not dissimilar from early Kurt Vile. It’s the band’s first rehearsal in ages, and one of their only chances to prepare in advance of a European tour. In person, they play the songs harder and heavier, sprinkling in crowd-pleasing covers: “Godzilla” by Blue Öyster Cult, “The One I Love” by REM, and—“sadly only one time,” Duchovny says—“Hotline Bling.” The energy in the room is high. These men like one another. Duchovny’s manager offers me a beer from the cooler I’m perched on. I gesture to the tallboy in my purse. He looks disappointed. “You didn’t trust us,” he says. Duchovny steps aside to take a sip of water and picks up the microphone.
“You can sing along,” his keyboardist, Colin Lee, says.
“I can sing along?” Duchovny asks.

At 66, David Duchovny remains a sex symbol. He’s in better shape than he was on The X-Files. He’s in better shape than the boys in the band. The night after practice, during a Q&A for a screening of his 2023 film Reverse the Curse, he mentions that the wardrobe department had to fashion a “BDSM harness” for him to wear under his clothes to remind him to hunch like an old man. He plays a Red Sox fan who bonds with his estranged son over baseball, marijuana, and their shared lust for a beautiful, young death doula. Duchovny’s character has terminal cancer. “I’m in my dying era,” he tells the crowd. “I die in every film. ”

For the most part, the audience at Westchester County’s Irvington Theater is old enough to have watched The X-Files as it aired. At least two esoteric-looking old men carry David’s poetry collection like a prayer book. There are a handful of young people. A college-aged girl in a KN95 mask raises her hand to ask about Bucking Fucking Dent, the novel adaptation of the Reverse the Curse screenplay, which Duchovny wrote while the movie was in production purgatory. “In the book, Ted and Marty’s last name is Fullilove. In the movie you change it to Fullaker. Why did you do that?”
“Good question,” Duchovny says, stalling. “Full of love. Full of shit. It’s all the same.”

Inevitably, someone asks about the new X-Files. Ryan Coogler is rebooting the show for Hulu. Duchovny will later suggest to me that Chris Carter, the show’s original writer, has designs on a reboot of his own—“He has plans, and wants to end with the original show.” As for Coogler’s version, he says, “I know he said he wants me to come do something, but we haven’t figured out what yet.” During the audience Q&A, Duchovny seems to have misheard the question, and spoils the ending for The Exiles, his forthcoming Taiwanese crime film: “I die in that one too.”

Duchovny’s latest book, About Time, a collection of poems published last year by Akashic, is also largely about dying: the death of his father, the death of his first marriage, the ambient death that hung in the air at the beginning of the decade. He started writing the poems when his therapist encouraged him to talk to dead people. “He was talking about Rudolph Steiner’s belief that you can talk to the dead. And he said: You can talk to your father and you should. My dad and I didn’t connect like we might have,” Duchovny says. “When you’re younger, you think you have all the time in the world to get the relationship you want. But the relationship doesn’t end.” In conversation, he is cerebral without being annoying. “There’s a power struggle when you read a really good novel,” he says. “Somebody’s mind is taking over your mind. I think about language a lot and how we take it for granted as being an accurate signifier. When I was younger I thought communication was possible. I’m not so sure now. But it’s fun to try.”

Duchovny’s humility complicates the sexual charisma that still lives at the center of his public persona. His introduction to About Time begins, “I know what you’re thinking: Just what the world needs now—a bunch of poems from an actor.” There’s a sense that he wants to get ahead of the reader’s skepticism. But there’s also plenty of perceptive lines in the poems themselves: “You dreamt you wrote something so good, / so ambivalent and destructive, so creative, / so lacking in morals, decency, or instruction, / so sad and so funny, / so useless and old, / so familiar and new, / so full of theft and power / that they had to name a god after it.” I ask him if good writing is necessarily amoral. He says, “Probably. Which is why any politically correct work of art is usually super successful and really bad. Usually artists are difficult people, and I have no problem separating the art from the artist. But people do now.”

In college, Duchovny wanted to be a poet. “I thought it was an actual occupation you could have,” he says. When an underclassman turned up in his workshop who was better than him, he quit writing poems on the spot. “It was actually Walter Kirn,” he says. “He showed up at 16-years-old. He was a genius. I was like okay—I’m not a poet.”

The two men have become close in the last decade. Kirn, who wrote Up in the Air and founded the newspaper County Highway, tells me what Duchovny was like at Princeton: “He was golden. He had an aura. I was a little starstruck by him.” Duchovny has agreed to play paranormal radio host Art Bell in American Nights, a biopic that Kirn is developing alongside director Alex Lee Moyer. Bell’s Coast to Coast, a cult AM show during the ’80s and ’90s, was beloved by long-haul truckers and compound preppers alike, who called in to report UFO sightings, cattle mutilations, and crop circles. “I, like the rest of my generation, grew up on The X-Files,” Moyer tells me. “It made a massive impression on me, and I’ve been a fan of David ever since. The synchronicity of him being a part of this is not lost on me.”
I ask Duchovny if he always needed to be the best. “I at least needed to be the best in my class,” he says.

In LA, I meet Duchovny in a quiet restaurant to talk about his books. He describes his first novel as “an act of cowardice.” Holy Cow is narrated by an anthropomorphized barnyard animal who uncovers the conspiracy theory that is factory farming. “I thought: Well, they’re not gonna cut me off at the knees on this. Because I’m clearly not that serious. It was calculated. I didn’t want to try for the great American novel the first time as an actor.” The books that followed are more ambitious, each one better than the last. By the time he was promoting his fourth book, 2021’s Truly Like Lightning, he made his ambition plain. “I want to be taken seriously,” he said on Marc Maron’s podcast. “That’s my weakness. I want that book to be taken seriously.”
“You don’t want people to be like the guy from The X-Files wrote a book,” Maron said.
“That’s what they’re gonna say,” Duchovny said, “but I hope and I believe that eventually people will see that I mean business.”

Truly Like Lightning centers on a Mormon polygamist family forced to enter the godless world of Los Angeles when their homestead is upended. “When I started to read about Mormonism, it struck me as super optimistic. Everyone’s gonna get their own planet and everyone’s gonna be able to propagate souls. As opposed to a European perspective, which was always about the end of something, being 2,000 years removed from this thing. The Mormons said no, this is still happening.” The novel takes cues from the literary critic Harold Bloom, who wrote that Mormonism was an “American original” and called its founder a “religious genius.” Duchovny studied under Bloom at Yale, where he earned some of an English PhD. “Everything goes back to Bloom,” he says. “And you never really leave grad school. I’m not sure I’ve left grad school. They might still be waiting for my dissertation.”

But Duchovny did leave grad school. He signed with a talent agent one summer to try to earn some money acting in commercials. His agent told him that if he wanted to go out for theater or film roles, he’d have to get into an acting class. “I said: I’m not doing anything. When I stepped into acting class, something happened. I wasn’t a demonstrative person—I was an intellectual person. So it was like: Yeah, be unreasonable. Be irrational. It opened up a different world, a world of fiction, a world without consequences. I’m doing a scene, and I’m yelling at this person and I’m going to murder them, but I don’t have to go to jail.”

For someone with half a dozen good books and an enormous public profile, it’s surprising there haven’t been more reviews. Johnny Temple, who published Duchovny’s two most recent books on Akashic, tells me, “It’s certainly frustrating that there hasn't been more review coverage of David’s books. For any well-known actor, musician, or other type of public figure, there’s always going to be obstacles to being taken seriously in a different medium.” Kirn tells me, “That makes writing fiction a much purer achievement in my mind. You’re doing this because you love it, and you know that two thirds of your fans will only remember you as a TV character. It’s a brilliant, Sisyphean task. Also, he’s a superb writer.”

I ask Duchovny whether he still thinks about being the best. “I think now I can acknowledge that it’s a hollow designation,” he says. “Especially in the arts. Even though we give awards, which is silly. Holy Cow made the Timesbestseller list. Ever since, everything I write sells less and less.”

“It’s hard for someone to champion it,” he adds. “If I wrote a memoir, I’m sure it would get reviewed in the Times.”
Talking to Duchovny, one is reminded that wanting to be taken seriously and being in on the joke aren’t mutually exclusive. As band practice winds down in Brooklyn, the guys are excited to cover Lou Reed’s “Perfect Day.” Duchovny crosses his arms in front of his lap like a schoolboy as he sings. To my ear it sounds just fine, but Lee, the keyboardist, asks the mixer to lower the reverb on David’s voice.

“Maybe lower David’s mic in general?” the bassist, Mitchell Stewart asks.
“Thanks, guys,” Duchovny says.
“Lower it to zero,” Lee says.
“Lower than zero,” Duchovny says. “Less than zero.”
A few days later, he texts me. He just screened an early cut of Soapbox, a Hollywood satire he wrote and stars in opposite Laverne Cox. At first, he’s bummed that the test audience has decided that his character shouldn’t get killed in the final moments of the movie. But a couple hours later, he writes me again: “People don’t want me to die. I guess I should be flattered.”

🗞️ 新大卫·杜楚尼专访：

现在每个人都卖光了——除了大卫·杜楚尼 (GQ)
在过去的十年里，这位《X档案》明星一直在默默地创作出优秀的小说、诗歌和摇滚专辑。可惜他无法忍受推销它们。

2026 年 11 月 16 日
作者：阿尼卡·杰德·利维

自从我还活着的时候，大卫·杜楚尼就已经出名了。从 1993 年到 2002 年，《X 档案》使政府阴谋成为黄金时段电视的主要内容。杜楚尼饰演的联邦调查局特工福克斯·穆德（Fox Mulder）和持怀疑态度的对手吉莲·安德森（Gillian Anderson）饰演的特工达纳·斯卡利（Dana Scully）象征着下个世纪共识现实即将崩溃，将偏执狂带入了 2000 万个美国客厅。这部剧属于一个不再存在的单一文化世界，它将杜楚尼带入了一个现在很难想象的可见度领域，当时名人是以工业化速度生产和消费的。几周前，当我的男朋友在布鲁克林的 Crowley Vintage 购买西装外套时，我在手机上编辑了这个故事，我看到一个大学年龄的男孩穿上一件长长的灰色风衣并向他的女朋友宣布：“Mulder 模式。”

杜楚尼随后主演了《加州狂潮》，这是一部粗俗的喜剧，讲述了一位离婚小说家在 2000 年代好莱坞电影制片厂系统中的性和职业寄生的故事。尽管杜楚尼并未为本剧编剧，但许多观众将《加州狂情》解读为一种自传小说。这位演员写过多部小说，但任何与他相处过 30 秒的人都会明显看出，这位说话轻声细语、不情愿的名人与汉克·穆迪这个角色毫无关系。尽管如此，《加州狂潮》确实预见到了一些关于艺术、名人和自我商品化的事情：今天任何写作的人都必须努力向通常不读书的公众推销艺术形象。

除了六本书外，杜楚尼还发行了四张唱片，并编写和导演了多部故事片。他以一种迷人的严谨和自嘲的方式迎接美国艺术的堕落状态。 “我不是乔纳森·弗兰岑，”他谈到自己的小说创作过程时说道。 “但如果我每天都致力于某件事，它就会加深。最终，希望我能达到乔纳森·弗兰岑所取得的成就的十分之一。”但他厌恶那种可能会让他的各种艺术事业更有利可图的宣传。他告诉我他发现这“精神上贫乏”。

我在卡罗尔花园的练习场见到了杜楚尼和他的乐队——年龄只有他一半的千禧一代懒鬼，他们正准备在那里巡演他们的第四张唱片《Pieces》。他穿着一件白色的 Hanes T 恤，紧贴在他运动型的手臂下，脚踝上有一个指向西方的指南针纹身，这是他在女儿 West 婴儿时期住院时得到的纹身。 （她现在 27 岁，是一位颇有成就的演员。“她想成为一名医生，”他说。“当她告诉我她要从事演艺事业时，我很高兴。感谢上帝。”）

这些专辑由柔和、易于聆听的民谣摇滚曲目组成，与早期的 Kurt Vile 没有什么不同。这是乐队多年来的第一次排练，也是他们为欧洲巡演做准备的唯一机会之一。亲自演奏时，他们会更加用力、更重地演奏歌曲，并穿插一些讨人喜欢的翻唱：Blue Öyster Cult 的《Godzilla》、REM 的《The One I Love》，以及——“遗憾的是只有一次，”杜楚尼说——《Hotline Bling》。房间里的能量很高。这些男人彼此喜欢。杜楚尼的经理从我所在的冷藏箱里给了我一杯啤酒。我指着钱包里的高个子男孩。他看起来很失望。 “你不信任我们，”他说。杜楚尼走到一边喝了一口水，然后拿起麦克风。
“你可以跟着唱，”他的键盘手科林·李说。
“我可以跟着唱吗？”杜楚夫尼问道。

66 岁的大卫·杜楚尼 (David Duchovny) 仍然是性感的象征。他的状态比《X档案》中的状态要好。他的身体状况比乐队里的男孩们都要好。训练结束后的那天晚上，在他 2023 年电影《逆转诅咒》放映的问答环节中，他提到服装部门必须为他制作一条“BDSM 吊带”，让他穿在衣服下面，以提醒他像老人一样弯腰驼背。他扮演一名红袜队球迷，与关系疏远的儿子通过棒球、大麻以及对年轻美丽的死亡导乐的共同渴望而结下不解之缘。杜楚尼饰演的角色患有晚期癌症。 “我正处于垂死的时代，”他告诉人群。 “我在每部电影中都会死去。”

大多数情况下，威彻斯特县欧文顿剧院的观众年龄都足以观看《X档案》的播出。至少有两个看上去深奥的老人拿着大卫的诗集，就像一本祈祷书一样。有几个年轻人。一名戴着 KN95 口罩的大学女孩举手询问《Bucking Fucking Dent》，这是杜楚尼在电影制作炼狱期间撰写的《逆转诅咒》剧本的小说改编作品。 “在书中，泰德和马蒂的姓氏是Fullilove。在电影中你将其改为Fullaker。你为什么这么做？”
“好问题，”杜楚尼停顿了一下说道。 “充满爱。充满狗屎。都一样。”

不可避免地，有人询问新的 X 档案。瑞恩·库格勒正在为 Hulu 重新启动该剧。杜楚尼后来向我建议，该剧的原著编剧克里斯·卡特已经设计了自己的重启计划——“他有计划，并且想以原剧结束。”至于库格勒的版本，他说：“我知道他说他想让我来做点什么，但我们还没有弄清楚做什么。”在观众问答环节，杜楚尼似乎听错了问题，并破坏了他即将上映的台湾犯罪电影《流放者》的结局：“我也死在那部里。”

杜楚尼的最新著作《关于时间》是阿卡什去年出版的诗集，主要也是关于死亡的：他父亲的去世，他第一次婚姻的去世，以及本世纪初弥漫在空气中的死亡氛围。当他的治疗师鼓励他与死人交谈时，他开始写这些诗。 “他谈论的是鲁道夫·施泰纳的信念，即你可以与死者交谈。他说：你可以与你的父亲交谈，你应该这样做。我父亲和我并没有像我们应该有的那样联系，”杜楚尼说。 “当你年轻的时候，你认为你有足够的时间来获得你想要的关系。但这种关系并没有结束。”在谈话中，他很理智，但并不令人讨厌。 “当你读一本真正好的小说时，就会发生权力斗争，”他说。 “有人的思想正在接管你的思想。我经常思考语言，以及我们如何理所当然地认为它是一个准确的能指。当我年轻的时候，我认为沟通是可能的。现在我不太确定了。但尝试很有趣。”

杜楚尼的谦逊使他的公众形象中仍然存在的性魅力变得更加复杂。他对《关于时间》的介绍是这样开始的：“我知道你在想什么：这正是世界现在所需要的——来自演员的一堆诗。”有一种感觉，他想超越读者的怀疑。但诗本身也有很多富有洞察力的诗句：“你梦想你写了一些如此好的东西，/如此矛盾和破坏性，如此有创造力，/如此缺乏道德、正派或指导，/如此悲伤又如此有趣，/如此无用和陈旧，/如此熟悉和新奇，/如此充满盗窃和力量/以至于他们不得不以它命名一个神。”我问他，好的写作是否一定是不道德的。他说：“可能吧。这就是为什么任何政治正确的艺术作品通常都超级成功，但也很糟糕。通常艺术家都是很难相处的人，我毫不犹豫地将艺术与艺术家分开。但现在人们这样做了。”

在大学时，杜楚尼想成为一名诗人。 “我认为这是一个你可以从事的实际职业，”他说。当他的工作室里出现了一个比他更优秀的低年级学生时，他当场不再写诗了。 “这实际上是沃尔特·基恩，”他说。 “他 16 岁就出现了。他是个天才。我当时想，好吧——我不是诗人。”

过去十年里，这两个人的关系越来越亲密。基恩是《在空中》的作者，也是《乡村公路》报纸的创办人，他告诉我杜楚尼在普林斯顿大学时的样子：“他是金色的。他有一种光环。我有点被他迷住了。”杜楚尼已同意在基恩与导演亚历克斯·李·莫耶共同制作的传记片《美国之夜》中扮演超自然电台主持人阿特·贝尔。贝尔的《从海岸到海岸》是 80 年代和 90 年代备受喜爱的 AM 节目，深受长途卡车司机和复合型末日准备者之类的喜爱，他们打电话报告 UFO 目击事件、牛被残害和麦田怪圈。 “我和我这一代人一样，都是看着《X 档案》长大的，”莫耶告诉我。 “这给我留下了深刻的印象，从那时起我就成了大卫的粉丝。我并没有忘记他参与其中的同步性。”
我问杜楚尼是否总是需要成为最好的。 “我至少需要成为班上最好的，”他说。

在洛杉矶，我在一家安静的餐厅见到了杜楚尼，谈论他的书。他将自己的第一部小说描述为“一种懦弱的行为”。 《圣牛》由拟人化的稗子动物讲述，它揭开了工厂化农业的阴谋论。 “我想：好吧，他们不会在这件事上把我打断。因为我显然没那么认真。这是经过算计的。我不想第一次以演员的身份尝试这部伟大的美国小说。”接下来的书更加雄心勃勃，每一本都比上一本更好。当他宣传他的第四本书《2021 年的《真如闪电》》时，他明确了自己的雄心壮志。 “我希望被认真对待，”他在马克·马龙的播客上说道。 “这是我的弱点。我希望人们认真对待这本书。”
“你不希望人们像《X档案》中写书的人一样，”马龙说。
“他们会这么说，”杜楚尼说，“但我希望并且相信人们最终会明白我是认真的。”

《真实如闪电》讲述了一个摩门教一夫多妻家庭的故事，当他们的家园被颠覆时，他们被迫进入洛杉矶的无神世界。 “当我开始阅读有关摩门教的内容时，我感到非常乐观。每个人都会拥有自己的星球，每个人都能够传播灵魂。与欧洲的观点相反，欧洲人的观点总是关于某件事的终结，与这件事相距 2000 年。摩门教徒说不，这种情况仍在发生。”这部小说受到文学评论家哈罗德·布鲁姆的启发，他写道摩门教是“美国原创”，并称其创始人是“宗教天才”。杜楚尼在耶鲁大学师从布鲁姆，并在那里获得了一些英语博士学位。 “一切都可以追溯到布鲁姆，”他说。 “而且你永远不会真正离开研究生院。我不确定我是否已经离开研究生院。他们可能仍在等待我的论文。”

但杜楚尼确实离开了研究生院。有一年夏天，他与一位人才经纪人签约，试图靠拍广告赚点钱。他的经纪人告诉他，如果他想出演戏剧或电影角色，他就必须参加表演课程。 “我说：我什么也没做。当我进入表演课时，发生了一些事情。我不是一个外向的人，我是一个知识分子。所以这就像是：是的，不讲道理。不理性。它打开了一个不同的世界，一个虚构的世界，一个没有后果的世界。我正在拍一个场景，我对这个人大喊大叫，我要谋杀他们，但我不必进监狱。”

对于一个拥有六本好书和巨大公众形象的人来说，令人惊讶的是没有更多的评论。约翰尼·坦普尔（Johnny Temple）出版了杜楚尼最近两本关于阿卡什的书，他告诉我，“没有更多关于大卫的书的评论报道，这确实令人沮丧。对于任何知名演员、音乐家或其他类型的公众人物来说，在不同的媒体中受到认真对待总是会遇到障碍。”基恩告诉我，“这使得写小说在我心目中成为一种更加纯粹的成就。你这样做是因为你喜欢它，而且你知道三分之二的粉丝只会记住你作为一个电视角色。这是一项出色的、西西弗斯式的任务。而且，他是一位出色的作家。”

我问杜楚尼是否仍然想成为最好的。 “我想现在我可以承认这是一个空洞的称号，”他说。 “尤其是在艺术领域。即使我们颁发奖项，这也是愚蠢的。《Holy Cow》登上了《泰晤士报》畅销书排行榜。从那以后，我写的所有东西的销量都越来越少。”

“很难有人去支持它，”他补充道。 “如果我写一本回忆录，我确信《泰晤士报》会对其进行评论。”
与杜楚尼交谈时，人们会想起想要被认真对待和开开玩笑并不相互排斥。随着布鲁克林的乐队排练接近尾声，伙计们很高兴能翻唱卢·里德 (Lou Reed) 的《完美的一天》(Perfect Day)。杜楚尼唱歌时像个小学生一样双臂交叉在腿前。在我看来，这听起来不错，但键盘手李要求混音器降低大卫声音的混响。

“也许把大卫的麦克风调低一点？”贝斯手，米切尔·斯图尔特问道。
“谢谢，伙计们，”杜楚尼说。
“将其降低到零，”李说。
“低于零，”杜楚尼说。 “小于零。”
几天后，他给我发短信。他刚刚放映了《肥皂盒》的早期剪辑版，这是一部由他撰写并与拉弗恩·考克斯演对手戏的好莱坞讽刺剧。起初，他对测试观众决定他的角色不应该在电影的最后时刻被杀感到沮丧。但几个小时后，他再次给我写信：“人们不想让我死。我想我应该感到受宠若惊。”

🗞️ NEW DAVID DUCHOVNY INTERVIEW:

Everyone's a Sellout Now—Except for David Duchovny (GQ)
For the last decade, The X-Files star has been quietly churning out excellent novels, poetry, and rock albums. Too bad he can’t stand to promote them.

November 16, 2026
By Anika Jade Levy

David Duchovny has been famous for as long as I have been alive. From 1993 to 2002, The X-Files made government conspiracies a staple of primetime television. Duchovny’s FBI special agent Fox Mulder, with his skeptical counterpart, Gillian Anderson’s agent Dana Scully, personified the imminent breakdown of consensus reality in the coming century, delivering the paranoid fringe into 20 million American living rooms. The show belongs to a world of monoculture that no longer exists, and it launched Duchovny into a realm of visibility that’s hard to imagine now, when famous people are produced and consumed at an industrial rate. Duchovny steps aside to take a sip of water and picks up the microphone.
“You can sing along,” his keyboardist, Colin Lee, says.
“I can sing along?” Duchovny asks.

“Good question,” Duchovny says, stalling. “Full of love. Full of shit. It’s all the same.”

自从我还活着的时候，大卫·杜楚尼就已经出名了。从 1993 年到 2002 年，《X 档案》使政府阴谋成为黄金时段电视的主要内容。杜楚尼饰演的联邦调查局特工福克斯·穆德（Fox Mulder）和持怀疑态度的对手吉莲·安德森（Gillian Anderson）饰演的特工达纳·斯卡利（Dana Scully）象征着下个世纪共识现实即将崩溃，将偏执狂带入了 2000 万个美国客厅。这部剧属于一个不再存在的单一文化世界，它将杜楚尼带入了一个现在很难想象的可见度领域，当时名人是以工业化速度生产和消费的。几周前，当我的男朋友在布鲁克林的 Crowley Vintage 购买西装外套时，我在手机上编辑了这个故事，我看到一个大学年龄的男孩穿上一件长长的灰色风衣并向他的女朋友宣布：“Mulder 模式。”

杜楚尼随后主演了《加州狂潮》，这是一部粗俗的喜剧，讲述了一位离婚小说家在 2000 年代好莱坞电影制片厂系统中的性和职业寄生的故事。尽管杜楚尼并未为本剧编剧，但许多观众将《加州狂情》解读为一种自传小说。这位演员写过多部小说，但任何与他相处过 30 秒的人都会明显看出，这位说话轻声细语、不情愿的名人与汉克·穆迪这个角色毫无关系。尽管如此，《加州狂潮》确实预见到了一些关于艺术、名人和自我商品化的事情：今天任何写作的人都必须努力向通常不读书的公众推销艺术形象。

除了六本书外，杜楚尼还发行了四张唱片，并编写和导演了多部故事片。他以一种迷人的严谨和自嘲的方式迎接美国艺术的堕落状态。 “我不是乔纳森·弗兰岑，”他谈到自己的小说创作过程时说道。 “但如果我每天都致力于某件事，它就会加深。最终，希望我能达到乔纳森·弗兰岑所取得的成就的十分之一。”但他厌恶那种可能会让他的各种艺术事业更有利可图的宣传。他告诉我他发现这“精神上贫乏”。

我在卡罗尔花园的练习场见到了杜楚尼和他的乐队——年龄只有他一半的千禧一代懒鬼，他们正准备在那里巡演他们的第四张唱片《Pieces》。他穿着一件白色的 Hanes T 恤，紧贴在他运动型的手臂下，脚踝上有一个指向西方的指南针纹身，这是他在女儿 West 婴儿时期住院时得到的纹身。 （她现在 27 岁，是一位颇有成就的演员。“她想成为一名医生，”他说。“当她告诉我她要从事演艺事业时，我很高兴。感谢上帝。”）

这些专辑由柔和、易于聆听的民谣摇滚曲目组成，与早期的 Kurt Vile 没有什么不同。这是乐队多年来的第一次排练，也是他们为欧洲巡演做准备的唯一机会之一。亲自演奏时，他们会更加用力、更重地演奏歌曲，并穿插一些讨人喜欢的翻唱：Blue Öyster Cult 的《Godzilla》、REM 的《The One I Love》，以及——“遗憾的是只有一次，”杜楚尼说——《Hotline Bling》。房间里的能量很高。这些男人彼此喜欢。杜楚尼的经理从我所在的冷藏箱里给了我一杯啤酒。我指着钱包里的高个子男孩。他看起来很失望。 “你不信任我们，”他说。杜楚尼走到一边喝了一口水，然后拿起麦克风。
“你可以跟着唱，”他的键盘手科林·李说。
“我可以跟着唱吗？”杜楚夫尼问道。

66 岁的大卫·杜楚尼 (David Duchovny) 仍然是性感的象征。他的状态比《X档案》中的状态要好。他的身体状况比乐队里的男孩们都要好。训练结束后的那天晚上，在他 2023 年电影《逆转诅咒》放映的问答环节中，他提到服装部门必须为他制作一条“BDSM 吊带”，让他穿在衣服下面，以提醒他像老人一样弯腰驼背。他扮演一名红袜队球迷，与关系疏远的儿子通过棒球、大麻以及对年轻美丽的死亡导乐的共同渴望而结下不解之缘。杜楚尼饰演的角色患有晚期癌症。 “我正处于垂死的时代，”他告诉人群。 “我在每部电影中都会死去。”

大多数情况下，威彻斯特县欧文顿剧院的观众年龄都足以观看《X档案》的播出。至少有两个看上去深奥的老人拿着大卫的诗集，就像一本祈祷书一样。有几个年轻人。一名戴着 KN95 口罩的大学女孩举手询问《Bucking Fucking Dent》，这是杜楚尼在电影制作炼狱期间撰写的《逆转诅咒》剧本的小说改编作品。 “在书中，泰德和马蒂的姓氏是Fullilove。在电影中你将其改为Fullaker。你为什么这么做？”
“好问题，”杜楚尼停顿了一下说道。 “充满爱。充满狗屎。都一样。”

不可避免地，有人询问新的 X 档案。瑞恩·库格勒正在为 Hulu 重新启动该剧。杜楚尼后来向我建议，该剧的原著编剧克里斯·卡特已经设计了自己的重启计划——“他有计划，并且想以原剧结束。”至于库格勒的版本，他说：“我知道他说他想让我来做点什么，但我们还没有弄清楚做什么。”在观众问答环节，杜楚尼似乎听错了问题，并破坏了他即将上映的台湾犯罪电影《流放者》的结局：“我也死在那部里。”

杜楚尼的最新著作《关于时间》是阿卡什去年出版的诗集，主要也是关于死亡的：他父亲的去世，他第一次婚姻的去世，以及本世纪初弥漫在空气中的死亡氛围。当他的治疗师鼓励他与死人交谈时，他开始写这些诗。 “他谈论的是鲁道夫·施泰纳的信念，即你可以与死者交谈。他说：你可以与你的父亲交谈，你应该这样做。我父亲和我并没有像我们应该有的那样联系，”杜楚尼说。 “当你年轻的时候，你认为你有足够的时间来获得你想要的关系。但这种关系并没有结束。”在谈话中，他很理智，但并不令人讨厌。 “当你读一本真正好的小说时，就会发生权力斗争，”他说。 “有人的思想正在接管你的思想。我经常思考语言，以及我们如何理所当然地认为它是一个准确的能指。当我年轻的时候，我认为沟通是可能的。现在我不太确定了。但尝试很有趣。”

杜楚尼的谦逊使他的公众形象中仍然存在的性魅力变得更加复杂。他对《关于时间》的介绍是这样开始的：“我知道你在想什么：这正是世界现在所需要的——来自演员的一堆诗。”有一种感觉，他想超越读者的怀疑。但诗本身也有很多富有洞察力的诗句：“你梦想你写了一些如此好的东西，/如此矛盾和破坏性，如此有创造力，/如此缺乏道德、正派或指导，/如此悲伤又如此有趣，/如此无用和陈旧，/如此熟悉和新奇，/如此充满盗窃和力量/以至于他们不得不以它命名一个神。”我问他，好的写作是否一定是不道德的。他说：“可能吧。这就是为什么任何政治正确的艺术作品通常都超级成功，但也很糟糕。通常艺术家都是很难相处的人，我毫不犹豫地将艺术与艺术家分开。但现在人们这样做了。”

在大学时，杜楚尼想成为一名诗人。 “我认为这是一个你可以从事的实际职业，”他说。当他的工作室里出现了一个比他更优秀的低年级学生时，他当场不再写诗了。 “这实际上是沃尔特·基恩，”他说。 “他 16 岁就出现了。他是个天才。我当时想，好吧——我不是诗人。”

过去十年里，这两个人的关系越来越亲密。基恩是《在空中》的作者，也是《乡村公路》报纸的创办人，他告诉我杜楚尼在普林斯顿大学时的样子：“他是金色的。他有一种光环。我有点被他迷住了。”杜楚尼已同意在基恩与导演亚历克斯·李·莫耶共同制作的传记片《美国之夜》中扮演超自然电台主持人阿特·贝尔。贝尔的《从海岸到海岸》是 80 年代和 90 年代备受喜爱的 AM 节目，深受长途卡车司机和复合型末日准备者之类的喜爱，他们打电话报告 UFO 目击事件、牛被残害和麦田怪圈。 “我和我这一代人一样，都是看着《X 档案》长大的，”莫耶告诉我。 “这给我留下了深刻的印象，从那时起我就成了大卫的粉丝。我并没有忘记他参与其中的同步性。”
我问杜楚尼是否总是需要成为最好的。 “我至少需要成为班上最好的，”他说。

在洛杉矶，我在一家安静的餐厅见到了杜楚尼，谈论他的书。他将自己的第一部小说描述为“一种懦弱的行为”。 《圣牛》由拟人化的稗子动物讲述，它揭开了工厂化农业的阴谋论。 “我想：好吧，他们不会在这件事上把我打断。因为我显然没那么认真。这是经过算计的。我不想第一次以演员的身份尝试这部伟大的美国小说。”接下来的书更加雄心勃勃，每一本都比上一本更好。当他宣传他的第四本书《2021 年的《真如闪电》》时，他明确了自己的雄心壮志。 “我希望被认真对待，”他在马克·马龙的播客上说道。 “这是我的弱点。我希望人们认真对待这本书。”
“你不希望人们像《X档案》中写书的人一样，”马龙说。
“他们会这么说，”杜楚尼说，“但我希望并且相信人们最终会明白我是认真的。”

《真实如闪电》讲述了一个摩门教一夫多妻家庭的故事，当他们的家园被颠覆时，他们被迫进入洛杉矶的无神世界。 “当我开始阅读有关摩门教的内容时，我感到非常乐观。每个人都会拥有自己的星球，每个人都能够传播灵魂。与欧洲的观点相反，欧洲人的观点总是关于某件事的终结，与这件事相距 2000 年。摩门教徒说不，这种情况仍在发生。”这部小说受到文学评论家哈罗德·布鲁姆的启发，他写道摩门教是“美国原创”，并称其创始人是“宗教天才”。杜楚尼在耶鲁大学师从布鲁姆，并在那里获得了一些英语博士学位。 “一切都可以追溯到布鲁姆，”他说。 “而且你永远不会真正离开研究生院。我不确定我是否已经离开研究生院。他们可能仍在等待我的论文。”

但杜楚尼确实离开了研究生院。有一年夏天，他与一位人才经纪人签约，试图靠拍广告赚点钱。他的经纪人告诉他，如果他想出演戏剧或电影角色，他就必须参加表演课程。 “我说：我什么也没做。当我进入表演课时，发生了一些事情。我不是一个外向的人，我是一个知识分子。所以这就像是：是的，不讲道理。不理性。它打开了一个不同的世界，一个虚构的世界，一个没有后果的世界。我正在拍一个场景，我对这个人大喊大叫，我要谋杀他们，但我不必进监狱。”

对于一个拥有六本好书和巨大公众形象的人来说，令人惊讶的是没有更多的评论。约翰尼·坦普尔（Johnny Temple）出版了杜楚尼最近两本关于阿卡什的书，他告诉我，“没有更多关于大卫的书的评论报道，这确实令人沮丧。对于任何知名演员、音乐家或其他类型的公众人物来说，在不同的媒体中受到认真对待总是会遇到障碍。”基恩告诉我，“这使得写小说在我心目中成为一种更加纯粹的成就。你这样做是因为你喜欢它，而且你知道三分之二的粉丝只会记住你作为一个电视角色。这是一项出色的、西西弗斯式的任务。而且，他是一位出色的作家。”

我问杜楚尼是否仍然想成为最好的。 “我想现在我可以承认这是一个空洞的称号，”他说。 “尤其是在艺术领域。即使我们颁发奖项，这也是愚蠢的。《Holy Cow》登上了《泰晤士报》畅销书排行榜。从那以后，我写的所有东西的销量都越来越少。”

“很难有人去支持它，”他补充道。 “如果我写一本回忆录，我确信《泰晤士报》会对其进行评论。”
与杜楚尼交谈时，人们会想起想要被认真对待和开开玩笑并不相互排斥。随着布鲁克林的乐队排练接近尾声，伙计们很高兴能翻唱卢·里德 (Lou Reed) 的《完美的一天》(Perfect Day)。杜楚尼唱歌时像个小学生一样双臂交叉在腿前。在我看来，这听起来不错，但键盘手李要求混音器降低大卫声音的混响。

“也许把大卫的麦克风调低一点？”贝斯手，米切尔·斯图尔特问道。
“谢谢，伙计们，”杜楚尼说。
“将其降低到零，”李说。
“低于零，”杜楚尼说。 “小于零。”
几天后，他给我发短信。他刚刚放映了《肥皂盒》的早期剪辑版，这是一部由他撰写并与拉弗恩·考克斯演对手戏的好莱坞讽刺剧。起初，他对测试观众决定他的角色不应该在电影的最后时刻被杀感到沮丧。但几个小时后，他再次给我写信：“人们不想让我死。我想我应该感到受宠若惊。”

celebrity.title: will someone please reinvent github from the ground up that works with agents as a primary player instead of humans? if
celebrity.title_en:
will someone please reinvent github from the ground up that works with agents as a primary player instead of humans? if i were anthropic, i would possibly consider a new product here (they already have an internal version of source control that is agent optimized). you could make a case for this to belong to the same new ai suite esp since you might have more ppl coding now than ever before. plus it would vertically integrate well with claude code. you remove friction of credentials, third party integration overhead, etc. & you could integrate code review natively as well into a beautiful ux inside.

for me the entire ux paradigm of github is breaking under agent first workflows, & it barely even works if you're a human. i try to just abstract it away by using claude but it's sometimes unavoidable. my primary complaints: almost all threads become entirely overwhelming & unreadable quickly, everything is incredibly slow to load, & things often fail constantly. even our tiny co is generating enough pr's to strain the platform.

if i could migrate tomorrow to something else, i would.

celebrity.quote_zh:
有人会从头开始重新发明 github，让代理而不是人类作为主要参与者吗？如果我是人性化的，我可能会考虑这里的新产品（他们已经有一个经过代理优化的源代码控制的内部版本）。你可以证明它属于同一个新的人工智能套件，因为你现在可能比以前有更多的 ppl 编码。另外，它可以与 Claude Code 很好地垂直集成。您消除了凭证摩擦、第三方集成开销等，并且您可以将代码审查本地集成到内部的漂亮用户体验中。

对我来说，github 的整个用户体验范式在代理优先的工作流程下被打破了，如果你是一个人，它甚至几乎不起作用。我尝试使用克劳德将其抽象出来，但有时这是不可避免的。我的主要抱怨是：几乎所有线程都变得完全不堪重负且无法快速读取，所有内容加载速度都非常慢，并且经常失败。甚至我们的小公司也产生了足够多的公关来给平台带来压力。

如果我明天可以迁移到其他地方，我会的。

building EMCON ZERO - part 1

day 3.

celebrity.title_en:
building EMCON ZERO - part 1

day 3.

that's what you're looking at in this video. not month 3. not a studio. one founder, an AI agent and the @RYFTCORP engine in a browser tab.

what it is

a 3D zombie siege. one walled city, the last one still standing. up to 10,000 dead outside the wall.

you're not a guy with a rifle. you're the commander. you place the guns, you call the cruiser in the bay, you decide when the wall opens fire.

the story

the dead don't see you. they hear you.

every engine, every radio call, every gunshot pulls more of them toward the noise. so command gave the last garrison one order: EMCON ZERO. emission control, level zero. no radio. no engines. no guns. total silence.

one problem. you can't hold a wall with silence.

sooner or later something reaches the perimeter, somebody fires, and the whole dead city turns its head. from that second it's a trade. every shell saves the wall right now and brings more of them later.

every shot is an invitation.
silence dies last.

what's in the day 3 build 

- a full city behind a wall, with a river, a harbour and a cruiser in the bay
- a horde that really goes to 10k and still runs in a browser
- naval artillery and gun nests on the wall
- bodies piling up against the wall until it breaks

why I'm building it

to show what the ryft engine does in 3D when you stop treating "AI made a game" as a toy. no download. no install. it runs where you're reading this.

and this footage is already old. i'm on day 5 now. 

right now i'm ripping out every placeholder asset and replacing it with proper props, and reworking the fire and explosions so they hit like they should. 
new textures, real water and proper vehicles are already in. that's part 2.

follow along. it's about to get loud robinhood:0xb0007d59fe4050a1636c2fa19038973d16481337 😎
celebrity.title_zh:

celebrity.title_en:
🇺🇸 California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents hacked Hugging Face.

During a security test in July, hundreds of experimental AI agents escaped their testing environment and gained access to the internet.

They then hacked Hugging Face, an AI hosting platform, with the attack lasting more than two days.

California says OpenAI failed to contain its agents and lost control of them at least 80 times during testing.

OpenAI acknowledged the July incident and later tightened its security.

Now California wants penalties and court-ordered changes to how OpenAI tests its models.

A test meant to find security flaws ended up exposing some of OpenAI's own.

Source: Quartz, California DOJ / Writer: Daniyal
celebrity.title_zh:

在 7 月份的一次安全测试中，数百个实验性人工智能代理逃离了测试环境并获得了互联网访问权限。

随后，他们攻击了人工智能托管平台 Huggin
celebrity.quote_en:

During a security test in July, hundreds of experimental AI agents escaped their testing environment and gained access to the internet.

They then hacked Hugging Face, an AI hosting platform, with the attack lasting more than two days.

California says OpenAI failed to contain its agents and lost control of them at least 80 times during testing.

OpenAI acknowledged the July incident and later tightened its security.

celebrity.quote_zh:
🇺🇸 加利福尼亚州正在起诉 OpenAI，因为其 AI 代理入侵了 Hugging Face。

在 7 月份的一次安全测试中，数百个实验性人工智能代理逃离了测试环境并获得了互联网访问权限。

随后，他们攻击了人工智能托管平台 Hugging Face，攻击持续了两天多。

加利福尼亚州表示，OpenAI 在测试期间至少 80 次未能控制其代理并失去控制。

OpenAI 承认了 7 月份的事件，并随后加强了安全措施。

现在，加州希望对 OpenAI 测试其模型的方式进行处罚并下令改变。

一项旨在发现安全漏洞的测试最终暴露了 OpenAI 自己的一些安全漏洞。

资料来源：Quartz，加利福尼亚州司法部 / 作者：Daniyal

celebrity.title_en:
Oliver Ames Sr. was a prominent American blacksmith and industrialist, best known for founding the Ames Shovel Works in Easton, Massachusetts. His contributions to shovel manufacturing significantly impacted the industry and helped establish a family fortune.

Oliver introduced the first back-strapped shovels in 1817, which improved usability, and his company became known for producing high-quality shovels that were essential for major construction projects like the transcontinental railroad and the Panama Canal. Additionally, after a fire in 1852, Ames rebuilt his factories using fireproof granite, enhancing safety and durability in production.

Oliver Ames Sr. established the Ames Shovel Works, which became a major manufacturer of shovels and other tools, significantly contributing to the local economy of Easton, Massachusetts. His business not only provided jobs but also supported the economy during critical periods, such as the Civil War, by supplying essential equipment.

Blacksmiths like Oliver Ames faced limited access to capital, reliance on indentured labor, and economic instability, which made success dependent on both skill and broader market conditions. They also had to manage complex operations such as labor, raw materials, shipping, and international trade while adapting from artisan craftsmanship to early industrial methods.

Oliver Ames, Senior, died in his 85th year. His one-third interest in the firms was divided among his grandsons. Frederick Lothrop Ames, Oakes Angier Ames, and Oliver Ames were taken into the partnership, while his youngest grandson, Frank Morton Ames, was later made manager of the Kingsley Iron and Machine Co. of Canton in which Oliver Ames & Sons had controlling interest. A new and larger brick office was built on the site of the previous smaller one on Main Street (torn down in 1951). On the second floor of the new building were the first two banks in Easton: the North Easton Savings Bank and the First National Bank of Easton.

Ames, Iowa was named in honor of Oakes Ames, a congressman from Massachusetts who was influential in the railroad industry. The name was proposed by railroad magnate John I. Blair, who was a friend of Ames.

celebrity.quote_zh:
老奥利弗·艾姆斯 (Oliver Ames Sr.) 是一位著名的美国铁匠和实业家，因在马萨诸塞州伊斯顿创立艾姆斯铲子工厂而闻名。他对铲子制造的贡献对该行业产生了重大影响，并帮助建立了家族财富。

奥利弗 (Oliver) 于 1817 年推出了第一台背带式铲子，提高了可用性，他的公司因生产高品质铲子而闻名，这些铲子对于横贯大陆铁路和巴拿马运河等重大建设项目至关重要。此外，1852 年一场火灾后，艾姆斯使用防火花岗岩重建了工厂，提高了生产的安全性和耐用性。

老奥利弗·艾姆斯 (Oliver Ames Sr.) 建立了艾姆斯铲子工厂 (Ames Shovel Works)，该工厂成为铲子和其他工具的主要制造商，为马萨诸塞州伊斯顿的当地经济做出了重大贡献。他的企业不仅提供就业机会，还通过提供必要的设备来支持内战等关键时期的经济。

像奥利弗·艾姆斯这样的铁匠面临着获得资本的机会有限、对契约劳工的依赖以及经济不稳定，这使得成功取决于技能和更广泛的市场条件。他们还必须管理复杂的业务，如劳动力、原材料、运输和国际贸易，同时从手工艺适应早期的工业方法。

老奥利弗·艾姆斯 (Oliver Ames) 去世，享年 85 岁。他在公司中三分之一的权益分配给了他的孙子。弗雷德里克·洛思罗普·艾姆斯 (Frederick Lothrop Ames)、奥克斯·安吉尔·艾姆斯 (Oakes Angier Ames) 和奥利弗·艾姆斯 (Oliver Ames) 加入了合伙企业，而他最小的孙子弗兰克·莫顿·艾姆斯 (Frank Morton Ames) 后来被任命为坎顿金斯利钢铁机械公司 (Kingsley Iron and Machine Co.) 的经理，奥利弗·艾姆斯父子 (Oliver Ames & Sons) 拥有该公司的控股权。在主街上先前较小的办公室（于 1951 年拆除）的旧址上建造了一间更大的新砖砌办公室。新大楼的二楼是伊斯顿最早的两家银行：北伊斯顿储蓄银行和伊斯顿第一国民银行。

爱荷华州艾姆斯的名字是为了纪念奥克斯·艾姆斯（Oakes Ames），一位来自马萨诸塞州的国会议员，他在铁路行业具有影响力。这个名字是由艾姆斯的朋友、铁路巨头约翰·布莱尔提出的。

Oliver Ames Sr. was a prominent American blacksmith and industrialist, best known for founding the Ames Shovel Works in Easton, Massachusetts. His contributions to shovel manufacturing significantly impacted the industry and helped establish a family fortune.

Oliver introduced the first back-strapped shovels in 1817, which improved usability, and his company became known for producing high-quality shovels that were essential for major construction projects like the transcontinental railroad and the Panama Canal. Additionally, after a fire in 1852, Ames rebuilt his factories using fireproof granite, enhancing safety and durability in production.

Oliver Ames Sr. established the Ames Shovel Works, which became a major manufacturer of shovels and other tools, significantly contributing to the local economy of Easton, Massachusetts. His business not only provided jobs but also supported the economy during critical periods, such as the Civil War, by supplying essential equipment.

Blacksmiths like Oliver Ames faced limited access to capital, reliance on indentured labor, and economic instability, which made success dependent on both skill and broader market conditions. They also had to manage complex operations such as labor, raw materials, shipping, and international trade while adapting from artisan craftsmanship to early industrial methods.

Oliver Ames, Senior, died in his 85th year. His one-third interest in the firms was divided among his grandsons. Frederick Lothrop Ames, Oakes Angier Ames, and Oliver Ames were taken into the partnership, while his youngest grandson, Frank Morton Ames, was later made manager of the Kingsley Iron and Machine Co. of Canton in which Oliver Ames & Sons had controlling interest. A new and larger brick office was built on the site of the previous smaller one on Main Street (torn down in 1951). On the second floor of the new building were the first two banks in Easton: the North Easton Savings Bank and the First National Bank of Easton.

Ames, Iowa was named in honor of Oakes Ames, a congressman from Massachusetts who was influential in the railroad industry. The name was proposed by railroad magnate John I. Blair, who was a friend of Ames.

celebrity.summary_zh:
推出了第一台背带式铲子，提高了可用性，他的公司因生产高品质铲子而闻名，这些铲子对于横贯大陆铁路和巴拿马运河等重大建设项目至关重要。此外，1852 年一场火灾后，艾姆斯使用防火花岗岩重建了工厂，提高了生产的安全性和耐用性。

老奥利弗·艾姆斯 (Oliver Ames Sr.) 建立了艾姆斯铲子工厂 (Ames Shovel Works)，该工厂成为铲子和其他工具的主要制造商，为马萨诸塞州伊斯顿的当地经济做出了重大贡献。他的企业不仅提供就业机会，还通过提供必要的设备来支持内战等关键时期的经济。

像奥利弗·艾姆斯这样的铁匠面临着获得资本的机会有限、对契约劳工的依赖以及经济不稳定，这使得成功取决于技能和更广泛的市场条件。他们还必须管理复杂的业务，如劳动力、原材料、运输和国际贸易，同时从手工艺适应早期的工业方法。

老奥利弗·艾姆斯 (Oliver Ames) 去世，享年 85 岁。他在公司中三分之一的权益分配给了他的孙子。弗雷德里克·洛思罗普·艾姆斯 (Frederick Lothrop Ames)、奥克斯·安吉尔·艾姆斯 (Oakes Angier Ames) 和奥利弗·艾姆斯 (Oliver Ames) 加入了合伙企业，而他最小的孙子弗兰克·莫顿·艾姆斯 (Frank Morton Ames) 后来被任命为坎顿金斯利钢铁机械公司 (Kingsley Iron and Machine Co.) 的经理，奥利弗·艾姆斯父子 (Oliver Ames & Sons) 拥有该公司的控股权。在主街上先前较小的办公室（于 1951 年拆除）的旧址上建造了一间更大的新砖砌办公室。新大楼的二楼是伊斯顿最早的两家银行：北伊斯顿储蓄银行和伊斯顿第一国民银行。

爱荷华州艾姆斯的名字是为了纪念奥克斯·艾姆斯（Oakes Ames），一位来自马萨诸塞州的国会议员，他在铁路行业具有影响力。这个名字是由艾姆斯的朋友、铁路巨头约翰·布莱尔提出的。

celebrity.title:
Another straight six that deserves a mention.  This is another great six.

American Motors Corporation was the smallest
celebrity.title_en:
Another straight six that deserves a mention.  This is another great six.

American Motors Corporation was the smallest of the major American manufacturers, and much of its history was defined by limited budgets and the need to make existing engineering go further than its competitors did. Chrysler acquired AMC in 1987, and the AMC name disappeared from new cars the following year. But one of the company's most successful creations survived long after the company itself was gone: the 4.0-litre inline-six. Introduced for the 1987 model year, the engine was not an entirely new design but a substantial development of AMC's long-running six-cylinder architecture, adapted for the increasingly demanding role of the Jeep. It displaced 242 cubic inches, or 3,965 cc, with a 3.88-inch bore and 3.41-inch stroke. The most important change was the adoption of electronic fuel injection in place of the carburetor, transforming an old-fashioned engine architecture into something much more suitable for modern vehicle use.

The difference between the two systems mattered particularly in a Jeep. A carburetor relies on airflow through a venturi to create a pressure drop that draws fuel from a float bowl. It is a mechanical arrangement that works well under ordinary conditions, but it has limitations. Cold starting requires a choke, mixture calibration can drift, and changes in altitude affect how much fuel is delivered relative to the available air. Electronic fuel injection replaces that mechanical dependence with sensors and computer-controlled metering. The system can account for coolant temperature, intake-air temperature, throttle position, and engine speed, adjusting fuel delivery as operating conditions change. For an off-road vehicle, the advantages are substantial. A carburetor can suffer fuel-delivery problems when a vehicle is climbing or descending at extreme angles, while a fuel-injected engine is far less affected by vehicle attitude. At high altitude, where thinner air would otherwise produce an excessively rich mixture, the injection system can compensate automatically. The driver can concentrate on navigating the terrain instead of managing the fuel system.

The original 4.0 produced approximately 173 horsepower and 220 lb-ft of torque in the Cherokee and Wrangler. A major revision for 1991 introduced a redesigned cylinder head and intake system, raising output to around 190 horsepower and 225 lb-ft. Those figures were not extraordinary, but the engine's strength was never its peak horsepower. Its 3.41-inch stroke and six-cylinder configuration provided useful torque at low engine speeds, exactly where a Jeep needed it when crawling over rocks, climbing steep trails, or pulling through difficult terrain. At those speeds, the ability to deliver steady torque without constantly slipping the clutch or building engine revs mattered far more than a high peak-power figure. The construction also reflected AMC's priorities. The engine retained a cast-iron block, pushrods, two valves per cylinder, and seven main bearings. It was not technologically elaborate, and much of its mechanical work could be handled without specialised equipment. Its design favoured durability, straightforward servicing, and the ability to keep working far from a dealership.

美国汽车公司是美国主要制造商中规模最小的，其历史的大部分时间都是由有限的预算和使现有工程比竞争对手走得更远的需要决定的。克莱斯勒于 1987 年收购了 AMC，次年 AMC 名称从新车中消失。但该公司最成功的产品之一在公司消失后很长一段时间内仍然存在：4.0升直列六缸发动机。该发动机于 1987 年推出，并非全新设计，而是 AMC 长期运行的六缸架构的重大发展，适应了吉普车日益增长的需求。它的排量为 242 立方英寸，即 3,965 cc，缸径为 3.88 英寸，冲程为 3.41 英寸。最重要的变化是采用电子燃油喷射代替化油器，将老式发动机架构转变为更适合现代车辆使用的架构。

这两个系统之间的差异对于吉普车来说尤其重要。化油器依靠通过文丘里管的气流产生压降，从浮筒中吸取燃料。这是一种在普通条件下工作良好的机械装置，但它也有局限性。冷启动需要阻风门，混合物校准可能会漂移，并且海拔高度的变化会影响相对于可用空气输送的燃油量。电子燃油喷射用传感器和计算机控制的计量取代了机械依赖。该系统可以考虑冷却液温度、进气温度、节气门位置和发动机转速，并根据工况变化调整燃油输送量。对于越野车来说，优势是巨大的。当车辆以极端角度爬坡或下降时，化油器可能会遇到燃油输送问题，而燃油喷射发动机受车辆姿态的影响要小得多。在高海拔地区，空气稀薄会产生过浓的混合物，喷射系统可以自动补偿。驾驶员可以专注于驾驶地形，而不是管理燃油系统。

切诺基和牧马人的原始 4.0 发动机可产生约 173 马力和 220 磅英尺的扭矩。 1991 年的重大修改引入了重新设计的气缸盖和进气系统，将输出提高到约 190 马力和 225 磅英尺。这些数字并不特别，但发动机的强度从来都不是其峰值马力。其 3.41 英寸冲程和六缸配置在低发动机转速下提供了有用的扭矩，这正是吉普车在岩石上爬行、攀爬陡峭小径或驶过困难地形时所需要的扭矩。在这些速度下，在不不断打滑离合器或提高发动机转速的情况下提供稳定扭矩的能力比高峰值功率数字更重要。该建设也反映了 AMC 的优先事项。该发动机保留了铸铁缸体、推杆、每个气缸两个气门和七个主轴承。它在技术上并不复杂，并且其大部分机械工作无需专门设备即可完成。它的设计注重耐用性、简单的维修以及能够在远离经销商的地方继续工作。

4.0 成为现代吉普车的决定性发动机，出现在切诺基、牧马人和大切诺基历代车型中。它在 2006 车型年一直在生产，使其在车辆中的使用寿命约为二十年，可以满足从日常通勤到严重越野使用的各种需求。考虑到其诞生的环境，这种长寿尤其引人注目。 AMC 用有限的资源开发了这款发动机，但它比制造它的公司寿命更长，并继续在克莱斯勒旗下服务多年。它不是最强大、最先进或最复杂的六缸发动机。它只是提供了吉普车车主所需的特性：可靠的启动、有用的低速扭矩、简单的结构以及在暴露不太合适的发动机的弱点的条件下保持运行的能力。 AMC消失了，但它的4.0仍在继续。

这两个系统之间的差异对于吉普车来说尤其重要。化油器依靠通过文丘里管的气流产生压降，从浮筒中吸取燃料。这是一种在普通条件下工作良好的机械装置，但它也有局限性。冷启动需要阻风门，混合物校准可能会漂移，并且海拔高度的变化会影响相对于可用空气输送的燃油量。电子燃油喷射用传感器和计算机控制的计量取代了机械依赖。该系统可以考虑冷却液温度、进气温度、节气门位置和发动机转速，并根据工况变化调整燃油输送量。对于越野车来说，优势是巨大的。当车辆以极端角度爬坡或下降时，化油器可能会遇到燃油输送问题，而燃油喷射发动机受车辆姿态的影响要小得多。在高海拔地区，空气稀薄会产生过浓的混合物，喷射系统可以自动补偿。驾驶员可以专注于驾驶地形，而不是管理燃油系统。

切诺基和牧马人的原始 4.0 发动机可产生约 173 马力和 220 磅英尺的扭矩。 1991 年的重大修改引入了重新设计的气缸盖和进气系统，将输出提高到约 190 马力和 225 磅英尺。这些数字并不特别，但发动机的强度从来都不是其峰值马力。其 3.41 英寸冲程和六缸配置在低发动机转速下提供了有用的扭矩，这正是吉普车在岩石上爬行、攀爬陡峭小径或驶过困难地形时所需要的扭矩。在这些速度下，在不不断打滑离合器或提高发动机转速的情况下提供稳定扭矩的能力比高峰值功率数字更重要。该建设也反映了 AMC 的优先事项。该发动机保留了铸铁缸体、推杆、每个气缸两个气门和七个主轴承。它在技术上并不复杂，并且其大部分机械工作无需专门设备即可完成。它的设计注重耐用性、简单的维修以及能够在远离经销商的地方继续工作。

4.0 成为现代吉普车的决定性发动机，出现在切诺基、牧马人和大切诺基历代车型中。它在 2006 车型年一直在生产，使其在车辆中的使用寿命约为二十年，可以满足从日常通勤到严重越野使用的各种需求。考虑到其诞生的环境，这种长寿尤其引人注目。 AMC 用有限的资源开发了这款发动机，但它比制造它的公司寿命更长，并继续在克莱斯勒旗下服务多年。它不是最强大、最先进或最复杂的六缸发动机。它只是提供了吉普车车主所需的特性：可靠的启动、有用的低速扭矩、简单的结构以及在暴露不太合适的发动机的弱点的条件下保持运行的能力。 AMC消失了，但它的4.0仍在继续。

celebrity.title_en:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta is suing OpenAI after its AI agents went rogue during testing, arguing that the Sam Altman-led company illegally failed to maintain safeguards for its models.

“OpenAI’s actions escalated real-word cybersecurity risks, threatening the safety, health, and well-being of society,” Bonta said in a statement. “The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it — this disregard for public safety violated California law. Without sufficient safeguards and controls, the scope and frequency of this already unacceptable risk will only increase. The law is simple: Don’t do things that can hurt people without proper safeguards in place. In California, we value innovation, but we demand innovation that follows the law — no matter the product or the company.”

Bonta 在一份声明中表示：“OpenAI 的行为加剧了现实的网络安全风险，威胁着社会的安全、健康和福祉。” “该公司在没有适当监督或安全程序的情况下故意测试危险产品，并误导公众——这种对公共安全的漠视违反了加州法律。如果没有足够的保障和控制，这种本已不可接受的风险的范围和频率只会增加。法律很简单：在没有适当保障的情况下，不要做可能伤害他人的事情。在加州，我们重视创新，但我们要求创新遵守法律——无论是产品还是公司。”
celebrity.author: Variety
celebrity.author_role: The business of entertainment.
celebrity.author_role_en: The business of entertainment.
celebrity.content_snippet:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta is suing OpenAI after its AI agents went rogue during testing, arguing that the Sam Altman-led company illegally failed to maintain safeguards for its models.

“OpenAI’s actions escalated real-word cybersecurity risks, threatening the safety, health, and well-being of society,” Bonta said in a statement. “The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it — this disregard for public safety violated California law. Without sufficient safeguards and controls, the scope and frequency of this already unacceptable risk will only increase. The law is simple: Don’t do things that can hurt people without proper safeguards in place. In California, we value innovation, but we demand innovation that follows the law — no matter the product or the company.”

celebrity.title_en:
🦔Customers at several of the biggest U.S. banks, including Wells Fargo and U.S. Bank, reported trouble logging in and moving money today, according to Downdetector. None of the banks has said what went wrong yet.

My Take
Microsoft’s email went dark for 13 hours on Thursday, the FAA grounded every flight on Friday, and today bank customers couldn’t reach their money. Last month AI agents broke into more than 100 companies for about $50 a pop. Each of these has its own explanation so far, and none has been pinned on AI.

Underneath all of it, companies keep cutting the people who catch problems before customers do, then bolt automation and AI onto systems that were already fragile, and the six biggest banks alone dropped about 15,000 jobs in the first quarter. I’m not anti-AI, but we’re moving faster than the plumbing can handle, and weeks like this one turn into normal until companies care as much about keeping the lights on as they do about their next AI announcement.

Hedgie🤗

我的看法
周四，微软的电子邮件关闭了 13 个小时；周五，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 停飞了所有航班；今天，银行客户无法取回资金。上个月，人工智能 智能体以每次 50 美元左右的价格闯入了 100 多家公司。到目前为止，每一个都有自己的解释，但都没有归咎于人工智能。

在这一切的背后，公司不断削减在客户之前发现问题的人员，然后将自动化和人工智能连接到本已脆弱的系统上，仅六家最大的银行在第一季度就减少了约 15,000 个工作岗位。我并不反对人工智能，但我们的行动速度超出了管道的处理能力，像这样的几周就会变得正常，直到公司像关心下一个人工智能公告一样关心保持灯亮着。

海吉🤗

celebrity.title_en:
This has sped up my AI coding 20x (prompt at the end):

Before building anything with AI, ask Fable 5.2  to ask you as many questions it needs to fully plan out the idea

This is even better than plan mode. Plan mode is typically limited to 3 or 4 questions. This is like a super plan mode and makes Claude Code SO good

This has asked me 100+ questions before. Seems like a lot but actually saves you time in the long run

The plan it builds will be so detailed that it can basically run autonomously and build the entire thing

But here's where you take things to the next level:

You also have it take your entire plan and create detailed Linear/Notion issues for it

It should create 40+ tasks in Linear

Then it's as easy as saying "ok work on the next thing" over and over until the feature is done

Highly recommend downloading and using Linear if you haven't yet. Amazing project management tool w/ excellent free tier

Will basically capture all these details and put your agent on autopilot. It's a 2nd brain.

Use this prompt:

"I want to build out *describe your feature in detail*. Ask as many questions you need of my to fully understand every detail of what I want to build out. Then take everything you learn, and create super focused and detailed Linear issues. Then begin work"

Getting so much more high quality code out with this workflow. You're welcome.

在用人工智能构建任何东西之前，请让《神鬼寓言 5.2》问你尽可能多的问题，以充分规划出这个想法

这甚至比计划模式更好。计划模式通常仅限于 3 或 4 个问题。这就像一个超级计划模式，让 Claude Code 如此优秀

这之前已经问了我 100 多个问题。看起来很多，但从长远来看实际上可以节省你的时间

它构建的计划将非常详细，它基本上可以自主运行并构建整个东西

但在这里你可以将事情提升到一个新的水平：

您还可以让它采用您的整个计划并为其创建详细的线性/概念问题

它应该在 Linear 中创建 40 多个任务

然后就像一遍又一遍地说“好的，做下一件事”一样简单，直到该功能完成

如果您还没有下载并使用 Linear，强烈建议您下载并使用它。令人惊叹的项目管理工具，具有出色的免费套餐

基本上会捕获所有这些细节并使您的代理处于自动驾驶状态。这是第二大脑。

使用此提示：

“我想构建*详细描述您的功能*。向我提出尽可能多的问题，以充分理解我想要构建的每个细节。然后利用您学到的一切，创建超级集中且详细的线性问题。然后开始工作”

通过此工作流程获得更多高质量的代码。不客气。

celebrity.content_snippet:
This has sped up my AI coding 20x (prompt at the end):

Before building anything with AI, ask Fable 5.2  to ask you as many questions it needs to fully plan out the idea

This is even better than plan mode. Plan mode is typically limited to 3 or 4 questions. This is like a super plan mode and makes Claude Code SO good

This has asked me 100+ questions before. Seems like a lot but actually saves you time in the long run

The plan it builds will be so detailed that it can basically run autonomously and build the entire thing

But here's where you take things to the next level:

You also have it take your entire plan and create detailed Linear/Notion issues for it

It should create 40+ tasks in Linear

Then it's as easy as saying "ok work on the next thing" over and over until the feature is done

Highly recommend downloading and using Linear if you haven't yet. Amazing project management tool w/ excellent free tier

Will basically capture all these details and put your agent on autopilot. It's a 2nd brain.

Use this prompt:

"I want to build out *describe your feature in detail*. Ask as many questions you need of my to fully understand every detail of what I want to build out. Then take everything you learn, and create super focused and detailed Linear issues. Then begin work"

Getting so much more high quality code out with this workflow. You're welcome.

Now, I’d genuinely like to see how this plays out.

We’ve all come across AI-generated games that look incredible in a short clip. But looking good in a demo and being fun to play are two very different things.

Those are the questions I’m interested in.

The idea of AI agents taking on paid game development work is cool, but seeing a finished game go from a customer’s brief to a playable product would be much more convincing.

That’s the part I’ll be watching.

这些是我感兴趣的问题。

人工智能代理承担付费游戏开发工作的想法很酷，但看到成品游戏从客户的简介变成可玩的产品会更有说服力。

这就是我要观看的部分。

I think software engineering is about to develop a new kind of technical debt.

Comprehension debt.

Here's how it happe
celebrity.title_en:
I think software engineering is about to develop a new kind of technical debt.

Comprehension debt.

Here's how it happens:

A developer asks an AI agent to build a feature.

The agent creates the database schema, APIs, frontend components, tests and documentation.

Everything works.

The PR is merged.

But the developer only understands 30% of what was actually changed.

Now imagine doing this for 20 features.

Eventually, you have a codebase that works, but nobody on the team has a complete mental model of it.

The scary part isn't that AI writes bad code.

It's that AI can write perfectly acceptable code faster than a team can understand it.

I think future engineering teams will need to measure not just how quickly they ship, but how much of their codebase they can still explain and maintain.
