items.title: A.I. Helps Find Major Security Bug in Java, a Software Platform Vital to the Internet
items.title_en: A.I. Helps Find Major Security Bug in Java, a Software Platform Vital to the Internet

inline_images.caption: Java is a popular programming language that is estimated to be in use by 90 percent of Fortune 500 companies, including banks, hospitals, the aviation industry and technology giants like Google and Amazon. (Paul Sakuma/Associated Press)
inline_images.alt: Java is a popular programming language that is estimated to be in use by 90 percent of Fortune 500 companies, including banks, hospitals, the aviation industry and technology giants like Google and Amazon.

items.author: Dustin Volz and Dylan Freedman
items.article_content:
A cybersecurity start-up revealed on Tuesday it had used a new A.I. model to uncover a critical software bug in Java, a popular programming language that is used by government agencies and about 90 percent of Fortune 500 companies.

It was the latest evidence of a reality facing companies and the government, as A.I. is revolutionizing the field of discovery in computer vulnerabilities, identifying flaws in code so rapidly that cybersecurity professionals are struggling to keep up.

Using leading A.I. models, the start-up Calif has now unearthed a string of serious vulnerabilities in recent months. The start-up’s latest effort exposed a flaw, using OpenAI’s recently released GPT-6 Cyber model, in Java, which is widely used by banks, hospitals, the aviation industry and technology giants, as well as government agencies, including those with national security missions.

“Java is the beating heart of the modern economy,” said Bruce Dang, a senior researcher at Calif. “Practically speaking, all major companies” will be affected by the bug, he added.

Mr. Dang and his colleagues have worked in recent days to coordinate with all government agencies in the intelligence-sharing alliance known as Five Eyes — which consists of the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Britain — and major vendors in the private sector, including Google and Microsoft.

The National Security Agency, whose classified network went down on Tuesday for what it described as “routine software maintenance,” did not respond to a request for comment. It was not clear whether that disruption was related to addressing the Java bug.

Oracle, the owner of the Java trademark and provider of commercial Java licenses, did not respond to a request for comment. The company released a software patch Tuesday.

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, in an alert, pressed organizations to “immediately patch” the vulnerability.

Announcements about exploits from Calif and other groups using A.I. tools have startled the cybersecurity world and upended what was considered achievable by a small band of coders just a few months ago. Those efforts, which involve working with A.I. models before they are publicly released, help alert network defenders to undetected problems in order to fix them before malicious hackers find them and wreak havoc.

But the Java discovery may be Calif’s most serious yet, one that could enable a hacker to gain remote access to sensitive internal systems. It comes on the heels of a cascade of seemingly independent disruptions in recent days — outages of Microsoft products, a nationwide grounding of flights and banking interruptions — that have shaken public confidence in the reliability of everyday technology and fanned fears that A.I. may be to blame. (So far, the explanations for each appear to be relatively benign.)

A.I.-assisted bug hunting and cyberattack building has made it much easier to identify weaknesses in systems, said Ollie Whitehouse, the chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Center in Britain. “We have seen this taking shape for some time, with A.I. being used to discover a growing number of latent vulnerabilities across software and the digital services we all rely on.”

The Java vulnerability is the second major bug Calif has unearthed with the aid of OpenAI models in the past few weeks. It discovered last month security flaws in PHP, a programming language estimated to be used by 70 percent of websites and apps on the internet.

The PHP disclosure set off fears around the world about significant disruptions for consumers and businesses and a mad scramble by companies to patch PHP before hackers could pounce. Government agencies, including the N.S.A., warned businesses to take websites offline if they could not immediately deploy a patch. Disruptions ultimately proved less serious than some predicted, however, as it became clear hackers could not easily reverse-engineer the attack method.

But the PHP flaws chiefly concerned software that helps websites function. In contrast, Java helps power the nuts and bolts of the modern digital world, including cloud computing architecture, identity management tools, email services and more.

“Java is everywhere,” said Thai Duong, the chief executive of Calif. He noted that the Java bug was not easy to weaponize into an attack, giving defenders more time to patch the issues.

“But vulnerabilities have a very long tail,” he added, predicting the bug could be a threat to systems that do not update in the next five to 10 years.

Among the most significant findings, Calif demonstrated that it could use this bug to break into Keycloak, a widely used authentication and log-in system. Keycloak protects thousands of organizations, including CERN, Hewlett Packard, UnitedHealthcare and NASA.

Quang Luong, a security researcher from Calif, discovered the bug in Java’s base64 decoder, a common algorithm that is used to translate binary computer data into a legible palette of text that includes lowercase and uppercase letters, numbers and punctuation. On certain computers, researchers found that Java encounters a bug when it tries to decode 64 “A” characters followed by one equal sign:

“AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=”

This bug, called Java4Shell, causes Java to erroneously execute code by tampering with a section of computer memory, which typically makes the program immediately crash. With the help of A.I., Calif researchers demonstrated that they could corrupt data by carefully arranging the memory — a technique called “heap grooming” — granting them full unauthorized access to the underlying system.

The New York Times independently verified Calif’s discovery after the start-up shared proof-of-concept details about the attack. The successful test took less than an hour.

The rapid advances with artificial intelligence in cybersecurity efforts mirror what the chess world champion Garry Kasparov observed after he lost a match to IBM’s Deep Blue computer nearly 30 years ago.

The best games of chess would not be played by humans or computers, he predicted, but by a hybrid of the two. The concept, which he called a “centaur” in a nod to the mythological half-human, half-horse creature, took off. For years, centaurs were seen as the best chess players, reaching new heights in the game.

Now companies and the government are contending with the threat of the “centaur hacker” — half A.I., half human, and fully capable of creating chaos on the internet.

The most alarming discoveries — for now, at least — still require human expertise. In recent months, small teams of veteran security researchers have used top-shelf A.I. models to build in days or hours the kinds of advanced cyberattacks that once took platoons of elite hackers at spy agencies like the National Security Agency months to construct.

Fouad Matin, who leads cyber preparedness and safety at OpenAI, said Calif’s Java research “shows how A.I. can assist expert security researchers with finding serious flaws in software we all depend on” and helps lead to collaborative fixes. “We want more security teams to have these capabilities and tools to help make critical software more secure for everyone,” Mr. Matin said.

Eduardo Vela Nava, an information security engineer at Google, said that “once notified, we swiftly rolled out mitigations and patches across Google services, developed detection to ensure there was no exploitation of the vulnerability, and provided guidance to our customers.”

Security experts expect those risks are likely to grow, at least in the short term. For about 20 years, centaur chess players were widely seen as capable of playing the best game of chess. But eventually, the centaurs were eclipsed by more advanced supercomputers.

Mr. Duong believes it may be only a matter of time until A.I. can independently build the most advanced cyberattacks, which could usher in a new age of unpredictable problems. The F.B.I. this week issued an alert warning that hackers were using new autonomous A.I. hacking tools to target government agencies and businesses around the world.

“I don’t know how much time we have — maybe three months, maybe three years,” Mr. Duong said. “But right now, the best hacker is the centaur hacker.”

New York Times:
Cybersecurity startup Calif says it used GPT-6 Cyber to uncover an RCE flaw in Java dubbed “Java4Shell”; Oracle has released a patch  —  The discovery by security company Calif shows A.I.'s ability to find gaping security holes in popul
items.content_snippet: The discovery by security company Calif shows A.I.'s ability to find gaping security holes in popular software.
items.summary_en: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized model for cybersecurity research that significantly enhances security audit and patching performance through optimized alignment. It has uncovered 81 high-severity flaws in Firefox and developed 948 exploits for Linux kernel vulnerabilities, currently restricted to authorized security teams due to its 'Critical' classification.

items.title_zh: 人工智能帮助发现对互联网至关重要的软件平台Java的主要安全漏洞

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI发布专用网络安全大模型GPT-6 Cyber，通过深度对齐优化，显著提升了在安全审计与漏洞修复方面的性能。该模型已在Firefox浏览器中挖掘出81个高危漏洞，并在Linux内核测试中成功构建948项利用方案，目前该工具被列为“关键”级别，仅限受邀安全机构使用。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized model for cybersecurity research that significantly enhances security audit and patching performance through optimized alignment. It has uncovered 81 high-severity flaws in Firefox and developed 948 exploits for Linux kernel vulnerabilities, currently restricted to authorized security teams due to its 'Critical' classification.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: GPT-6 Cyber的出现标志着AI红队测试已从辅助工具进化为具备自主攻击链构建能力的深度威胁防御系统。随着此类模型能力的增强，软件供应链的安全性将从人工审查彻底转向模型对抗的“算法防线”，这也将迫使全球监管机构重新评估针对高阶自动化攻击工具的出口管制红线。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The release of GPT-6 Cyber signifies that AI red-teaming has evolved into a system capable of autonomous exploit chain construction. As these capabilities scale, software supply chain security will shift from manual audits to model-based adversarial defense, forcing regulators to re-evaluate export controls on high-tier offensive AI tools.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: OpenAI发布专用网络安全大模型GPT-6 Cyber，通过深度对齐优化，显著提升了在安全审计与漏洞修复方面的性能。该模型已在Firefox浏览器中挖掘出81个高危漏洞，并在Linux内核测试中成功构建948项利用方案，目前该工具被列为“关键”级别，仅限受邀安全机构使用。
ai_analysis.digest_en: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized model for cybersecurity research that significantly enhances security audit and patching performance through optimized alignment. It has uncovered 81 high-severity flaws in Firefox and developed 948 exploits for Linux kernel vulnerabilities, currently restricted to authorized security teams due to its 'Critical' classification.

成功识别并修复Firefox及Linux内核中数百处关键漏洞

Identified and assisted in patching hundreds of critical vulnerabilities in Firefox and the Linux kernel.

items.article_content_zh:
一家网络安全初创公司周二透露，它已经使用了一种新的人工智能技术。 Java 是一种流行的编程语言，被政府机构和大约 90% 的财富 500 强公司使用。

这是企业和政府面临的现实的最新证据，因为人工智能。正在彻底改变计算机漏洞的发现领域，识别代码缺陷的速度如此之快，以至于网络安全专业人员都在努力跟上。

使用领先的人工智能近几个月来，初创公司 Calif 发现了一系列严重的漏洞。这家初创公司的最新成果暴露了一个缺陷，即使用 OpenAI 最近发布的 Java 语言 GPT-6 网络模型，该模型被银行、医院、航空业和科技巨头以及政府机构（包括承担国家安全任务的机构）广泛使用。

加州高级研究员 Bruce Dang 表示：“Java 是现代经济的心脏。”他补充说，“实际上，所有大公司”都将受到该漏洞的影响。

党先生和他的同事最近几天一直致力于与“五眼”情报共享联盟（由美国、加拿大、澳大利亚、新西兰和英国组成）中的所有政府机构以及包括谷歌和微软在内的私营部门的主要供应商进行协调。

美国国家安全局的机密网络于周二因“例行软件维护”而瘫痪，该局没有回应置评请求。目前尚不清楚这次中断是否与解决 Java 错误有关。

Java 商标的所有者和商业 Java 许可证的提供商 Oracle 没有回应置评请求。该公司周二发布了一个软件补丁。

网络安全和基础设施安全局在一份警报中敦促各组织“立即修补”该漏洞。

加州和其他组织发布的利用人工智能工具进行攻击的消息震惊了网络安全界，并颠覆了几个月前一小群程序员认为可以实现的目标。这些工作包括在人工智能模型公开发布之前与它们合作，帮助网络防御者注意未被发现的问题，以便在恶意黑客发现并造成破坏之前修复它们。

但Java的发现可能是加州迄今为止最严重的，它可能使黑客能够远程访问敏感的内部系统。最近几天，一系列看似独立的中断——微软产品中断、全国范围内的航班停飞和银行业务中断——动摇了公众对日常技术可靠性的信心，并加剧了人们对人工智能可能是罪魁祸首的担忧。（到目前为止，对每种现象的解释似乎都相对温和。）

英国国家网络安全中心首席技术官奥利·怀特豪斯（Ollie Whitehouse）表示，人工智能辅助的漏洞挖掘和网络攻击构建使识别系统漏洞变得更加容易。“我们已经看到这种情况形成一段时间了，人工智能被用来发现我们都依赖的软件和数字服务中越来越多的潜在漏洞。”

Java漏洞是Calif在过去一年里在OpenAI模型的帮助下发现的第二个重大漏洞。

但 PHP 缺陷主要涉及帮助网站运行的软件。相比之下，Java 有助于为现代数字世界的具体细节提供动力，包括云计算架构、身份管理工具、电子邮件服务等。

加利福尼亚州首席执行官 Thai Duong 表示：“Java 无处不在。”他指出，Java 漏洞不容易被武器化为攻击手段，这让防御者有更多时间来修复问题。

“但是漏洞有很长的尾巴，”他补充道，并预测该错误可能会对未来五到十年内不更新的系统构成威胁。

最重要的发现之一是，Calif 证明它可以利用此错误侵入 Keycloak（一种广泛使用的身份验证和登录系统）。 Keycloak 保护数千个组织，包括 CERN、惠普、UnitedHealthcare 和 NASA。

来自加州的安全研究员Quang Luong发现了Java的base64解码器中的漏洞。base64解码器是一种常见的算法，用于将二进制计算机数据转换为包含小写字母、大写字母、数字和标点的易读文本。研究人员发现，在某些计算机上，当Java尝试解码64个“A”字符后跟一个等号时，会遇到一个漏洞：

这个名为Java4Shell的漏洞会导

人工智能在网络安全领域的快速进步与国际象棋世界冠军加里·卡斯帕罗夫 (Garry Kasparov) 近 30 年前输给 IBM 深蓝计算机后所观察到的情况如出一辙。

他预测，最好的国际象棋游戏不会由人类或计算机来玩，而是由两者的混合体来玩。他将这个概念称为“半人马”，以向神话中的半人半马生物致敬。多年来，半人马被视为最好的国际象棋棋手，在棋艺上达到了新的高度。

现在，公司和政府正在应对“半人马黑客”的威胁——一半是人工智能，一半是人类，完全有能力在互联网上制造混乱。

最令人震惊的发现——至少目前——仍然需要人类的专业知识。近几个月来，由经验丰富的安全研究人员组成的小团队使用了顶级的人工智能。这些模型可以在几天或几小时内构建出各种高级网络攻击，而这些攻击曾经需要国家安全局等间谍机构的精英黑客几个月才能构建。

OpenAI负责网络准备和安全的福阿德·马丁（Fouad martin）表示，加州的Java研究“表明，人工智能可以帮助安全研究专家发现我们都依赖的软件中的严重缺陷”，并有助于促成合作修复。“我们希望更多的安全团队拥有这些能力和工具，帮助每个人都能更安全地使用关键软件，”马丁说。

谷歌的信息安全工程师爱德华多·维拉·纳瓦（Eduardo Vela Nava）表示，“收到通知后，我们迅速在谷歌的服务中推出了缓解措施和补丁，开发了检测措施，以确保没有人利用这个漏洞，并为我们的客户提供了指导。”

安全专家预计，至少在短期内，这些风险可能会增加。在大约20年的时间里，半人马棋手被普遍认为有能力下最好的国际象棋。但最终，半人马被更先进的超级计算机所取代。

Duong 先生认为，人工智能出现这种情况可能只是时间问题。可以独立构建最先进的网络攻击，这可能会迎来一个充满不可预测问题的新时代。联邦调查局本周发布了一份警报，称黑客正在使用新的自主人工智能。针对世界各地政府机构和企业的黑客工具。

“我不知道我们还有多少时间——也许是三个月，也许是三年，”杨先生说。 “但现在，最好的黑客是半人马黑客。”

paragraphs: A cybersecurity start-up revealed on Tuesday it had used a new A.I. model to uncover a critical software bug in Java, a popular programming language that is used by government agencies and about 90 percent of Fortune 500 companies.

It was the latest evidence of a reality facing companies and the government, as A.I. is revolutionizing the field of discovery in computer vulnerabilities, identifying flaws in code so rapidly that cybersecurity professionals are struggling to keep up.

Using leading A.I. models, the start-up Calif has now unearthed a string of serious vulnerabilities in recent months. The start-up’s latest effort exposed a flaw, using OpenAI’s recently released GPT-6 Cyber model, in Java, which is widely used by banks, hospitals, the aviation industry and technology giants, as well as government agencies, including those with national security missions.
“Java is the beating heart of the modern economy,” said Bruce Dang, a senior researcher at Calif. “Practically speaking, all major companies” will be affected by the bug, he added.

Mr. Dang and his colleagues have worked in recent days to coordinate with all government agencies in the intelligence-sharing alliance known as Five Eyes — which consists of the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Britain — and major vendors in the private sector, including Google and Microsoft.

The National Security Agency, whose classified network went down on Tuesday for what it described as “routine software maintenance,” did not respond to a request for comment. It was not clear whether that disruption was related to addressing the Java bug.
Oracle, the owner of the Java trademark and provider of commercial Java licenses, did not respond to a request for comment. The company released a software patch Tuesday.
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, in an alert, pressed organizations to “immediately patch” the vulnerability.

Announcements about exploits from Calif and other groups using A.I. tools have startled the cybersecurity world and upended what was considered achievable by a small band of coders just a few months ago. Those efforts, which involve working with A.I. models before they are publicly released, help alert network defenders to undetected problems in order to fix them before malicious hackers find them and wreak havoc.

But the Java discovery may be Calif’s most serious yet, one that could enable a hacker to gain remote access to sensitive internal systems. It comes on the heels of a cascade of seemingly independent disruptions in recent days — outages of Microsoft products, a nationwide grounding of flights and banking interruptions — that have shaken public confidence in the reliability of everyday technology and fanned fears that A.I. may be to blame. (So far, the explanations for each appear to be relatively benign.)

A.I.-assisted bug hunting and cyberattack building has made it much easier to identify weaknesses in systems, said Ollie Whitehouse, the chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Center in Britain. “We have seen this taking shape for some time, with A.I. being used to discover a growing number of latent vulnerabilities across software and the digital services we all rely on.”

The Java vulnerability is the second major bug Calif has unearthed with the aid of OpenAI models in the past few weeks. It discovered last month security flaws in PHP, a programming language estimated to be used by 70 percent of websites and apps on the internet.

The PHP disclosure set off fears around the world about significant disruptions for consumers and businesses and a mad scramble by companies to patch PHP before hackers could pounce. Government agencies, including the N.S.A., warned businesses to take websites offline if they could not immediately deploy a patch. Disruptions ultimately proved less serious than some predicted, however, as it became clear hackers could not easily reverse-engineer the attack method.

But the PHP flaws chiefly concerned software that helps websites function. In contrast, Java helps power the nuts and bolts of the modern digital world, including cloud computing architecture, identity management tools, email services and more.
“Java is everywhere,” said Thai Duong, the chief executive of Calif. He noted that the Java bug was not easy to weaponize into an attack, giving defenders more time to patch the issues.
“But vulnerabilities have a very long tail,” he added, predicting the bug could be a threat to systems that do not update in the next five to 10 years.

Among the most significant findings, Calif demonstrated that it could use this bug to break into Keycloak, a widely used authentication and log-in system. Keycloak protects thousands of organizations, including CERN, Hewlett Packard, UnitedHealthcare and NASA.

Quang Luong, a security researcher from Calif, discovered the bug in Java’s base64 decoder, a common algorithm that is used to translate binary computer data into a legible palette of text that includes lowercase and uppercase letters, numbers and punctuation. On certain computers, researchers found that Java encounters a bug when it tries to decode 64 “A” characters followed by one equal sign:
“AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=”

This bug, called Java4Shell, causes Java to erroneously execute code by tampering with a section of computer memory, which typically makes the program immediately crash. With the help of A.I., Calif researchers demonstrated that they could corrupt data by carefully arranging the memory — a technique called “heap grooming” — granting them full unauthorized access to the underlying system.
The New York Times independently verified Calif’s discovery after the start-up shared proof-of-concept details about the attack. The successful test took less than an hour.

The rapid advances with artificial intelligence in cybersecurity efforts mirror what the chess world champion Garry Kasparov observed after he lost a match to IBM’s Deep Blue computer nearly 30 years ago.

The best games of chess would not be played by humans or computers, he predicted, but by a hybrid of the two. The concept, which he called a “centaur” in a nod to the mythological half-human, half-horse creature, took off. For years, centaurs were seen as the best chess players, reaching new heights in the game.
Now companies and the government are contending with the threat of the “centaur hacker” — half A.I., half human, and fully capable of creating chaos on the internet.

The most alarming discoveries — for now, at least — still require human expertise. In recent months, small teams of veteran security researchers have used top-shelf A.I. models to build in days or hours the kinds of advanced cyberattacks that once took platoons of elite hackers at spy agencies like the National Security Agency months to construct.

Fouad Matin, who leads cyber preparedness and safety at OpenAI, said Calif’s Java research “shows how A.I. can assist expert security researchers with finding serious flaws in software we all depend on” and helps lead to collaborative fixes. “We want more security teams to have these capabilities and tools to help make critical software more secure for everyone,” Mr. Matin said.

Eduardo Vela Nava, an information security engineer at Google, said that “once notified, we swiftly rolled out mitigations and patches across Google services, developed detection to ensure there was no exploitation of the vulnerability, and provided guidance to our customers.”

Security experts expect those risks are likely to grow, at least in the short term. For about 20 years, centaur chess players were widely seen as capable of playing the best game of chess. But eventually, the centaurs were eclipsed by more advanced supercomputers.

Mr. Duong believes it may be only a matter of time until A.I. can independently build the most advanced cyberattacks, which could usher in a new age of unpredictable problems. The F.B.I. this week issued an alert warning that hackers were using new autonomous A.I. hacking tools to target government agencies and businesses around the world.
“I don’t know how much time we have — maybe three months, maybe three years,” Mr. Duong said. “But right now, the best hacker is the centaur hacker.”

items.author: Dave Michaels and Anissa Gardizy and Robbie Whelan
items.article_content:
The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia, whose star chief executive Jensen Huang recently resigned after revelations of extramarital affairs, one with a suspected Chinese spy and another with an employee, according to people familiar with the matter.

The civil investigation adds to the crisis facing Nvidia, whose shares have fallen more than 10% since Huang was ousted. The focus of the investigation couldn’t immediately be learned but includes whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, some of the people said,

Nvidia posted a stronger-than-expected third quarter and a bullish outlook in its first earnings report after Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO in a scandal that has reportedly spawned an SEC investigation.

On the company's earnings call, newly appointed chairman Harvey Jones said the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," despite a movement among some employees and investors to bring him back.

Why it matters: Nvidia remains squarely at the center of the AI economy — and investors are anxious for guidance on the company's strategic roadmap following Huang's sudden exit.

Zoom in: Nvidia recorded quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion and net income of $65.3 billion, both more than doubling its performance from a year earlier.

S&P Capital IQ analysts had expected revenue of $108.7 billion and net income of $60.5 billion.

The company's data center revenue — its largest segment — rose 110% from a year ago to $107.6 billion.

The showing — which included a whopping gross profit margin of 74.8% — immediately calmed investors who have shaved more than $1 trillion off of Nvidia's market cap since the Huang scandal broke.

The stock was up as much as 5% in after-hours trading Tuesday following the company's earnings call.

It marks the first moment for interim CEO Colette Kress — who is also still serving as CFO — to exert her leadership during the most tumultuous moment in the company's history.

On the earnings call, she struck a steady tone, saying the company's momentum and innovation remain substantial.

Kress didn't mention Huang by name on the call but acknowledged the turbulent time and the "diverse" opinions — an apparent reference to the campaign to bring back Huang.

What we're watching: WSJ reported Tuesday afternoon that the SEC has opened a civil probe into the company.

An SEC spokesperson declined to comment.

Nvidia reps did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and the executives didn't discuss it on the call — but they said their quarterly 10Q filing with the SEC will be delayed.

The earnings call came hours after Huang posted a public letter saying he'd be "honored" to return as CEO.

Tech analyst Dan Ives earlier said the board could face a special shareholder meeting called by at least 15% of shareholders.

Jones said the company would not take questions on Huang's exit. He said the board would consider external and internal candidates and wants to move "as quickly as possible" but won't make a move until it finds "exactly the right person."

The intrigue: Huang reportedly faced pushback from Kress as he pushed financing deals to backstop the AI ecosystem.

On Tuesday's call, Kress signaled that the company would continue to provide financing where appropriate but would be "selective" and ensure that guarantees are necessary.

Editor's note: This story was updated to include comments from Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones and interim CEO Colette Kress made on the company's earnings call.

items.summary_en: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating Nvidia to evaluate whether its prior disclosures provided shareholders with an accurate depiction of its business. The inquiry remains in the preliminary fact-finding stage, focusing on whether the company's reporting on US chip export controls and related risks meets material disclosure requirements under securities laws.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国证券交易委员会（SEC）目前正针对英伟达（NVIDIA）开启核查，旨在评估其过往披露的信息是否向投资者提供了准确的业务画像。该调查仍处于早期核查阶段，重点在于确定公司在应对美国芯片出口管制及相关财务风险披露上，是否满足证券法律对重大信息披露的合规性要求。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating Nvidia to evaluate whether its prior disclosures provided shareholders with an accurate depiction of its business. The inquiry remains in the preliminary fact-finding stage, focusing on whether the company's reporting on US chip export controls and related risks meets material disclosure requirements under securities laws.

elements_zh.who: 美国证券交易委员会（SEC）、英伟达（NVIDIA）
elements_zh.where: 美国资本市场监管审查环境
elements_zh.what: 对公司信息披露真实性与完整性进行核查
elements_zh.why: 核实其在出口管制背景下对股东的风险告知义务是否履行到位

elements_en.who: US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Nvidia
elements_en.what: Reviewing the accuracy and completeness of investor disclosures
elements_en.why: To verify if the company fulfilled its obligations regarding risk disclosure amidst export control challenges

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 本轮审查的核心逻辑在于英伟达在应对地缘政治制裁时，其对供应链脆弱性和潜在市场损失的披露是否足以支撑投资人的知情权。若监管证实其在出口限制的影响范围上存在信息“遮掩”，英伟达或面临行政处罚，且可能触发针对其股价波动的各类证券集体诉讼，从而对其极高市场预期背后的溢价形成压力测试。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The core of this inquiry lies in whether Nvidia’s disclosures regarding supply chain fragility and market loss under geopolitical sanctions have adequately informed shareholders. Should regulators prove intentional obfuscation of the impact of export controls, the firm risks administrative penalties and shareholder class-action lawsuits, potentially exerting pressure on the valuation premium built upon its aggressive market growth projections.

items.article_content_zh:
据知情人士透露，美国证券交易委员会正在调查英伟达，该公司明星首席执行官黄仁勋最近因婚外情被曝光而辞职，其中一名与一名疑似中国间谍，另一名与一名员工发生婚外情。

此次民事调查加剧了英伟达面临的危机，自黄仁勋被赶下台以来，英伟达股价已下跌超过 10%。一些知情人士表示，调查的重点尚不清楚，但包括该公司的披露是否误导了投资者，

在黄仁勋因丑闻被罢免首席执行官职务后，英伟达公布了强于预期的第三季度业绩和乐观的前景，据报道该丑闻引发了 SEC 的调查。

在公司的财报电话会议上，新任命的董事长哈维琼斯表示，尽管一些员工和投资者采取行动，要求詹森重新担任首席执行官，但董事会“不打算恢复詹森的首席执行官职位”。

为什么重要：英伟达仍然处于人工智能经济的中心，在黄仁勋突然退出后，投资者迫切希望获得有关该公司战略路线图的指导。

放大：英伟达季度营收为 1158 亿美元，净利润为 653 亿美元，均较上年同期增长一倍多。

S&P Capital IQ 分析师此前预计营收为 1087 亿美元，净利润为 605 亿美元。

该公司最大的业务——数据中心收入比一年前增长了 110%，达到 1076 亿美元。

这一表现——包括高达 74.8% 的毛利率——立即安抚了投资者，自黄蜂丑闻爆发以来，英伟达市值已缩水逾 1 万亿美元。

在该公司召开财报电话会议后，该股周二盘后交易中上涨了 5%。

这标志着临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）（目前仍担任首席财务官）首次在公司历史上最动荡的时刻发挥领导作用。

在财报电话会议上，她语气平稳，表示公司的发展势头和创新仍然强劲。

克雷斯在电话中没有提到黄的名字，但承认当时的动荡时期和“不同”的观点——这显然是指召回黄的运动。

我们正在关注的内容：《华尔街日报》周二下午报道称，美国证券交易委员会已对该公司展开民事调查。

SEC 发言人拒绝发表评论。

Nvidia 代表没有立即回应置评请求，高管们也没有在电话会议上讨论此事，但他们表示，向 SEC 提交的 10 季度季度报告将被推迟。

财报电话会议召开前几个小时，黄仁勋发表了一封公开信，称他“很荣幸”重新担任首席执行官。

科技分析师 Dan Ives 早些时候表示，董事会可能面临由至少 15% 的股东召集的特别股东大会。

琼斯表示，该公司不会接受有关黄退出的问题。他表示，董事会将考虑外部和内部候选人，并希望“尽快”采取行动，但在找到“完全合适的人选”之前不会采取行动。

阴谋：据报道，黄在推动融资交易以支持人工智能生态系统时遭到了克雷斯的抵制。

在周二的电话会议上，克雷斯表示，该公司将继续在适当的情况下提供融资，但将是“有选择性的”，并确保担保是必要的。

编者注：本文已更新，其中包括 Nvidia 董事长哈维·琼斯 (Harvey Jones) 和临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 在公司财报电话会议上发表的评论。

paragraphs: The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia, whose star chief executive Jensen Huang recently resigned after revelations of extramarital affairs, one with a suspected Chinese spy and another with an employee, according to people familiar with the matter.

The civil investigation adds to the crisis facing Nvidia, whose shares have fallen more than 10% since Huang was ousted. The focus of the investigation couldn’t immediately be learned but includes whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, some of the people said,

Nvidia posted a stronger-than-expected third quarter and a bullish outlook in its first earnings report after Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO in a scandal that has reportedly spawned an SEC investigation.

On the company's earnings call, newly appointed chairman Harvey Jones said the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," despite a movement among some employees and investors to bring him back.
Why it matters: Nvidia remains squarely at the center of the AI economy — and investors are anxious for guidance on the company's strategic roadmap following Huang's sudden exit.
Zoom in: Nvidia recorded quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion and net income of $65.3 billion, both more than doubling its performance from a year earlier.
S&P Capital IQ analysts had expected revenue of $108.7 billion and net income of $60.5 billion.
The company's data center revenue — its largest segment — rose 110% from a year ago to $107.6 billion.
The showing — which included a whopping gross profit margin of 74.8% — immediately calmed investors who have shaved more than $1 trillion off of Nvidia's market cap since the Huang scandal broke.
The stock was up as much as 5% in after-hours trading Tuesday following the company's earnings call.
It marks the first moment for interim CEO Colette Kress — who is also still serving as CFO — to exert her leadership during the most tumultuous moment in the company's history.
On the earnings call, she struck a steady tone, saying the company's momentum and innovation remain substantial.
Kress didn't mention Huang by name on the call but acknowledged the turbulent time and the "diverse" opinions — an apparent reference to the campaign to bring back Huang.
What we're watching: WSJ reported Tuesday afternoon that the SEC has opened a civil probe into the company.
An SEC spokesperson declined to comment.
Nvidia reps did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and the executives didn't discuss it on the call — but they said their quarterly 10Q filing with the SEC will be delayed.
The earnings call came hours after Huang posted a public letter saying he'd be "honored" to return as CEO.
Tech analyst Dan Ives earlier said the board could face a special shareholder meeting called by at least 15% of shareholders.

Jones said the company would not take questions on Huang's exit. He said the board would consider external and internal candidates and wants to move "as quickly as possible" but won't make a move until it finds "exactly the right person."
The intrigue: Huang reportedly faced pushback from Kress as he pushed financing deals to backstop the AI ecosystem.
On Tuesday's call, Kress signaled that the company would continue to provide financing where appropriate but would be "selective" and ensure that guarantees are necessary.
Editor's note: This story was updated to include comments from Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones and interim CEO Colette Kress made on the company's earnings call.

items.title: Not even Sam Altman is safe from AI deepfakes on Instagram
items.title_en: Not even Sam Altman is safe from AI deepfakes on Instagram

inline_images.caption: Sam Altman Speaks At OpenAI Developers Conference In San Francisco
inline_images.alt: Sam Altman Speaks At OpenAI Developers Conference In San Francisco

items.author: Mia Sato
items.article_content:
Instagram is filled with people posting deepfaked content — including, as of late, from one of Meta’s most prominent executives.

Earlier in November, Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, shared a short clip to promote Muse, the company’s consumer AI agent. In the AI-generated clip, Wang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Jolly, the anthropomorphic mascot of Muse, are on a four-way video call. When Altman joins the call he’s dressed like Jolly, wearing a furry hooded suit and face paint to look like the cutesy character. The clip is captioned “When the homies meet about openai product strategy,” a reference to the AI agent race and the recent popularity of Muse.

Just a few years ago, AI content portraying real people led to strong public statements rebuking the use of the technology to imitate humans. In some cases legal action was threatened. Now, AI content has become part of the texture of a new reality, especially on social media. Leading up to the midterm elections, for example, political groups ran millions of dollars’ worth of AI-generated ads attacking opponents.

Wang has been doing a lot of what some have described as “anti-PR” to promote Muse, tweeting hundreds of times and referring to more traditional marketers as “corposlops.” Still, a major tech executive posting an AI video of a competitor is notable, especially on a platform that’s been criticized recently over AI-generated content. After an AI-generated image of actress Mia Goth gained traction in October, the Pearl star’s representative told The Verge it was “incomprehensible” that Instagram allowed the image to spread instead of focusing on the “protection and integrity of a public figure’s likeness.” Other celebrities, including Scarlett Johansson, are regularly the subject of sexualized AI imagery; Meta has removed some accounts in the past that it found to be posing as someone else and using their likeness.

Meta requires AI-generated videos depicting people to be labeled as AI, like Wang’s post is. Static images, however, have no such requirement, meaning the AI image of Goth had no disclosure. To make matters worse, the image was shared by a fan account with a blue verification badge given by Instagram.

Reached for comment, Meta spokesperson Tracy Clayton noted that Wang’s post is labeled as AI content. Clayton also pointed out that Altman has made his likeness available for AI content generation, as when OpenAI launched its Sora app (and it was quickly flooded with fake Altman videos). OpenAI didn’t respond to requests for comment.

items.title_zh: AI深度伪造蔓延，科技高管互为目标
items.summary_zh: Meta高管利用AI深度伪造技术制作包含友商高管的视频引发争议，凸显生成式AI在社交平台上的监管缺口

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Meta首席AI官Alexandr Wang近期在Instagram发布了一段由AI生成的视频，内容涉及Meta首席执行官马克·扎克伯格（Mark Zuckerberg）与OpenAI首席执行官萨姆·奥特曼（Sam Altman）的虚构视频通话。尽管该内容依平台规定标注为AI生成，但仍加剧了外界对于深度伪造技术模糊现实边界、冲击公众人物名誉权的担忧。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Alexandr Wang, Chief AI Officer at Meta, recently posted an AI-generated video on Instagram featuring fictitious video calls between Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Although the clip is labeled as AI-generated per platform requirements, it has intensified concerns regarding how deepfake technology blurs the line between reality and fabrication, posing risks to public figure integrity.

elements_zh.where: Meta旗下社交平台Instagram
elements_zh.what: 发布AI深度伪造的虚构视频，并将竞对高管纳入其中

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此事件反映出AI巨头在利用生成式内容进行营销时，已进入某种“去边界化”的博弈状态。当Meta自身高管带头使用深度伪造工具调侃竞争对手时，平台在执行AI内容标签政策时的中立性与严肃性将面临更严峻的质疑，这不仅会削弱平台对恶意虚假信息的打击公信力，也进一步恶化了公众人物名誉保护的商业生态环境。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident illustrates how AI tech giants have entered a state of 'de-bordering' in marketing through generated content. When a top Meta executive uses deepfake tools to satirize competitors, the platform’s neutrality and rigor in enforcing AI labeling policies are compromised, undermining the credibility of its efforts to mitigate malicious misinformation and degrading the ecosystem for protecting public figures' likenesses.

items.article_content_zh:
Instagram 上到处都是发布深度造假内容的人，其中包括最近来自 Meta 最著名的高管之一的内容。

11 月初，Meta 首席人工智能官 Alexandr Wang 分享了一段宣传该公司消费者人工智能代理 Muse 的短片。在 AI 生成的视频中，Wang、Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格、OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼以及 Muse 的拟人吉祥物 Jolly 正在进行四方视频通话。当奥特曼加入通话时，他穿得像乔利一样，穿着毛茸茸的连帽套装，脸上涂着颜料，看起来就像这个可爱的角色。该剪辑的标题是“当兄弟们见面讨论 openai 产品策略时”，指的是 AI 代理竞赛和 Muse 最近的流行。

就在几年前，描绘真人的人工智能内容引发了强烈的公开声明，谴责使用该技术来模仿人类。在某些情况下，威胁要采取法律行动。现在，人工智能内容已经成为新现实的一部分，尤其是在社交媒体上。例如，在中期选举之前，政治团体投放了价值数百万美元的人工智能生成的广告来攻击对手。

为了推广 Muse，王做了很多被一些人称为“反公关”的事情，他发了数百条推文，并将更传统的营销人员称为“corposlops”。尽管如此，一位主要科技高管发布竞争对手的人工智能视频还是值得注意的，尤其是在一个最近因人工智能生成内容而受到批评的平台上。 10 月份，人工智能生成的女演员米娅·高斯 (Mia Goth) 的一张照片受到关注后，这位珍珠明星的代表告诉 The Verge，Instagram 允许这张照片传播，而不是专注于“公众人物肖像的保护和完整性”，这是“不可理解的”。其他名人，包括斯嘉丽约翰逊，经常成为性感人工智能图像的主题； Meta 过去删除了一些发现冒充他人并使用其肖像的帐户。

Meta 要求人工智能生成的描绘人物的视频被贴上人工智能的标签，就像王的帖子一样。然而静态图像没有这样的要求，这意味着哥特的人工智能图像没有泄露。更糟糕的是，这张图片是由一个带有 Instagram 提供的蓝色验证徽章的粉丝账户分享的。

Meta 发言人特雷西·克莱顿 (Tracy Clayton) 联系我们寻求评论时指出，王的帖子被标记为人工智能内容。克莱顿还指出，奥特曼已经将他的肖像用于人工智能内容生成，就像 OpenAI 推出其 Sora 应用程序时一样（很快就充斥着假奥特曼视频）。 OpenAI 没有回应置评请求。

【起因与机理】利用生成式AI工具宣传企业产品，但引发了关于AI内容监管与公众人物肖像保护的讨论
【核心事实细节】Meta内部高管参与AI深度伪造内容传播，模糊了官方内容与虚假信息的界限。
【行业影响与走向】事件揭示了社交媒体对深度伪造技术监管的双重标准风险。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] Promotion of AI products while sparking debates on content regulation and likeness protection
[Key Fact Detail] Meta executive involvement in deepfake content blurs the line between official PR and misinformation.

paragraphs: Instagram is filled with people posting deepfaked content — including, as of late, from one of Meta’s most prominent executives.

Earlier in November, Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, shared a short clip to promote Muse, the company’s consumer AI agent. In the AI-generated clip, Wang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Jolly, the anthropomorphic mascot of Muse, are on a four-way video call. When Altman joins the call he’s dressed like Jolly, wearing a furry hooded suit and face paint to look like the cutesy character. The clip is captioned “When the homies meet about openai product strategy,” a reference to the AI agent race and the recent popularity of Muse.

Just a few years ago, AI content portraying real people led to strong public statements rebuking the use of the technology to imitate humans. In some cases legal action was threatened. Now, AI content has become part of the texture of a new reality, especially on social media. Leading up to the midterm elections, for example, political groups ran millions of dollars’ worth of AI-generated ads attacking opponents.

Wang has been doing a lot of what some have described as “anti-PR” to promote Muse, tweeting hundreds of times and referring to more traditional marketers as “corposlops.” Still, a major tech executive posting an AI video of a competitor is notable, especially on a platform that’s been criticized recently over AI-generated content. After an AI-generated image of actress Mia Goth gained traction in October, the Pearl star’s representative told The Verge it was “incomprehensible” that Instagram allowed the image to spread instead of focusing on the “protection and integrity of a public figure’s likeness.” Other celebrities, including Scarlett Johansson, are regularly the subject of sexualized AI imagery; Meta has removed some accounts in the past that it found to be posing as someone else and using their likeness.

Meta requires AI-generated videos depicting people to be labeled as AI, like Wang’s post is. Static images, however, have no such requirement, meaning the AI image of Goth had no disclosure. To make matters worse, the image was shared by a fan account with a blue verification badge given by Instagram.

Reached for comment, Meta spokesperson Tracy Clayton noted that Wang’s post is labeled as AI content. Clayton also pointed out that Altman has made his likeness available for AI content generation, as when OpenAI launched its Sora app (and it was quickly flooded with fake Altman videos). OpenAI didn’t respond to requests for comment.

items.title: AppLovin among firms in talks to acquire Criteo, sources say
items.title_en: AppLovin among firms in talks to acquire Criteo, sources say

inline_images.caption_en: AppLovin among firms in talks to acquire Criteo, sources say (Photo: REUTERS)

items.author: Reuters
items.article_content:
NEW YORK, Nov 17 (Reuters) - US advertising technology firm AppLovin is among the companies in talks to acquire smaller Paris-based peer Criteo, according to two people familiar with the matter.

Reuters reported in July that other prospective buyers included Vista Equity Partners and the smaller Quinti Capital, which during the summer expressed interest in jointly acquiring Criteo.

Following that approach led by Vista, Criteo engaged an investment bank to help evaluate its strategic alternatives, including a potential sale, said the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.

Criteo declined to comment.

AppLovin, Vista Equity and Quinti did not respond to requests for comment.

Details of the AppLovin discussions, including a potential sale price, were unclear.

Criteo's shares have fallen more than 50% over the past five years amid its lackluster market performance, leaving the company with a market value of roughly $1 billion, based on LSEG data.

A transaction involving Criteo could be announced before the end of the year, although no deal is guaranteed and the company may ultimately decide to remain independent, the people told Reuters.

Nasdaq-listed Criteo, founded in 2005 and headquartered in Paris, provides advertising technology that helps brands, retailers and agencies target consumers across digital channels and measure the effectiveness of their marketing campaigns.

The company's stock has fallen despite its efforts to reshape its business around the fast-growing retail media market after changes to online privacy rules disrupted parts of the ad-tech industry.

Palo Alto, California-based AppLovin helps businesses market and monetize apps through artificial intelligence-driven advertising software. Its market value on Monday was $136 billion, LSEG data show.

items.article_content_zh:
路透纽约 11 月 17 日电 — 据两位知情人士透露，美国广告科技公司 AppLovin 正参与洽谈收购规模较小的巴黎同行 Criteo。

路透社此前于今年 7 月报道称，其他潜在买家还包括 Vista Equity Partners 以及规模较小的 Quinti Capital，两家机构曾在今夏表达过联合收购 Criteo 的意向。

匿名知情人士表示，在 Vista 牵头接触后，Criteo 已聘请一家投资银行协助评估其战略选项，包括潜在的整体出售方案。

Criteo 对此拒绝置评。AppLovin、Vista Equity 与 Quinti 亦未回应置评请求。

目前关于 AppLovin 洽谈的具体细节（包括潜在收购报价）尚不明确。

根据伦敦证券交易所集团（LSEG）的数据，由于市场表现持续低迷，Criteo 股价在过去五年间累计下跌超过 50%，目前公司市值约为 10 亿美元。

知情人士向路透社透露，涉及 Criteo 的交易可能在今年年底前正式宣布，但目前尚无法保证最终达成协议，公司也仍有可能决定保持独立运营。

在纳斯达克上市的 Criteo 成立于 2005 年，总部位于巴黎，主营广告技术业务，帮助品牌商、零售商及代理机构跨数字渠道精准触达消费者并评估营销活动效果。

尽管在线隐私规则变革冲击了部分广告科技行业后，Criteo 一直在努力围绕快速增长的零售媒体市场重塑业务，但其股价依然承压走低。

总部位于美国加州帕洛阿尔托的 AppLovin 通过人工智能驱动的广告软件帮助企业开展应用推广与商业化变现。LSEG 数据显示，截至周一，AppLovin 市值高达 1,360 亿美元。

【起因与机理】Criteo长期估值低迷，AppLovin寻求规模效应以巩固广告投放技术栈地位
【关键数据与实测】标的公司Criteo五年内市值缩水逾50%，当前市值约10亿美元。
【各方立场与态度】该事件反映了广告技术领域的存量资产整合趋势。

items.title: Corporate-Card Startup Ramp Raising Funds at $70 Billion Valuation
items.title_en: Corporate-Card Startup Ramp Raising Funds at $70 Billion Valuation
items.author: Kate Clark
items.article_content:
Fintech company is reportedly seeking at least $1 billion after doubling annualized revenue to $2 billion.

Ramp, the fast-growing corporate-card and financial-management technology company, is in preliminary discussions to raise at least $1 billion at a valuation exceeding $70 billion, potentially marking its third financing round in a year.

The proposed investment would further increase Ramp’s valuation, which has more than doubled over the past 12 months as businesses increasingly adopt its financial software and artificial intelligence tools.

Existing investors Coatue Management and Thrive Capital, founded by Josh Kushner, are reportedly discussing leading the financing, according to The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the negotiations.

Founded in 2019 and led by CEO Eric Glyman, Ramp has rapidly emerged as one of the most valuable privately held financial technology companies.

In October, the company announced that its annualized revenue had surpassed $2 billion, roughly double what it was a year earlier.

Ramp also completed a $1.85 billion financing round last month at a $60 billion valuation. A new round exceeding $70 billion would represent at least a 16.7% increase in just weeks.

The company’s corporate-card business still generates most of its revenue, but its broader financial-management platform is becoming an increasingly important growth driver.

Ramp expects revenue from other services, including bill payments and banking, to surpass its corporate-card revenue within the next year.

AI Spending Creates New Growth Opportunities

Artificial intelligence has become a key part of Ramp’s expansion strategy.

The company is benefiting from rising corporate spending on AI services while developing tools that help businesses monitor and control those expenses.

Its Router product, for example, helps companies manage AI-related expenditures, addressing a growing challenge as enterprises deploy multiple AI models, applications and subscription services.

The expansion reflects Ramp’s strategy of evolving beyond corporate credit cards into a comprehensive financial-management platform that combines payments, expense controls, automation and AI-powered software.

Acquisition Strategy and Potential IPO

Ramp is expected to use part of the proceeds from its proposed financing to pursue mergers and acquisitions, potentially expanding its product offerings and market reach.

The company could pursue an initial public offering as early as 2027, although no formal timetable has been established.

Investors are closely monitoring the market for technology IPOs, including Anthropic’s anticipated public offering, as a potential indicator of investor demand for high-growth technology companies.

Ramp’s existing investor base includes Thrive Capital, Coatue Management, D1 Capital Partners, Founders Fund and Redpoint Ventures.

At a valuation exceeding $70 billion, Ramp would further strengthen its position among the world’s most valuable privately held technology companies.

The proposed transaction remains in preliminary discussions, and its final size, valuation and participating investors could change.

items.article_content_zh:
据报道，金融科技公司在将年收入翻倍至 20 亿美元后，正在寻求至少 10 亿美元的融资。

Ramp 是一家快速发展的公司卡和财务管理技术公司，目前正在初步讨论筹集至少 10 亿美元资金，估值将超过 700 亿美元，这可能是一年内的第三轮融资。

拟议的投资将进一步提高 Ramp 的估值，随着企业越来越多地采用其财务软件和人工智能工具，Ramp 的估值在过去 12 个月内增加了一倍多。

据《华尔街日报》援引知情人士的消息称，现有投资者 Coatue Management 和乔什·库什纳 (Josh Kushner) 创立的 Thrive Capital 正在讨论主导此次融资。

Ramp 成立于 2019 年，由首席执行官 Eric Glyman 领导，已迅速成为最有价值的私营金融科技公司之一。

10月，该公司宣布年化收入超过20亿美元，大约是去年同期的两倍。

Ramp 上个月还完成了 18.5 亿美元的融资，估值为 600 亿美元。新一轮融资超过 700 亿美元，意味着短短几周内至少增长了 16.7%。

该公司的公司卡业务仍然产生大部分收入，但其更广泛的财务管理平台正在成为越来越重要的增长动力。

Ramp 预计其他服务（包括账单支付和银行业务）的收入将在明年超过其公司卡收入。

人工智能支出创造新的增长机会

人工智能已成为Ramp扩张战略的关键组成部分。

该公司受益于企业在人工智能服务上的支出不断增加，同时开发了帮助企业监控和控制这些支出的工具。

例如，其路由器产品可帮助企业管理人工智能相关支出，解决企业部署多种人工智能模型、应用程序和订阅服务时面临的日益严峻的挑战。

此次扩张反映了 Ramp 的战略，即从企业信用卡发展成为一个综合性财务管理平台，结合了支付、费用控制、自动化和人工智能驱动的软件。

收购策略和潜在IPO

Ramp 预计将利用拟议融资的部分收益进行并购，从而有可能扩大其产品供应和市场覆盖范围。

该公司最早可能会在 2027 年进行首次公开​​募股，但尚未确定正式时间表。

投资者正在密切关注科技 IPO 市场，包括 Anthropic 预期的公开发行，以此作为投资者对高增长科技公司需求的潜在指标。

Ramp 现有的投资者包括 Thrive Capital、Coatue Management、D1 Capital Partners、Founders Fund 和 Redpoint Ventures。

Ramp 的估值超过 700 亿美元，将进一步巩固其在全球最有价值的私营科技公司中的地位。

拟议的交易仍在初步讨论中，其最终规模、估值和参与投资者可能会发生变化。

【起因与机理】作为高成长企业，通过高频融资扩张市场份额并巩固其在企业支付与财务自动化赛道的领先地位
【关键数据与实测】Ramp计划融资超10亿美元。
【各方立场与态度】该事件系Ramp一年内第三次融资，凸显其激进扩张策略。

items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
OpenAI releases two new language models. GPT-6.2 Astra is aimed at demanding professional work, while GPT-6.2 Sol is built for everyday use. OpenAI says both outperform their predecessors on benchmarks and cost less to run.

GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are available now for Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Pro-500 subscribers can use Ultrafast mode with both models. For the first time, Pro-200 subscribers also get Ultrafast access, starting with GPT-6.2 Sol.

Developers can access both models through the OpenAI API. OpenAI says API pricing for GPT-6.2 Astra is 20 percent cheaper than its predecessor's, at $8 per million input tokens, $0.40 for cached inputs, and $40 per million output tokens. GPT-6.2 Sol keeps GPT-6.1 Sol's pricing at $2 for input, $0.10 for cached inputs, and $10 for output per million tokens.Ad

OpenAI trained GPT-6.2 Astra to handle professional conventions in fields like law, finance, and accounting more reliably. The company says presentations pull layouts, colors, and typography from templates, matching exact font sizes. Slide titles are meant to capture a slide's main point, while body text stays focused on key details.Ad

OpenAI's announcement leans hard on the price-to-performance ratio of its models. On Agents' Last Exam, a benchmark that tests multi-step professional workflows, GPT-6.2 Astra scores 5.2 points above its predecessor GPT-6 Astra at less than a third of the cost, according to OpenAI. It leads Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 by 5.5 points at just 5 percent of the cost. Only Google's Gemini 4 Carbon keeps up with Astra on this benchmark.

On the legal benchmark Harvey LAB-AA, which covers tasks like contract clause analysis, GPT-6.2 Astra more than doubles Claude Fable 5.2's pass rate at about one-sixth of the cost, according to OpenAI. On the internal GDPval-v2 benchmark, which includes consulting, finance, and design tasks, OpenAI says Astra gains 6.2 percentage points over its predecessor while using 22 percent fewer output tokens.Ad

OpenAI says computer use, already a strong suit of the predecessor, got better again. In testing, the model reportedly built a 3D car model, wrote a physics solver in Python, and animated the results in Blender. In another demo, it modeled a remote-controlled car part by part and produced an animated assembly guide.

OpenAI also claims progress in web design. On the 3D benchmark AA-3D, human judges compare two blinded interactive experiences. GPT-6.2 Astra takes first with 1,318 Elo points, ahead of Claude Fable 5.2 at 1,271 and GPT-6.2 Sol at 1,259.Ad

On Terminal-Bench-Science, a benchmark that tests scientific workflows in a terminal, the model scores 9 percentage points above GPT-6 Astra, again at less than a third of the cost, according to OpenAI. Astra also sets a new high on the Vals Science Index, which measures how well models interpret biological data and run experiments, OpenAI says.Ad

GPT-6.2 Sol is for users who want a fast, versatile model for everyday tasks, OpenAI says. On the coding benchmark FrontierCode 2.0, which checks whether code changes meet the quality bar of real projects, Sol trails Astra by just 0.5 points at one-fifth the cost. OpenAI says the model also handles non-work tasks well.

GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol have also gotten better at cybersecurity, according to OpenAI. They find and exploit vulnerabilities more effectively, write more secure code, and deliver better bug fixes, with notably higher token efficiency in several tests. Both models hit the "Critical" threshold for cybersecurity in OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, just as GPT-6 Astra did before them.

OpenAI is adding stricter safeguards for potentially risky cybersecurity requests in response. These safeguards should make abuse harder but will also limit legitimate vulnerability research and security testing, OpenAI says.

OpenAI plans to offer the new models through OpenAI Daybreak, which already gives vetted security researchers access to other models with fewer guardrails. The published cybersecurity benchmark numbers come from internal tests with safeguards and classifiers turned off. OpenAI lays out its methodology in the accompanying safety report.

In the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, which rolls up nine evaluations across knowledge work, coding, science, and general knowledge, GPT-6.2 Astra finishes second, just behind Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2. Astra jumps five points over GPT-6 Astra, according to Artificial Analysis, passing Google's Gemini 4 Carbon (60 points) and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 (59 points). GPT-6.2 Sol picks up two points to reach 57, matching GPT-6 Astra's level at only about 15 percent of the cost per task.

OpenAI owns the Pareto frontier on cost versus performance, the line where no other model is both cheaper and better, according to Artificial Analysis. Only Anthropic and Meta models also land on that frontier. OpenAI holds most of the top spots on efficiency too, measured by output tokens per task. Claude Fable 5.2 is the only outside model that shows up there.

Artificial Analysis backs up OpenAI's claims in science and factual knowledge. GPT-6.2 Astra leads on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 and places second behind Claude Fable 5.2 on the physics reasoning test CritPt v2, the factual knowledge benchmark AA-Omniscience, and the knowledge benchmark HLE-Diamond. Astra also leads in 3D design (AA-3D) and robotics (AA-Robotics v0.1), scoring 79 on robotics against Sol's 78 and Claude Fable 5.2's 75.

Coding is a different story, though. According to Artificial Analysis, both models have flatlined there. In the Coding Agent Index, measured with the Codex harness at max compute, GPT-6.2 Astra stays right where GPT-6 Astra was. GPT-6.2 Sol actually drops three points from GPT-6.1 Sol. That decline comes from a 14-point slide on SWE-Atlas-QnA-AA, where the model omits key facts from its answers more often than its predecessor did.

Artificial Analysis also flags a high hallucination rate. At maximum effort, GPT-6.2 Astra hallucinates 59 percent of the time, Sol 55 percent. The metric is AA-Omniscience Hallucination Rate, which measures how frequently a model guesses on factual questions instead of saying it doesn't know. These are unusually hard questions, so the numbers don't reflect everyday hallucination rates.

Research organization Epoch AI tested GPT-6.2 Astra on its own benchmarks before launch. The model scores 174 points in the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI), tying Anthropic's Fable 5.2. Both models beat what the previous trend for reasoning models would have predicted before Astra, according to Epoch AI.

On real-world tasks pulled from Epoch AI's own research, Astra fell behind Fable 5.2 and barely improved over GPT-6 Astra. According to Epoch AI, the model missed the central question on simpler research projects and spun its wheels trying to fix things. On a task about researching AI data centers, Astra played it too safe and skipped key estimates, something Epoch AI says no contractor could get away with. Epoch AI rated Astra's writing as relatively strong compared to other tested models but still below its own bar.

One thing that stands out is Astra's ability to run complex reasoning within a single output token, with no visible chain of thought. Epoch AI clocks 12.3 serial steps for Astra, up from 10.5 for GPT-6 Astra and 4.2 for Claude Fable 5.1, the strongest non-OpenAI model at the time. Models that can reason this way without showing their work are harder to monitor, a safety concern that already came up with the first Astra model.

On FrontierMath Erdős, a benchmark of unsolved math problems, GPT-6.2 Astra cracked 7 of 68 tasks, each formally verified in the proof assistant Lean. The old record was 3 of 68, set by GPT-6.1 Sol. One of the seven had no known solution before.

GPT-6.2 Astra ranks 7th and GPT-6.2 Sol 9th in the Vals Index, separated by just 1.6 points. The price gap is wide, though. Sol runs $3.18 per task, less than a third of Astra's $10.68, making it the cheapest model in the top 10, according to Vals AI. Astra also got cheaper than its predecessor, scoring 2.6 points above GPT-6 Astra at roughly half of its $21.28 per-task cost. Vals AI says Astra uses the fewest output tokens in the top 10, averaging 91,000 per task.

Vals AI backs OpenAI's claim to the top spot on the Vals Science Index. Astra leads that ranking and takes first on Terminal-Bench Science and VCB 1–100 at about half the cost and half the runtime of GPT-6 Astra. Sol comes in third on Terminal-Bench Science at roughly a quarter of Astra's cost. On the broader Terminal-Bench 4 for agentic coding, Astra places 5th and Sol 7th.

Legal tests are where the models fall short, according to Vals AI. On the HLAB benchmark, Astra and Sol double their predecessors' scores but rank only 11th and 21st. On the Legal Research benchmark, the drop is even steeper, with Astra at 30th and Sol at 52nd. Vals AI says the models make nearly twice as many tool calls as their predecessors but write shorter answers.

In September, OpenAI announced a specialized product called "Astra for Law." It does significantly better than the base model on the Legal Research Bench, reaching 6th place. Vals AI tested both models with a one-million-token context window and 128,000 max output tokens at full reasoning effort.

According to OpenAI, GPT-6.2 Astra is the first externally released model to reach the "High" threshold for AI self-improvement. OpenAI says the model can meaningfully speed up AI research, on par with giving every OpenAI researcher an extra, highly skilled research engineer.

OpenAI calls this out explicitly as a risk. Models that can help build future AI systems could push the field forward faster than safety measures and human oversight can keep up. The industry is currently wrestling with this under the label "RSI".

As countermeasures, OpenAI points to tighter controls in research environments and its monitoring system Control Room, which can track research tasks and shut them down if needed. The company also says it has expanded monitoring that examines how models reason and act and automatically flags unauthorized behavior.

On alignment, meaning how well the model follows user instructions and communicates openly, the new models match their predecessors, according to OpenAI. In two tests, however, they more often failed to flag obstacles blocking their work, like a missing file or an unavailable search tool.

items.summary_en: OpenAI has officially released the GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol models, optimized for high-complexity professional workflows and daily tasks respectively. In terms of pricing, the API cost for GPT-6.2 Astra has been reduced by 20%, with input pricing set at $8 per million tokens, further enhanced by caching mechanisms for improved computational efficiency; both models are now available to enterprise and developer users.
items.title_zh: OpenAI发布GPT-6.2系列模型并下调API定价
items.summary_zh: OpenAI推出GPT-6.2 Astra与Sol模型，在提升专业任务性能的同时降低了API调用成本
items.article_content_zh:
OpenAI 发布了两种新的语言模型。 GPT-6.2 Astra 旨在满足要求较高的专业工作，而 GPT-6.2 Sol 则适合日常使用。 OpenAI 表示，两者在基准测试中都优于其前辈，而且运行成本更低。

GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 现已可供 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 中的 Plus、Pro、Enterprise 和 Edu 用户使用。 Pro-500 用户可以在这两种型号上使用超快模式。从 GPT-6.2 Sol 开始，Pro-200 订阅者还首次获得超快访问。

开发人员可以通过 OpenAI API 访问这两个模型。 OpenAI 表示，GPT-6.2 Astra 的 API 定价比其前身便宜 20%，每百万输入代币为 8 美元，缓存输入为 0.40 美元，每百万输出代币为 40 美元。 GPT-6.2 Sol 保持 GPT-6.1 Sol 的输入定价为 2 美元，缓存输入为 0.10 美元，输出为每百万代币 10 美元。

OpenAI 训练了 GPT-6.2 Astra，使其能够更可靠地处理法律、金融和会计等领域的专业惯例。该公司表示，演示文稿从模板中提取布局、颜色和版式，匹配精确的字体大小。幻灯片标题旨在捕捉幻灯片的要点，而正文则重点关注关键细节。

OpenAI 的声明很大程度上依赖于其模型的性价比。据 OpenAI 称，在测试多步骤专业工作流程的 Agents Last Exam 基准测试中，GPT-6.2 Astra 的得分比其前身 GPT-6 Astra 高出 5.2 分，而成本却不到其前身的三分之一。它比 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5.2 领先 5.5 个百分点，而成本仅为 Anthropic 的 5%。在这一基准测试中，只有 Google 的 Gemini 4 Carbon 能与 Astra 保持同步。

据 OpenAI 称，在涵盖合同条款分析等任务的法律基准 Harvey LAB-AA 上，GPT-6.2 Astra 的通过率是 Claude Fable 5.2 的两倍多，而成本约为六分之一。 OpenAI 表示，在包括咨询、财务和设计任务在内的内部 GDPval-v2 基准上，Astra 比其前身提高了 6.2 个百分点，同时使用的输出代币减少了 22%。

OpenAI 表示，计算机的使用已经是前身的强项，现在又变得更好了。据报道，在测试中，该模型构建了 3D 汽车模型，用 Python 编写了物理解算器，并在 Blender 中对结果进行了动画处理。在另一个演示中，它对遥控汽车的各个部分进行了建模，并制作了动画装配指南。

OpenAI 还声称在网页设计方面取得了进展。在 3D 基准 AA-3D 上，人类评委比较两种盲态交互体验。 GPT-6.2 Astra 以 1,318 Elo 点位居第一，领先于 Claude Fable 5.2 的 1,271 点和 GPT-6.2 Sol 的 1,259 点。

据 OpenAI 称，在 Terminal-Bench-Science（测试终端中科学工作流程的基准）上，该模型的得分比 GPT-6 Astra 高出 9 个百分点，而成本又不到 GPT-6 Astra 的三分之一。 OpenAI 表示，Astra 还创下了 Vals 科学指数的新高，该指数衡量模型解释生物数据和运行实验的能力。

OpenAI 表示，GPT-6.2 Sol 适合那些想要快速、多功能模型来完成日常任务的用户。在编码基准 FrontierCode 2.0（检查代码更改是否满足实际项目的质量标准）上，Sol 仅落后 Astra 0.5 个百分点，而成本仅为 Astra 的五分之一。 OpenAI 表示，该模型还可以很好地处理非工作任务。

据 OpenAI 称，GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 在网络安全方面也取得了更好的进展。他们更有效地发现和利用漏洞，编写更安全的代码，并提供更好的错误修复，在多项测试中代币效率显着提高。这两种模型都达到了 OpenAI 准备框架中网络安全的“关键”门槛，就像之前的 GPT-6 Astra 一样。

作为回应，OpenAI 正在针对潜在风险的网络安全请求添加更严格的保护措施。 OpenAI 表示，这些保障措施应该会加大滥用的难度，但也会限制合法的漏洞研究和安全测试。

OpenAI 计划通过 OpenAI Daybreak 提供新模型，该模型已经让经过审查的安全研究人员能够访问其他护栏较少的模型。公布的网络安全基准数据来自关闭防护措施和分类器的内部测试。 OpenAI 在随附的安全报告中阐述了其方法。

在人工智能分析智能指数中，GPT-6.2 Astra 排名第二，仅次于 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5.2，该指数汇总了知识工作、编码、科学和一般知识的九项评估。根据Artificial Analysis，Astra 比 GPT-6 Astra 提升了 5 分，超过了 Google 的 Gemini 4 Carbon（60 分）和 Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5.5（59 分）。 GPT-6.2 Sol 获得了 2 分，达到 57 分，与 GPT-6 Astra 的水平相当，而每项任务的成本仅为 GPT-6 Astra 的 15% 左右。

items.title: Apple's System Status page shows an outage affecting iCloud sign-in for "all users", the App Store, and Apple Music; some users report failed iPhone activations (Sarah Perez/TechCrunch)
items.title_en: Apple's System Status page shows an outage affecting iCloud sign-in for "all users", the App Store, and Apple Music; some users report failed iPhone activations (Sarah Perez/TechCrunch)

inline_images.caption: Image Credits:Bryce Durbin / TechCrunch
inline_images.alt: Image Credits:Bryce Durbin / TechCrunch

items.author: TechCrunch
items.article_content:
After a recent slew of tech outages, service disruptions, and flight chaos this week, now it’s Apple customers who are facing technical issues.

On Reddit, some folks also noted that they were unable to activate a new iPhone, which is likely related to these ongoing issues.

Given the recent increase in AI-driven cyberattacks, users across social media have already begun to speculate about the cause. In particular, users are expressing concerns about the Apple outage, as it arrives only days after technical failures at Microsoft led to its cloud systems that power flagship services like Outlook and Teams failing due to cascading software issues.

Similarly, a brief outage of Chase’s banking app this week garnered attention, as did an ongoing partial outage (at the time of publication) of the National Security Agency’s internal classified network, both of which were blamed on software glitches.

So far, none of the outages in the past week have been attributed to cyberattacks, but rather to technical problems.

Apple has yet to issue any sort of formal statement about the outages, beyond acknowledging via its status page that the issues are occurring. TechCrunch reached out to the company for comment but hasn’t heard back yet — if we do, we will update.

After the initial outages were reported, Apple’s status page was updated to include other outages impacting Apple School Manager, iCloud Mail, iCloud Web Apps (iCloud.com), and Schoolwork.

Post updated after publication with the status of the outages.

ai_analysis.insight_en: These frequent outages reveal an over-reliance on centralized underlying software scheduling systems by hyperscalers, where single points of failure trigger cascading global disruptions. items.article_content_zh:
本周，在经历了一系列技术中断、服务中断和航班混乱之后，现在面临技术问题的是苹果客户。

在 Reddit 上，一些人还指出他们无法激活新 iPhone，这可能与这些持续存在的问题有关。

鉴于最近人工智能驱动的网络攻击有所增加，社交媒体上的用户已经开始猜测其原因。特别是，用户对苹果的服务中断表示担忧，因为就在几天前，微软的技术故障导致其为 Outlook 和 Teams 等旗舰服务提供支持的云系统因级联软件问题而出现故障。

同样，本周大通银行应用程序的短暂中断引起了人们的关注，国家安全局内部机密网络的持续部分中断（截至本文发布时）也引起了人们的关注，这两起事件都被归咎于软件故障。

到目前为止，过去一周的中断都不是由网络攻击造成的，而是由技术问题造成的。

除了通过其状态页面承认问题正在发生之外，苹果尚未就此次中断发表任何形式的正式声明。 TechCrunch 联系该公司征求意见，但尚未收到回复——如果收到，我们会更新。

在报告最初的中断后，Apple 的状态页面已更新，包括影响 Apple School Manager、iCloud Mail、iCloud Web Apps (iCloud.com) 和 Schoolwork 的其他中断。

items.title: Google updates Gemini Privacy Hub to extend its retention period for temporary chats and chats with history turned off from 72 hours to around two months (Jagmeet Singh/TechCrunch)
items.title_en: Google updates Gemini Privacy Hub to extend its retention period for temporary chats and chats with history turned off from 72 hours to around two months (Jagmeet Singh/TechCrunch)

inline_images.caption: Image Credits:Jagmeet Singh / TechCrunch
inline_images.alt: Image Credits:Jagmeet Singh / TechCrunch

items.author: TechCrunch
items.article_content:
Google is extending how long it keeps temporary Gemini chats and conversations made with chat history turned off to around two months, saying the change aims to improve safety and security as AI systems become more capable.

The change, which will roll out globally in the Gemini app over the coming weeks, marks a significant increase from the previous 72-hour retention period mentioned in Google’s Gemini Apps Privacy Hub, according to an archived version from November 12.

OpenAI, by comparison, says it may keep temporary chats in ChatGPT for up to 30 days, whereas Anthropic retains incognito chats in Claude for 30 days by default. However, companies may keep some data longer for legal or safety reasons, or to investigate policy violations.

Google did not answer questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed, instead pointing to a blog post that says chats are kept longer to respond to users, process feedback, and protect its services and users. Its updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models.

The longer retention period comes as Google introduces separate settings for Gemini’s chat history and AI training. Until now, both were tied to a single “Keep Activity” setting. Users will now be able to keep their conversations in their chat history without using them to train Google’s generative AI models.

Google says both new settings will be turned off by default for users who previously disabled Keep Activity. For those who had Keep Activity turned on, their chat history will remain enabled. They can, though, decide separately whether Google can use their conversations to train AI models.

Its updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models.

The longer retention period comes as Google introduces separate settings for Gemini’s chat history and AI training. Until now, both were tied to a single “Keep Activity” setting. Users will now be able to keep their conversations in their chat history without using them to train Google’s generative AI models.

Google says both new settings will be turned off by default for users who previously disabled Keep Activity. For those who had Keep Activity turned on, their chat history will remain enabled. They can, though, decide separately whether Google can use their conversations to train AI models.

items.article_content_zh:
谷歌将临时 Gemini 聊天和关闭聊天记录的对话的保留时间延长至两个月左右，并表示这一变化旨在随着人工智能系统变得更加强大，提高安全性。

根据 11 月 12 日的存档版本，这一变化将在未来几周内在 Gemini 应用程序中在全球范围内推出，这标志着 Google Gemini 应用程序隐私中心提到的之前 72 小时保留期的显着增加。

相比之下，OpenAI 表示，它可能会在 ChatGPT 中保留临时聊天最多 30 天，而 Anthropic 默认情况下会在 Claude 中保留隐身聊天 30 天。然而，出于法律或安全原因，或者为了调查政策违规行为，公司可能会将某些数据保留更长时间。

谷歌没有回答有关促成这一变化的原因以及它是否会影响对话的访问或审查方式的问题，而是指出一篇博客文章称，聊天会保留更长时间，以响应用户、处理反馈并保护其服务和用户。其更新的 Gemini Apps Privacy Hub 也将潜在的系统故障作为保留聊天的原因，并表示临时对话不用于训练人工智能模型。

随着谷歌为Gemini的聊天记录和人工智能训练引入了单独的设置，保留时间更长了。到目前为止，两者都绑定到一个单一的“保持活动”设置。用户现在可以将他们的对话保存在聊天记录中，而无需使用它们来训练b谷歌的生成式人工智能模型。

谷歌表示，对于之前禁用“保持活动”的用户，这两项新设置将默认关闭。对于那些打开了“保持活动”的人，他们的聊天记录将保持启用状态。不过，他们可以单独决定谷歌是否可以利用他们的对话来训练人工智能模型。

items.title: Google’s Spark AI agent becomes ‘Tasks’ — and now it’s free
items.title_en: Google’s Spark AI agent becomes ‘Tasks’ — and now it’s free

inline_images.caption: Tasks in Gemini
inline_images.alt: Tasks in Gemini

items.author: Emma Roth
items.article_content:
Google is rebranding its Spark AI agent as “Tasks” and making it free to use. The feature, which is powered by Google’s new Gemini 4 Hydrogen AI model, can do things like create meal plans, manage your calendar, and dig through your emails to find recurring expenses you might not need.

Users in the US will get access to a few other features, including the ability for the AI agent to call businesses to compare product pricing and check inventory, purchase items with Google Pay, and sign into accounts that support Google Password Manager. US users can also assign Gemini tasks by emailing gemini@google.com or texting it.

Google first introduced its Spark AI agent in May, but it was only available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. The launch of tasks in Gemini brings Spark’s capabilities to all users in the US, Canada, Japan, Korea, Australia, and India. You can find tasks by opening Gemini and changing the toggle on the homepage from “Chat” to “Tasks.”

Tasks in Gemini is just one of the many agentic AI features that have emerged over the past year, including Claude Duet, OpenAI’s Dots, and Meta’s Muse. Google says Gemini will perform tasks in a “hardware-isolated virtual machine that’s dedicated to your account and never shared with other users.” You can also provide instructions for Gemini while it completes tasks. When performing more sensitive tasks, like purchasing an item, it will stop working and ask for your permission before following through.
